Debug: Project-wide Debug. Inherits the entire UnityEngine.Debug surface (Log/LogWarning/LogError/…) and adds the TRACE level: per-system diagnostic logging that is OFF by default and toggled at runtime with the EnableTrace/DisableTrace console commands.
Debug.LogTrace(1): Explicit-type managed form, for call sites keyed to their owning system type.
Debug.LogTrace(2): Trace-level log line for a system/job, prefixed with its registered name. No-op unless EnableTrace armed type T; the whole call (arguments included) is compiled out of release builds.
Debug.TraceEnabled(0): Explicit-type form — required for file-scope or generic job structs, which key by their owning system type (see the class doc's keying rule).
Debug.TraceEnabled(1): Is trace logging enabled for this system/job? Idiomatic call: Debug.TraceEnabled(this).
FFComponents.Abilities.DeterministicAbil: Saved authoritative per-ability-kind fire state on the player entity — the ONLY cooldown authority. The client-side `PlayerAbilityCooldownTracker` is prediction/presentation and never simulation input. One element per covered `AbilityType`.
Highest applied completed-operation event sequence for this kind: the exactly-once guard. Duplicate or stale sequences do nothing.
The op-carried release edge for one commanded ship.
Completed-operation event sequence this release belongs to (provenance).
Agreed `FFTimeData.simulationElapsedTime` raw at which the command ends. Raw fixed-point, never a float duration that each peer decrements at its own rate.
FFComponents.Abilities.PlayerAbilityComm: One host-baked commanded ship for a mover-command intent (Frenzy / Guardian go-to-spot / Obliterator ship-command), joined to its `PlayerAbilityFireIntent` by `EventSequence`.
Baked orbit direction (Frenzy leg): 1 = clockwise, 0 = counter-clockwise.
FFComponents.Abilities.PlayerAbilityFire: Pending/consumed intent written by applying one host-completed ability operation exactly once. `CombatProjectileBirthSystem` (Plasma) and the mover-command appliers consume it at `TargetSimulationTimeRaw`; it persists across save/join/recovery until consumed and pruned.

Canonical fixed-point aim — raw fp, never a float round-trip. Plasma: the aim direction. ObliteratorDisc: the host-baked displacement from the cast point to the disc's end point. Layout unchanged; only the meaning per kind widened.
0 = pending, 1 = consumed (kept as provenance until pruned).
Completed-operation event sequence; joins the commanded-ship rows below.
Plasma: the host-baked, clamped shooter lead in milliseconds; the bolt is born at the shooter's simulation position predicted this far ahead (`PlayerFireLead.PredictOrigin`).

Deterministic release edge for mover-command kinds: target time plus the op-carried duration, in simulation-time raw. The commanded ships' cleanup is gated by THIS value — never by float disc/tracker completion state.
FFComponents.Artifacts.PendingActivation: One reward a pending activation drops when it lands (an obelisk's Lumin Orbs).
An item index: remapped to the current item table when a save loads (NestedRemapFields).
FFComponents.Artifacts.PendingStructureA: An activation that has been mined but has not taken effect yet: the burst is playing. Added to the portal, obelisk, Oracle or artifact assembler by the networked mining completion (`MiningCompletedNetworkOperation.ApplyActivation`) and consumed by `PendingStructureActivationSystem`, which sets `ActivatableStructure.Activated`, drops the rewards and removes this component on the first heartbeat who…

`Player.Guid` of the player who mined it. Presentation only: that player hears the activation sound wherever they are; other players hear it in range. The narration is for every player in the session.
Agreed `FFTimeData.simulationElapsedTime` raw at which the activation takes effect. Raw fixed-point, never a countdown each peer decrements at its own rate.
An artifact assembler becomes player-placed so logistics bots pick up from it.
How many of the four reward slots are used.
FFComponents.Artifacts.StructureActivati: Which burst and sound an activation plays. Obelisks, Oracles and assemblers share one.
The voice line the activating player hears once the activation lands.

How long the burst plays before an activation takes effect: production's delays (0.21.0.35 `MiningAction.ActivatePortal` waited 4000 ms, `ActivateObeliskOrOracle` 3000 ms), as simulation seconds. At the game's 16 heartbeats per second that is 64 heartbeats for a portal and 48 for an obelisk, Oracle or artifact assembler.
FFComponents.Blueprints.BlueprintGhostOw: The entity whose `BlueprintMetaData` instantiated this ghost — the local player for an in-hand preview, or the `BlueprintMaster` singleton for the remote-apply path (`BlueprintTool.InstantiateAndPlaceBlueprintFromString`).
FFComponents.Blueprints.ConstructionTask: This is not really only for Construction tasks. Used for Supply Bots and Construction bots to be assigned tasks like building, grabbing items, or moving items
FFComponents.Combat.AoeImpactDamage: A one-heartbeat area hit at its `LocalTransform`: `AoeImpactDamageSystem` deals `Damage` to every entry of its KNN vision (radius = the vision's range), then deletes it. Transient, never saved.
FFComponents.Combat.AoeImpactDamage.Excl: the shot's own target, already hit in full; a splash (a share of the shot's damage, `WeaponConfig.AoeImpactDamageShare`) spares it. `Entity.Null` for a flat area hit.
FFComponents.Combat.AoeImpactDamage.Vali: only what the shot itself could hit takes the splash: never an untargetable entity or one without an `AsteroItem` (`KnnProjectileCollisionSystem`'s own filter). False for a flat area hit, which keeps damaging every vision entry as before.
FFComponents.Combat.AutomationPlayerInvu: Test-harness-only immunity latch (the paired determinism audits' `InvulnerablePlayers` isolation). While present on a player entity, `PlayerInvulnerabilityDerivationSystem` skips it, so the harness's direct `Health.Invulnerable = true` write survives the per-heartbeat 029 derivation — which otherwise recomputes (and wipes) the flag from vehicle/defeat/grace state within one heartbeat of the harnes…
FFComponents.Combat.C3KnnEnemyVision: Enemy-family C3 vision: the nearest eight ENEMY-family providers in range, nearest first under the total rank. Parallel to `KnnEnemyVision` and disjoint from it.
FFComponents.Combat.C3KnnFleetVision: Fleet-family C3 vision: the nearest eight FLEET-family providers in range, nearest first under the total rank. Parallel to `KnnFleetVision` and disjoint from it: no C3 consumer may read the legacy buffer and no legacy consumer may read this one.
FFComponents.Combat.C3SharedSpatialIndex: The two per-family shared indices. `C3StaticIndexMaintenanceSystem` is the ONLY writer of either half (isolation-manifest.md §5); every consumer takes a read-only `DeterministicSpatialIndexView` from `FleetView` or `EnemyView` and queries it.
Raw `FFTimeData.simulationElapsedTime` the dynamic half was rebuilt at.

Keys that arrived twice as an ADD in one drain. Both are dropped and the key is retired, so the provider becomes unresolvable on EVERY peer instead of resolving to whichever publisher a given peer happened to order first — the same fail-closed rule `DeterministicSpatialSnapshotMap.FailedClosedIdentities` applies to duplicate identities.
The C3 view: excludes nothing, because C3 has no KNN-disabling concept.
The LEGACY float family's view: identical except that it hides every provider carrying `DisableKnnMarker`.
The read-only point lookup into one static half — "is this entity a published static provider here, and where is it?". The `FleetView` counterpart for the question a spatial query cannot answer.

Dynamic samples whose provider kind is `CombatSpatialKeyKind.None` and which therefore belong to no family. They are OMITTED from both maps rather than guessed into one — the "unclassified producer fails closed" rule of the spatial-provider contract.

Legacy static sources the static half cannot key: mobile-station parts (`Placeable.IsFlying`), which leave the world grid while they fly and so have no injective tile identity. They are OMITTED and COUNTED rather than packed under a key two of them could share — the same fail-closed rule as `UnclassifiedDynamicProviders`, and the counter is what stops the omission from being silent.
FFComponents.Combat.C3StaticIndexIntake: The ONE door into `C3SharedSpatialIndex`'s static half. The ordered placement/removal path publishes here; `C3StaticIndexMaintenanceSystem` drains it at a heartbeat boundary, sorts by structural key and applies. Nothing else may touch the index.
FFComponents.Combat.C3VisionBuffer: A C3 holder's fixed-width vision slots, null-terminated exactly like the legacy `SmallBuffer{T}`: slots are filled nearest-first from zero and every slot after the last neighbour is non-existent.
FFComponents.Combat.C3VisionBuffer.Count: Populated slots, i.e. the index of the first non-existent slot.
FFComponents.Combat.C3VisionBuffer.MaxLe: Slot capacity, pinned to the frozen query width rather than restated.
FFComponents.Combat.C3VisionElement: One neighbour in a C3 holder's vision record (data-model.md §6).
FFComponents.Combat.C3VisionElement.Dist: The cached canonical rank distance, in the index's shifted squared domain (`DeterministicSpatialIndexMath.DistanceShiftBits`) — the same `long` the query ranked on, carried so a consumer never re-derives it and never re-orders the record.
FFComponents.Combat.C3VisionElement.Exis: Occupancy is decided by the STRUCTURAL key, not by `Target`: a C3 record's identity is its key, and every provider the index can return carries a non-zero one (`DeterministicSpatialKey` refuses the reserved zero identity).
FFComponents.Combat.C3VisionElement.IsSe: True for the holder's own record. Explicit-self consumers receive self at slot zero BY CONTRACT (data-model.md §6), not as an incidental zero-distance tie, so a consumer that wants to skip itself tests this flag rather than comparing a distance to zero.
FFComponents.Combat.C3VisionElement.Posi: The neighbour's authoritative position at the index build this record came from.
FFComponents.Combat.C3VisionElement.Targ: Same-world lookup handle only; never a key field, never a sort term.
The neighbour's structural identity — the only term that decides membership and order, through the index's total rank `(distance, x, y, z, key.W0..W3)`.
FFComponents.Combat.C3VisionProducerRepo: The typed per-heartbeat record of HOW the C3 vision producer resolved each holder's own origin — the twin of `C3VisionProvisioningReport` for `FFSystems.Combat.DeterministicCombatVisionSystem`.
Fleet holders whose identity the snapshot retired as a duplicate (`C3VisionStatus.DuplicateProvider`). Counted apart from `FleetMissing` because it is an integrity event, not an absent provider.
Fleet holders cleared by the WHOLE-GRAPH fault path — no index or no snapshot this heartbeat (`C3VisionStatus.IndexUnavailable`).
Fleet holders in NEITHER index, left `C3VisionStatus.MissingProvider`. The fail-closed residue, and the number R19 drives toward zero.
Fleet holders whose origin came from this heartbeat's DYNAMIC snapshot.
Fleet holders whose origin came from a published STATIC provider record — the R19 path.
Producer passes completed since the world was created.
FFComponents.Combat.C3VisionProvisioning: The typed completion record for `FFSystems.Combat.C3VisionProvisioningSystem` — the pass that puts `C3KnnFleetVision` / `C3KnnEnemyVision` on the entities that carry the legacy vision components, written as a world singleton and refreshed every heartbeat.
Entities that hold `C3KnnEnemyVision` after the most recent pass.
Enemy-family records added since the world was created (cumulative).
Entities that hold `C3KnnFleetVision` after the most recent pass.
Fleet-family records added since the world was created (cumulative).

Legacy fleet-vision holders still missing their C3 twin at the END of the most recent pass. It is zero by construction unless a structural change failed, and it is recorded rather than asserted because a provisioner that throws inside the load path becomes a silent no-op (the `CombatLegacyMigrationReport` lesson).
Passes this system has completed since the world was created.
FFComponents.Combat.C3VisionStatus: Why a holder's record is or is not usable this heartbeat. A C3 consumer must branch on this rather than on an empty buffer: "no neighbours in range" and "this holder has no resolvable provider" are the same buffer and very different facts, and guessing between them is how a fail-open reaches simulation.
FFComponents.Combat.ChaseC3FallbackRepor: The typed per-heartbeat record of HOW `FFSystems.UnitStateMachine.ChaseSystem` resolved each of its three pose reads on the C3 branch — the chaser itself, the owner it is leashed to, and the target it is steering at.
Fail-closed events on this pass, across all three sites.

The LOWEST `AsteroItem.ConfigIndex` seen on any fail-closed entity this session, or -1 when nothing has failed closed. It names the CLASS, which is the thing an operator needs in order to tell an expected transient (a just-spawned ship) from an unexpected population, and a raw count cannot.

Owner-leash reads whose owner is a MOVER with no current rail. The leash test is skipped; the chase itself continues, because a missing leash decision is the conservative non-decision (it cannot yank a ship to idle on a pose nobody can vouch for).
Owner-leash reads answered from a player commander's replicated `Player.SimulationPosition`.
Owner-leash reads answered from the owner's current rail sample.

Owner-leash reads answered from a grid-placed STATIC's transform — a defense platform, an enemy spawner, a station core. The dominant case by construction and the one transform read the C3 branch keeps, because a structure has no fixed-point pose in the game today.
Chase passes completed on the C3 branch since the world was created.

Chasers with NO current rail sample. Every entity this system iterates is an admitted mover by its own query (`LinearMotion` + `LocalTransform`), so there is no legitimate non-rail source for it: the participant makes no decision at all this heartbeat — no leash test, no steering, no rotation.
Chasers that resolved their own pose from a current rail sample.
Target reads whose target is a MOVER with no current rail. There is nothing to steer at, so the chaser makes no move this heartbeat.
Target reads answered from a player target's replicated simulation position.
Target reads answered from the target's current rail sample.
Target reads answered from a grid-placed static's transform.
Fail-closed events this session, across all three sites.
FFComponents.Combat.CombatLegacyMigratio: The typed completion record for T027's production-loader legacy combat migration (`Serialization.CombatLegacyMigrationSystem`), written exactly once per load as a world singleton.

Camps left unidentified because two or more share a generating chunk coordinate. FR-002 says that cannot happen; if it ever does, stamping them would hand the serial assigner a duplicate reservation key and throw out of EVERY heartbeat thereafter, so the whole colliding group is skipped and counted here instead.

Camps skipped because they already carried an id or an undrained pending record. A non-zero value on a first migration would mean the injectivity assumption below (one camp per chunk) is being leant on by something else and wants a look.

Enemy camps this load stamped with `PendingCombatIdentity`. A camp is a transform-less, roster-less simulation shell, so it is neither a roster root nor a mover candidate and no earlier pass could reach it — yet it is the PRODUCER whose id every attack ship and every camp station derives its provenance from.
Holders excluded from the admitted set before a row was built.
The escaped exception, when `FlagFaulted` is set.
The migration reached its end without an unhandled exception.
An exception escaped a migration stage; `Fault` carries it.
Nothing needed migrating, so the ranking/candidate passes were skipped.

The applied world came from the authoritative peer, so the ranking/candidate passes were skipped even though there WAS pending work. See `CombatLegacyMigrationSystem.AppliesRemoteAuthoritativeWorld`: minting ids the host does not hold is the desync, not the cure.
Current-schema rails the invariant pass made C3-ineligible.
`LinearMotion` holders admitted as migration candidates.
Candidates that received a freshly minted id this load.
Candidates left at id zero — no kind, or an exhausted id space.
The world allocator watermark this load stored.
Candidates that actually received a current-schema rail.
Roster roots that received a freshly minted id this load.
Tied roots the durable fold could not separate either (entity-handle order).
Roster roots whose durable structural signature matched another pending root.
Roster roots the ranking pass considered (identified and pending alike).
Tied rows the durable fold could not separate either (ordered by query order).
Candidate rows that shared a bit-identical canonical row with another candidate.
FFComponents.Combat.CombatMoverKinematic: Non-zero `[Save]` fixed-point movement rail for enemy and player-fleet movers. Authoritative heartbeat-boundary state: only fixed-heartbeat C3 systems mutate it, rail entities are excluded from legacy `LinearMotionSystem` integration, and no presentation transform ever feeds back into it.

Overlap force with TWO explicitly ordered phase writers, never an unordered single-writer claim (data-model §2): phase 1, heartbeat-H integration consumes the value written after H-1 exactly once as position displacement (`CollisionForce * fixedDelta`) and clears it (D4 FIX-IN-RAIL: consume-on-apply); phase 2, the post-integration overlap producer writes the H+1 value from the immutable start-H sn…
Full-width behavior deadline in raw `FFTimeData.simulationElapsedTime` — never 16-bit heartbeat arithmetic (the wrapping `ushort` frame counter is not a clock).
Current C3 destination when `FlagHasDestination` is set; written by the heartbeat behavior writers at decision boundaries.
Legacy `LinearMotion.IsColliding` avoidance latch. D8 preserves the latch behavior; the latched tangent sign lives in `FlagAvoidanceTangentNegative`.
Whether the tangent sign has EVER been chosen — the third state the legacy float `LinearMotion.Mod` encoded and a lone sign bit cannot.
Legacy `LinearMotion.Mod == -1`: the deflection tangent direction chosen when the avoidance latch engaged. `Mod` only ever takes ±1, so the float is losslessly a sign bit.
Legacy `LinearMotion.CollidesWithWorld`: gates the world-avoidance branch of integration; behavior-written at state transitions (fleet-idle, entrance nav, ship transfer).
Legacy `LinearMotion.IgnoreKnnCollisions`: behavior-written per heartbeat; the overlap producer skips force production for the mover while set, so it gates the H+1 force.

This rail's `Position`/`Velocity`/`Heading` are a per-heartbeat MIRROR of the legacy float authority, not state the C3 integrator produced — set by `CombatMoverRailMirrorSystem` on every rail that `FlagInitialized` does NOT cover.
Legacy `LinearMotion.UseMultiHitRaycasts`: per-entity avoidance raycast strategy, baked config for large hulls.
Deterministic accumulated environmental force; integration applies `GravityForce * fixedDelta` once and clears it every heartbeat.
Authoritative gameplay-facing direction. Written by the C3 integrator under the D5 speed-threshold deadband (rotate only while `|v| > 1.6 u/s`).
Authoritative heartbeat-boundary world position. Written ONLY by the C3 integrator on heartbeat ticks; `LocalTransform` for a rail entity is projection OUTPUT, never an input.
Producer-owned birth provenance/order; never packed into the spatial key.

Units per simulation second (same units/second model at 16 and 60 UPS). Written by the heartbeat behavior writers; consumed by integration as `Position += Velocity * fixedDelta`. Behavior never folds `CollisionForce` into it.
FFComponents.Combat.CombatMoverRailProvi: The typed completion record of `CombatMoverRailProvisioningSystem` (ruling R8: a load/heartbeat-path system that can silently no-op must publish numbers, not leave the reader to infer that it ran).
Passes this system has completed since the world was created.
Entities carrying a `CombatMoverKinematics` after the most recent pass, whatever installed it — the migration on the load path or this system on the live one.

Rails the MOST RECENT pass declined to seed because the entity's pose or identity was not yet real — an unkeyed rail, or one whose pose still reads the origin (`CombatRailProvisioning.TryResolveSeedPose`). Last-pass rather than cumulative, like `Unprovisioned`: a deferral is a state the next pass re-evaluates, not an event.
Rails added since the world was created (cumulative).

Rails SEEDED since the world was created (cumulative) — the value pass, not the structural one. Equal to `RailsProvisioned` in steady state; a gap means a rail was added but its seeding job never ran for it, which is the silent half of the failure this record exists to surface.
Reference records added since the world was created (cumulative).
Resolved-sample records added since the world was created (cumulative).

Admitted movers still missing a rail at the END of the most recent pass. Zero by construction unless a structural change failed; recorded rather than asserted, because a provisioner that throws becomes a silent no-op (the `CombatLegacyMigrationReport` lesson).
FFComponents.Combat.CombatMoverTargetRef: Saved semantic target/owner handoff state for a rail-backed chaser (data-model.md §2). `TargetKey` is published/cleared only by the named C4 bridge (`C4CombatTargetKeyBridgeSystem`, H+1 visibility), an ordered spawn/transfer handoff, or a seeded isolation input; `OwnerKey` is set at spawn/transfer.
Stable commander/owner relationship; valid only while `FlagOwnerPresent`.
Semantic target identity; valid only while `FlagTargetPresent`.
FFComponents.Combat.DefensePlatformAttac: A neighbouring defense platform saw an enemy: attack it next heartbeat. Added through a command buffer at the end of one heartbeat and consumed (then removed) on the next (`DefensePlatformDefenseSystem`), so a join snapshot can fall in between. [Save]: without it the joiner's platforms skipped the attack the host's made, their attack cooldowns drifted apart and they released different ships.
FFComponents.Combat.DeterministicCombatO: Non-zero world-scoped compact identity on every player, dynamic admitted C3 object, and projectile-capable emitter. Injective per save lineage; assigned only through `FFCore.Combat.CombatObjectIdentityReservation` / legacy migration and NEVER reallocated for a live record. Zero means "not yet assigned" and is never a valid id.
Non-zero world-singleton monotonic allocator feeding `DeterministicCombatObjectId`. Consumed without wrap; exhaustion fails closed.
FFComponents.Combat.DeterministicJoinEve: Non-zero `[Save]` world-singleton authoritative event sequence for player join/bootstrap birth provenance. Incremented ONLY at peer-converged points (the `PlayerJoined` op apply, which drains at the identical queue position on every peer including the host's own idempotent copy, or single-peer bootstrap creation), so the counter value converges cross-peer. Overflow fails closed, never wraps.
FFComponents.Combat.DeterministicShotOrd: The same invariant for the per-shooter SHOT ordinal: one ordered fire DECISION consumes exactly one `DeterministicShotSequence` ordinal, and every projectile of an authored multi-shot pattern shares it, distinguished by pattern subordinal. Overflow fails closed — the caller must not fire rather than wrap an ordinal onto an identity that already exists.

The ordinal a FRESH shooter's counter starts at, in one place because two independent sites seed it — the T027 load migration and `PlayerAbilityStateInstallSystem` — and they seed the same object arriving by different routes. If they ever disagreed, two peers would mint different shot ordinals, and therefore different projectile keys, for one agreed cast: exactly the cross-peer fork R24 closed.
FFComponents.Combat.DeterministicShotSeq: Saved per-shooter monotonic shot ordinal: one ordinal per AI/player fire; a multi-projectile pattern shares the shot ordinal and distinguishes members by authored pattern subordinal. Overflow fails closed, never wraps.
FFComponents.Combat.DeterministicSpatial: One admitted provider's start-of-heartbeat sample (data-model.md §5). `Entity` is a same-world lookup handle for C4 compatibility only — it is never packed into a key, never persisted, and never a sort term.
The canonical lookup key this sample was published under.
Provider category for validation and evidence. `CombatSpatialKeyKind.None` when the entity carries no admitted role tag — descriptive provenance, never a lookup term.
Authoritative provider position at snapshot-build heartbeat; always from a rail.

The immutable heartbeat map from `DeterministicSpatialKey` to the admitted sample (data-model.md §5). Published once per heartbeat as a singleton by `DeterministicSpatialSnapshotSystem`; every C3 consumer in that heartbeat reads the same instance, so a rail that moves mid-heartbeat cannot change a sample another consumer already resolved.
Raw `FFTimeData.simulationElapsedTime` the snapshot was gathered at.

Burst-safe construction of the canonical dynamic-domain key. The packing is duplicated from `DeterministicSpatialKey`'s factories on purpose: those throw a formatted `ArgumentException` on the reserved zero identity, which Burst cannot compile. `CombatMoverSpatialSnapshotTest.CanonicalDynamicKeyMatchesTheFactoryPacking` pins the two against each other so the copy cannot drift.
The key a dynamic-domain provider is published under: domain + object identity, with the kind byte stripped.

Identities that failed CLOSED because more than one provider published them. Injective `CombatObjectId` is the key's premise; a violation makes the identity unresolvable on every peer rather than being resolved by iteration order, which is archetype-creation order and therefore not agreed cross-peer.
Diagnostics only, and valid only once the gather job has completed — the gather runs as a scheduled job, so nothing on the hot path reads these.

Resolves a semantic key to this heartbeat's sample. A default key, an unbuilt snapshot, an unpublished identity and a duplicated identity all resolve to nothing — there is no entity or transform fallback anywhere on this path.
Container-level overload so a job can carry the samples as a plain `[ReadOnly]` native container instead of a wrapper struct the job safety system would have to introspect.
FFComponents.Combat.DeterministicSpawnOr: The single home of the producer spawn-ordinal consumption invariant: one birth consumes exactly one ordinal from the producer's live `DeterministicSpawnSequence`, siblings in the same batch observe each other's consumption, and the counter never rewinds or skips.
FFComponents.Combat.DeterministicSpawnSe: Saved per-producer spawn sequence defining reservation provenance for enemy/AI producers (it is provenance input, not the global identity). Overflow fails closed, never wraps.
FFComponents.Combat.FleetCommander.Playe: A player's fleet capacity before any technology reward is applied. Every player starts here and `FleetCommandReward` recomputes `MaxFleetSize` as this baseline plus the sum of the currently-unlocked capacity techs — never `+=` onto whatever the component already held, which double-counted on any path that replayed the rewards over a deserialized (already-rewarded) value.
FFComponents.Combat.GivenUpTarget: A target this shooter gave up on. While it is listed the targeting vision filter skips it, so the next-best target is acquired instead of re-locking the same hopeless one every tick. [Save] for the same reason as the tracker.
FFComponents.Combat.HealthBarInitializer: "Build me a health bar" latch, enabled by a hit and disabled once HealthBarCreatorSystem has built the bar. Baked DISABLED beside `HealthBarReference` for the same reason: toggling keeps the owner's archetype fixed.
FFComponents.Combat.HealthBarPlacement: Where a health bar sits under its owner (it is the owner's child): lying flat and facing the camera, a fixed distance below the owner on screen, whichever way the owner is turned. Both components are undone from the owner's rotation, so the one used must be the rotation the owner is drawn with: HealthBarSystem uses the simulation's, WorldEntityInterpolationRenderSystem the smoothed one it draws.
FFComponents.Combat.HealthBarReference: The owner's HUD health bar. Baked DISABLED onto every `Health` entity and toggled rather than added/removed: Entities never frees an archetype, and adding and removing this per hit minted an (archetype x bar) twin for every damageable kind until the 16 MB archetype store ran out. Enabled only while a bar exists; `Value` is Entity.Null otherwise.
FFComponents.Combat.HealthRegenData: [Save] because `Timer` is simulation truth, not a derivable cache: `HealthRegenSystem` withholds regeneration until it reaches `TimeBeforeHealthRegens` (10 s) since the entity last took damage, and NOTHING else in the world records when that was.
FFComponents.Combat.IC3KnnVision: The interface over the two C3 vision components, so one generic Burst job per family declares write access to exactly its own component — the same shape `IKnnVision` gives the legacy family. Implementors must remain unmanaged `IComponentData` structs with unchanged field layout.
FFComponents.Combat.IC3KnnVision.Count: The exact number of populated slots, written by the producer alongside the buffer.
FFComponents.Combat.IC3KnnVision.Range: Finite query range, fixed-point. A negative or zero range yields no neighbours.
FFComponents.Combat.PendingCombatIdentit: Saved pending birth-reservation provenance awaiting canonical id assignment by the serial early-fixed assigner (`CombatIdentityAssignmentSystem`). Carries the frozen `CombatObjectIdentityReservation.Record` rank fields.
Authored pattern subordinal; 0 for single births.
Authoritative event sequence: from `DeterministicJoinEventSequence` for Bootstrap/PlayerJoin player records, or the producer's `DeterministicSpawnSequence` for Simulation-domain spawns.
Producer's `DeterministicCombatObjectId` for Simulation-domain records; MUST be zero for Bootstrap/PlayerJoin (AssignCanonical fails closed on a mismatch).
Raw `FFTimeData.simulationElapsedTime` at the converged stamping point.
FFComponents.Combat.ProjectileEffects.Sp: drawn beside the impact when the shot HIT something (the Plasma bolt's splash ring, sized to its area), never when it ran out of range. Presentation only.
FFComponents.Combat.ProjectileKinematics: Versioned authoritative fixed-point movement record for a C3 projectile. Movement/range progress never reads a projected pose; movement-owned expiry (range/lifetime, D1/D3 FIX-IN-RAIL) is distinct from C4 hit-driven deletion.
Saved projectile-capable emitter identity; joins the projectile spatial key.
Fixed trajectory endpoint, or the current C3 steering goal sample when homing.
Movement-owned expiry latched (range passed, zero-length path, lifetime bound).
Whether `TargetKey` resolved in the current heartbeat's snapshot.
Authored multi-shot pattern order under one shared shot ordinal.
Monotonic per-shooter shot ordinal (one per ordered fire decision).
Current semantic target identity when steering is supplied by C3.
Homing angular limit per simulation second.
Movement mode of a rail-backed projectile.
FFComponents.Combat.ResolvedCombatMoverS: DERIVED start-of-heartbeat key resolution output (data-model.md §2) — rebuilt before C3 behavior each heartbeat and never saved or fingerprinted. Target and owner availability are independent: a missing sample never chooses a replacement or mutates state (C4 owns retarget/clear/target-loss policy).
Start-of-heartbeat commander/owner sample; valid only while `OwnerAvailable`.
Start-of-heartbeat target sample; valid only while `TargetAvailable`.
FFComponents.Combat.ShipSpawnCommand.All: When true, this command's whole `Count` may be spawned to the same commander in a single heartbeat — it bypasses the per-commander "one ship per heartbeat" spread limit (`UsedCommanders`). This is purely about delivery cadence and does NOT affect fleet capacity (see `IgnoreFleetCapacity`). Used by the `spawnShips` cheat so e.g. 100 ships appear at once.
FFComponents.Combat.ShipSpawnCommand.Ign: When true, ships in this command spawn to a commander even if doing so exceeds the commander's `MaxFleetSize`. Orthogonal to `AllowMultiplePerCommander` (cadence) — this controls only the capacity check. Used by the `spawnShips` cheat so the full count spawns without first raising the fleet-size limit.
FFComponents.Combat.TargetProgressEvalua: The pure give-up decision, kept out of the Burst job so it can be unit tested without the targeting system's singletons. Progress means a new lowest observed health: a heal that is then ground back down part way is not progress, so a regen stalemate still trips the rule.

Raises the low to the target's health now, for a target that healed while this shooter was not shooting it (holding it out of weapon range, or lost and acquired again). The low of an earlier fight would otherwise stand, and shots that land would count as no progress until they wore the whole heal off again.
FFComponents.Combat.TargetProgressTracke: Targeting state for the "shots that never land" give-up rule.
FFComponents.Commands.BlueprintFlipComma: flips of the local player's held blueprint waiting for `BlueprintFlipSystem`, one bit per axis. Each press toggles its bit, so two presses of the same flip before the next heartbeat cancel, exactly as the two flips would. Local and presentation-only, like `RotateCommand`: the flipped ghosts reach the other peers through the placement request, never through this.

A rotate press was already waiting when the first of these flips was pressed, so the rotate applies first, as the systems run. When false, a waiting rotate was pressed after the flip and waits a heartbeat for it.
FFComponents.Commands.PendingRotation: the hand-off from the network-operation drain to the rotation cascade. The `RotateStructure` apply leg appends one entry per accepted rotation during `HeartbeatSystem.PerformQueuedOperations()` (op-drain order, identical on every peer); `RotateInPlaceControllerSystem` consumes the buffer FIFO on the next heartbeat's fixed pass, re-resolving the tile to the live entity at consumption.
FFComponents.Commands.PendingRotation.Ta: The baked absolute direction to rotate the target to.
FFComponents.Commands.PendingRotation.Ti: The baked, grid-resolvable target tile — resolved to the live entity at consumption.
FFComponents.Commands.PendingRotationQue: Shared locator for the PendingRotation hand-off buffer: it lives on the HOST player entity (peer-stable across all peers, save-restored on join/load), created lazily on first use — the lazy AddBuffer is a structural change but happens at the same op-drain position on every peer (all peers apply the same first rotation op). One helper so a future change to the location happens in one place.
FFComponents.Connectors.ConnectorGroupUp: This is a marker placed on individual connectors to indicate that the entire group attached to that connector needs to be recalculated. This is not placed on the connector group because the connector group is ephemeral. This will cause the existing group to be deleted and replaced with a new group, attached to all connectors in the group.
FFComponents.Connectors.PerpendicularCon: One-heartbeat connector-group handoff emitted by `ConnectorItemMovementCalculatorSystem` and consumed by `PerpendicularConnectorTransferSystem`. Deliberately not `[Save]`: `ConnectorGroup` entities are derived, ephemeral state that the normal entity marshaller never captures.
FFComponents.Connectors.SideLoadTurn: which side last put an item onto this connector side-on, so belts feeding it from both sides take turns instead of the side whose travel direction sorts first taking every gap. `PerpendicularConnectorTransferSystem` reads it to order contenders and writes it on every side-on insertion.
FFComponents.Connectors.SideLoadTurn.Las: `None`, or 1 + the travel `Direction` of the last side-on insertion.
FFComponents.Connectors.SideLoadTurn.Ran: Where an item travelling `direction` stands in line: the side after the one served last goes first (0), then round the compass. With no history, plain direction order.
FFComponents.Core.NetworkItemsUpdateCont: Container for networked item updates to be processed.
List of pending networked item updates.
FFComponents.Core.NetworkedItemUpdate: Represents a single update operation for a networked item.
FFComponents.Core.NetworkedItemUpdate.Ch: The chunk coordinates in the game world.
FFComponents.Core.NetworkedItemUpdate.Co: The number of items involved in the operation.
FFComponents.Core.NetworkedItemUpdate.Op: The type of operation (Add or Remove).
FFComponents.Core.NetworkedItemsCache: Provides a centralized cache system for networked inventory items across containers in an Entity Component System (ECS) architecture.
FFComponents.Core.NetworkedItemsCache.Ad: Adds items to a specific container entity and updates the cache.
FFComponents.Core.NetworkedItemsCache.Bu: Initializes the cache data structures with persistent allocators.
FFComponents.Core.NetworkedItemsCache.Cl: Clears all items from the entity cache.
FFComponents.Core.NetworkedItemsCache.Co: Contains data about items within a specific container entity.
Total count of the item in this container.
Number of items reserved for pending operations.
FFComponents.Core.NetworkedItemsCache.Ge: Finds the nearest container with available (non-reserved) items of the specified type. Prioritizes containers with more available items that are closer to the origin.
FFComponents.Core.NetworkedItemsCache.It: Stores the total count of each item type across all containers. Key: Item identifier (int) Value: Total count IMPORTANT: Do not update this directly! Use provided methods.
Maps item identifiers to container entities that contain those items. Key: Item identifier (int) Value: Container data including entity reference and count
FFComponents.Core.NetworkedItemsCache.Re: Makes every container's `ContainerData.Reserved` the sum of the live `NetworkReservation`s that name it, and nothing else.
Recalculates the total item counts across all containers. Only performs recalculation if the cache is marked as needing update.
Removes items from a specific container entity and updates the cache.
Reserves a specified number of items in a container for pending operations.
FFComponents.Core.NetworkedItemsCache.Se: Searches for a storage container that can hold the specified item stack.
FFComponents.Core.NetworkedItemsCache.Un: Releases reserved items in a container.
FFComponents.Core.Operation: Defines the types of operations that can be performed on networked items.
FFComponents.Core.Placeable.Direction: The direction this object is currently facing
FFComponents.Core.Placeable.GetAdjacentT: Gets the tile coordinates surrounding the placeable, not including any height information
FFComponents.Core.Placeable.GetBounds(2): Obtains the bounds of the given placeable given its length, width, and gridTile. The gridtile is the upper left tile of the placeable.
FFComponents.Core.Placeable.GetCenterTil: Obtains the center tile (or the lower left of the center tiles, if the dimensions are even) for the given placeable for its current rotation.
FFComponents.Core.Placeable.GetLowerLeft: Obtains the lower left grid tile for the current placeable, given the given tile position (center of entity) Adjusts based on the length and width of the placeable, based on its current rotation.
Obtains the lower left grid tile for the current placeable, given the given world position (center of entity) Adjusts based on the length and width of the placeable, based on its current rotation.
Obtains the lower left grid tile for the given placeable, given the given world position (center of entity) Adjusts based on the length and width of the placeable, based on its current rotation.
FFComponents.Core.Placeable.GetOccupiedT: Returns the tiles occuped by this placeable.
FFComponents.Core.Placeable.GridTile: The current GridTile of this object. If the object is bigger than 1x1, it's the lower left grid tile of the object
FFComponents.Core.Placeable.IsFlying: Whether this object is currently flying (mobile stations)
FFComponents.Core.Placeable.IsStable: Whether this part is currently stable. Calculated in StationGridCalculationSystem
FFComponents.Core.Placeable.OriginalDire: The direction this object was facing when it was placed.
FFComponents.Core.Placeable.OriginalTile: The position the placeable was actually placed at. Usually this is the tile of its LocalTransform, but some placeables move, like inserters and cargo barges, so we keep track of where they were originally placed for blueprint copying. Same for original direction too.
FFComponents.Core.Placeable.PlayerPlaced: Whether the player placed this object. Everything in the base would be player placed, but enemy structures, asteroids, etc, would not be.
FFComponents.Core.SoundEffect: A one-heartbeat request to play a sound, consumed and destroyed by SoundEffectSystem. Presentation only: the census strips it (DeterminismStateFingerprintJobs.BuildExplicitStrip) and nothing in the simulation reads it.
FFComponents.Core.SoundEffect.Position: Where in the world the sound happens. Build sounds are positional (U9): every peer runs the construction and placement systems for every player, so the sound plays at the building and fades with distance instead of reaching players nowhere near it.
FFComponents.Crafting.Crafter.ForceCraft: If true, the crafter does not need inputs to produce outputs.
FFComponents.Crafting.PendingCraftedShip: A player-crafted ship is waiting to spawn into its player's fleet. Added only by the networked DeployCraftedShip op (never baked), so it exists identically on every peer; `PlayerCraftedShipDeploySystem` re-issues the `FFComponents.Combat.ShipSpawnCommand` each heartbeat until the spawn lands (the spawn system clears un-spawnable commands every tick, e.g.
FFComponents.DysonSpheres.DysonDroneTran: Fixed-point travel rail for a Dyson drone in `StarSlotNavigationState`. The orbit-slot target is frozen ONCE at the nav-start heartbeat into `Destination` — drones must not chase the live rotator-spun slot per frame, because the per-frame `LinearMotionSystem` integrates wall-clock delta time, making position-per-heartbeat (and therefore the arrival heartbeat) peer-divergent.
FFComponents.Enemies.EnemyCampEconomy: Permanent per-camp economy ledger for the 027 absorb-and-spend attack model. The ledger is simulation truth and therefore rides saves and multiplayer world snapshots with the camp shell.
FFComponents.Enemies.EnemyCampEconomy.Ne: Absolute deterministic launch-schedule window. This is derived from serialized simulation time rather than Heartbeat.CurrentHeartbeatFrame, which resets on multiplayer joins and recovery applies.
FFComponents.Enemies.EnemyCampEconomyAut: Optional authoring surface for validation prefabs and future hand-authored camps. The runtime camp prefab deliberately does not use it: newly generated camps add the component in EnemyCampPlacementJob, while the restoration pass uses component absence to recognize pre-027 saves and derive their initial schedule.
FFComponents.Enemies.EnemyCampInitialStr: Birth record for a camp placed at chunk generation: the spawner budget from the strength-by-distance curve and the RNG seed for the camp's first (robust) build. The builder consumes these instead of entity-handle/elapsed-time RNG so the initial spawner set is a pure function of (MasterSeed, chunk). Pre-027 camps lack this component and keep the legacy robust-build path.
FFComponents.Enemies.EnemyCampMetaData.G: Use when you want the camp builder system to generate several spawners for this camp on the next tick. Useful when on the first frame it spawns, or when loading a game where the camp was in a disabled chunk.
FFComponents.Haulers.HaulerFlightPhase: Which flight-phase segment the rails currently describe.
FFComponents.Haulers.HaulerFlightRails: Fixed-point movement rail for the mobile-station flight state machine. One instance on the hauler meta entity, re-armed per flight phase: undock lift, transit, queue advance, dock approach, dock rotation, and descent are each a straight segment (or an angular sweep) whose endpoints are frozen in fp when the phase starts.
FFComponents.Haulers.HaulerFlightRails.A: Arms the docking rotation sweep (position endpoints stay pinned at the pad).
Arms a fresh linear segment: endpoints frozen, progress zeroed.
FFComponents.Haulers.HaulerFlightRails.C: The authoritative fp position on the current segment. Successor phases anchor on THIS (or on `Destination` when complete), never on the float transforms, so presentation drift can never feed back into simulation.
FFComponents.Haulers.HaulerFlightRails.D: Reference structure's fp position at the current phase end.
Arc-length progress along the current segment; heartbeat-lane writes only.
FFComponents.Haulers.HaulerFlightRails.O: Reference structure's fp position at the current phase start.
FFComponents.Haulers.HaulerFlightRails.P: Which phase segment this rail currently describes.
FFComponents.Haulers.HaulerFlightRails.R: The current rotation sweep is fully traversed.
Radians to sweep in the docking rotation phase (zero outside it).
Radians progressed in the docking rotation phase; heartbeat-lane writes only.
FFComponents.Haulers.HaulerFlightRails.S: The current phase segment is fully traversed (fp gate — replaces float thresholds).
Unit direction of the current segment (fp3.zero for a degenerate segment).
FFComponents.Haulers.HaulerId: A mobile station's identity in network ops: a number unique among the live haulers, given once by `HaulerIdAssignmentSystem` on the heartbeat the hauler appears and kept for its life.
FFComponents.Haulers.HaulerManualDriveSt: Authoritative real-time-piloting state for a hauler meta entity. Kept separate from `HaulerFlightRails` — manual driving and scheduled flight are mutually exclusive (driving suspends the schedule, `Hauler.IsOn = false`) and each component's invariants stay simpler apart than folded into one.

True while this heartbeat (or the most recently applied one) carried nonzero drive intent for this hauler. Drives the suspend/resume trigger (contract C6): the heartbeat this flips false-to-true is the same heartbeat `Hauler.IsOn` flips to false.
The most recently applied heartbeat's replicated direction intent.
The most recently applied heartbeat's replicated rotation intent.
FFComponents.Haulers.HaulerManualHeading: How far a flying station is turned from its placeables' `Placeable.Direction` (by hand, with the drive keys or the station panel's rotate buttons, and by a landing's turn toward its pad) since it last touched down, in radians, wrapped to (-pi, pi].
The signed turn that takes a station whose facing is `quarterTurns` quarter turns short of its landing facing, further turned by hand by `turnedRadians`, onto that facing: the shortest way round.
FFComponents.Haulers.LandingZoneOwnFacin: Marks a landing zone whose facing (its `Placeable.Direction`) is its own: every landing at it faces that way. Every zone made since carries it, added where zones are made (the Land command's `PlaceLandingZone`, the blueprint instantiator: hand placement, paste, Q); a zone saved before gets its ships' facing once, from `Step0_50_0_77LandingZoneOwnFacing`, which then marks it, so a later load never…
FFComponents.Haulers.LandingZoneShipCopy: One building of the ship a landing zone last saw land on it: which item, which tile relative to the zone, which way it faced. The zone's buffer of these is a copy, not a link, so it keeps showing that ship as it landed after the ship is destroyed, rebuilt or changed. The landing zone ghost draws it when no ship is on its way.
Canonical order: by tile (height, then z, then x), then item, then facing.
Replaces `copy` with the buildings of `landed`, placed on a zone at `zoneTile`, in canonical order.
The building's item config id (`Placeable.ItemIdentifier`), remapped on load.
The copy of `landed` (a building's placeable where it stands, or will stand, on the zone) for a zone at `zoneTile`. False for an offset a 16-bit tile cannot hold, which no ship reaches.

`building` (a building of the copy laid out on `zone`) turned `quarterTurns` quarter turns clockwise (Up to Right, as a landing turns) about the zone's centre: where the same ship stands when the zone faces that much further round.
The building's landing grid tile (its lower-left tile) minus the zone's grid tile.
FFComponents.Haulers.StationCargo: what a station's wait conditions read from one of its cargo-hold buildings (the ones with `Stations.CargoHold`: Cargo Hold, Large, Provider, Requester, Networked Storage, Singularity Chest and Trash Can). MobileStationInStationStateSystem decides with it and the stop panel shows the same reading, so the two cannot disagree.
FFComponents.Haulers.StationCargo.Counts: Whether this hold counts toward "cargo holds full", "cargo holds empty" and item counts. A Trash Can does not (`InventoryOperationType.Destructive`): it destroys everything it is fed, so it never holds an item and is never full. Counted, it kept "cargo holds full" from ever passing on a station that carried one.
FFComponents.Haulers.StationCargo.HasRoo: Whether an enabled primary slot of this hold can take more. Disabled slots never fill, so they do not count.
FFComponents.Haulers.StationCargoReading: a station's counted cargo holds (`StationCargo.Counts`), summed.
Whether any counted hold holds an item.
Whether any counted hold has an enabled slot that can take more.
"Cargo holds empty": no counted hold holds an item. A station with no cargo hold carries nothing, so it is empty.

"Cargo holds full": no counted hold can take more. A station with no cargo hold is never full; it can load nothing, and a stop that left it the moment it landed hid that its route was waiting on a hold it does not have (the stop panel says so on the row instead).
How many of the station's buildings count as cargo holds.
FFComponents.Haulers.StationLock: A locked station: its structures form no station connection with a structure of another station, so it can land, or sit landed, flush against other buildings and keep exactly its own. Lives on the hauler, beside the other station settings (`Hauler.IsOn`, the route, the name); absent means unlocked, which is how every station starts and how every save written loads.
FFComponents.Haulers.StationLockHint: Which locked station a structure that has no station yet came from: the replacement of an upgraded structure (`ConstructionBotTaskSystem.SwapStation`) and the ghost a destroyed one leaves (`PlaceableDeletionSystem`), when the structure belonged to a locked station.
FFComponents.Haulers.StationLockHint.Try: The hint a structure's replacement or ghost carries: false unless its station is locked.
FFComponents.Haulers.StopCondition.Compa: ItemCount only: how the cargo holds' count of `RequiredItem` meets `RequiredItemCount`.
FFComponents.Haulers.StopCondition.Join: How this condition joins the one above it (`StopConditionJoin`); ignored on the first.
FFComponents.Heat.HeatProducer.AmbientTe: Deep-space ambient, in Celsius -- the temperature a structure is placed at and the floor that both cooling and idle decay bottom out on (StationGridCalculationSystem). Lives on the component rather than in either caller so the placement seed (ConfigLoadingUtil.InitializePowerComponents) and the simulation floor cannot drift apart.
FFComponents.Heat.HeatWarningThresholds: The shared overheating-warning predicates. They live here, below all callers, so the in-world warning icon (FFSystems.StationGrid.GridWarningCheckerSystem), the HUD alert (FFSystems.Heat.HeatWarningAlertSystem), the red glow shell (FFSystems.Heat.HeatDamageApplicationSystem) and the hover info panel (UI.Panels.HoverInfo.HoverHeatStats) cannot drift apart -- they previously each carried their own c…
The temperature test: this producer is at least `OverheatingWarningMargin` above `targetTemp`. Per-structure, and the only input to the quiet `ShouldWarn` verdict.
How far ABOVE the target (cooling) temperature the overheating warning starts.

The loud verdict -- the HUD overheat alert with its siren and flashing red panel (FFSystems.Heat.HeatWarningAlertSystem), and the red glow shell drawn over the structure (FFSystems.Heat.HeatDamageApplicationSystem). Everything `ShouldWarn` requires, AND `willOverheat`: the station is producing more heat than its installed cooling could ever absorb.
The quiet verdict -- "this structure is too hot" -- shown by the in-world warning icon (FFSystems.StationGrid.GridWarningCheckerSystem) and the hover info panel (UI.Panels.HoverInfo.HoverHeatStats).

The grid-wide half: the station produces more heat than the cooling it has INSTALLED could ever absorb, so its producers are not merely hot, they are getting hotter with nothing on the station able to stop it.
FFComponents.Heat.OverheatMapWarningPin: The world-map warning pin that FFSystems.Heat.HeatWarningAlertSystem spawned for an overheating structure, held on the structure so the system can find its own pin again on later heartbeats.
FFComponents.Heat.OverheatingState: Per-structure heat state, derived once per heat pass instead of re-derived by every consumer.
FFComponents.Heat.OverheatingState.GlowP: Where the glow mesh sits when hidden -- far enough above the structure to be off screen. Lives here rather than as a literal in the two systems that move it so "parked" means one thing.
FFComponents.Heat.OverheatingState.GlowS: Where the glow mesh sits when shown: exactly on the structure it belongs to.
FFComponents.Heat.OverheatingState.IsGlo: The last glow visibility pushed to `RenderMeshChildren.OverheatingMesh`. Owned exclusively by HeatDamageApplicationSystem -- the grid calculation never touches it -- and exists so that system can skip the transform write when nothing changed.
FFComponents.Heat.OverheatingState.IsToo: `HeatWarningThresholds.IsTooHot` as of the last heat pass. Written by StationGridCalculationSystem, which is the only thing that moves `CurrentTemperature` at all and does so on one heartbeat in eight -- so this cannot go stale between passes, because the input it is derived from cannot change either.
FFComponents.Heat.OverheatingState.WillO: The grid-wide half: the owning grid produces more heat than its installed cooling could ever dissipate, so it is losing the heat fight. Flips for every producer on a station at once, which is why it is never a warning condition on its own -- alone it would light up a whole station of stone-cold structures.
FFComponents.Helpers.InventoryHelper.IsR: True when `item` is an ingredient of `recipe` that the inventory does not hold enough of to start a craft. Uses the same counts and costs the crafter itself does, so what the UI shows as starved is exactly what is holding production up. A recipe that only needs one of its ingredients (`recipeIsAnyInList`) has nothing starved as long as one of them is covered.
FFComponents.Helpers.InventoryHelper.Pas: Whether a belt item may enter although the inventory has no room: it stores nothing and is empty, so at most one item is ever inside, on its way to the output belt. Such a hold used to stop the whole belt running through it.
FFComponents.Helpers.InventoryHelper.Sto: Every primary slot is disabled (the "Disable Slots" slider at its maximum). A cargo hold set up that way is a docking point that stores nothing: belt items pass through it (`PassesBeltItemsThrough`), so whatever is inside is in transit and the ship's wait conditions leave it out.
FFComponents.Helpers.LogisticsBayOutputP: The rules for a logistics bay's barge-only output port, shown to players as the Barge Loading Bay (`LogisticsBayOutputPort`): how much it holds, which arriving items it takes once the bay's normal slots are full, and how a barge draws from it.

Whether any of the barges loading from `bay` would load `item`. `bargeFiltersByBay` holds one filter per cargo barge whose pickup end is that bay (LogisticsBayOutputPortSystem.BargeSources). Order-independent (an "any" over the set), so it does not matter what order the barge scan collected the filters in.

Whether a cargo barge with `filter` would load `item`. Mirrors the filter branches of InserterPickupSystem.PickUpItems: a set item must match, FilterAll takes nothing, the category options match on ItemCategory ("Other" is anything but ore/component/intermediate), and no filter takes all.

How many of `item` the port holds: `capacityMultiplier` (the bay's `GetCapacityMultiplier(in LogisticsUnitConfig)`) times one ordinary slot, with the player's stack-size setting applied -- the same formula a cargo barge's own hold uses (InserterPickupSystem.GetSlotStackLimit with LogisticsUnitConfig.StackSizeMultiplier).

How many ordinary stacks the port of a bay with `bayConfig` holds: the config's StackSizeMultiplier, which the bay tiers set to 2, 5 and 10 (Logistics, Fast and Express Logistics Bay): about one load of the paired barge for an item that stacks at 100. A bay config that sets none gets `LogisticsBayOutputPort.CapacityMultiplier`. Config only, so every peer reads the same depth.
How many ordinary stacks the port of `bay` holds, from the bay's own item config. A bay with no AsteroItem (never the case for a placed one) gets the default depth.

How many of `count` arriving items the port takes as overflow: what the bay's normal slots had no room for. The port only ever takes overflow. It never draws on the normal slots, so those fill first and stay full for belts, inserter arms and barges alike.
Puts `count` of `item` into the port. The caller has asked `GetOverflowRoom` first and has taken exactly that many from wherever they came from.
Takes up to `maxCount` items out of the port. Clears the port's item once it is empty.

Moves up to `maxCount` of the port's item into another inventory (a player collecting from the bay's panel). Only what the target actually accepts leaves the port, so a full target leaves the rest in the port. Works whether or not a barge is fetching; `LogisticsBayOutputPort.Enabled` only gates the fill.
FFComponents.Helpers.LogisticsHelper.Get: The number of cargo models that should be on the hull right now. Models track how *full* the unit is rather than a fixed item count, so a barge loaded to the brim shows a full deck whether that took 480 ore or 10 of something that stacks in ones. Rounded up, so a unit carrying anything at all shows at least one model.

The most of a particular item a unit can actually carry: its hold, capped by however much of that item one inventory slot will take. An item that stacks in ones fills the slot long before the hold is full.
How many cargo models a full hold draws. Fixed per barge, so a loaded barge always looks the same no matter which item it is hauling.
FFComponents.Helpers.LogisticsHelper.Ite: How many carried items one cargo model stands for on a barge hauling an ordinary item. A barge carries hundreds of items and a model entity per item costs far more than it reads on screen, so the models are batched. This only sets how many models a full hold draws -- see `GetCargoModelCount`.
FFComponents.Helpers.LogisticsHelper.Loa: Adds `count` items to the unit's carried total and spawns however many extra cargo models that total now calls for. For an inserter arm that is one model per item; for a barge a model only appears every `ItemsPerCargoModel` items.
FFComponents.Helpers.MinerBotPhysicalHan: Publish the canonical pose before changing ownership or spatial eligibility.
FFComponents.Helpers.PlaceableHelper.Cre: Many operations require a PlaceableConfig, but they really only need the height, width, and length. This function just converts a Placeable to a PlaceableConfig with these elements.
FFComponents.Helpers.PlaceableHelper.Get: Returns a list of connected entities that all share the specified Typed component, excluding any entity marked for deletion. Traversal still passes through deletion-marked entities so live entities on the other side of a soon-to-be-removed structure remain reachable.
Get the list of entities contained within the grid tiles that are occupied by the provided placeable
Given an arbitrary number of 90 degree rotations, find the minimum number that is equivalent to the provided rotations.
FFComponents.Helpers.PlaceableHelper.Rot: Rotates the placeable clockwise once, updating the fields on the placeable.
FFComponents.Helpers.ResearchBotPhysical: Call before an immediate ownership or spatial-eligibility change.
FFComponents.Indicators.ActiveItemDispla: When a cargo hold went empty while it still shows its last item, on the simulation clock. Not saved, and no simulation system reads it.
FFComponents.Indicators.ConfiguredRange: A player-CONFIGURED range, in world units — genuine per-entity state and, for the defense platform, simulation truth: `DefensePlatformKnnRangeSystem` feeds `AttackRange` into `KnnEnemyVision.Range` every tick.
FFComponents.Indicators.RangeIndicatorDa: RETIRED by feature 063 — nothing produces this any more. It survives ONLY so that a save written before the 0.50.0.9 upgrade step still deserializes: the step reads the restored values in `PostLoadUpgrade`, carries them into `ConfiguredRange` for the two structures whose range is really player state, and removes the component everywhere else.
FFComponents.Indicators.RangeIndicatorDi: Presentation only — the radii the range rings are currently drawn at, in world units, plus whether they are showing. Deliberately NOT `[Save]`: every value here is recomputed by `RangeIndicatorSystem` from config (or from `ConfiguredRange`) whenever the structure is hovered or selected, so persisting it could only ever preserve a stale answer.
FFComponents.Knn.KnnNeighbourRankLookups: The three identity lookups `KnnSourceOrder.Build` keys a source by, packaged so a job can hand them to `KnnVisionSelect` without the helper reaching into the job. Built inline inside `Execute` from the job's own flat `[ReadOnly]` fields — the lookups are value-copied, never re-acquired.
FFComponents.Knn.KnnSourceOrder: Builders for `KnnSourceOrderKey`. Deliberately a pure function of raw component VALUES rather than of an `EntityManager` or a chunk, so the Bursted gather job, the Bursted repel consumer and the managed audit instrument all key the same population the same way — a mirror implementation that disagreed with its producer would order the tree one way and report another.
FFComponents.Knn.KnnSourceOrder.Rank64(1: A 64-bit rank for the ≤8-slot consumption sort, where carrying four words per neighbour would cost more than the sort saves.
FFComponents.Knn.KnnSourceOrderKey: A cross-peer total order over the legacy KD-tree's SOURCE population. WHY THIS EXISTS. `KnnSystem.GatherSourcesJob` fills the KD-tree's point array in ECS query iteration order, which is archetype CREATION order — append-only history of how a World was built, not a function of simulation state. A long-running host and a client that restored the same world from a join snapshot never share it.
FFComponents.Knn.KnnVisionCandidate: One neighbour a consumer is choosing between, with the two things the choice may legitimately depend on: a metric (a distance, usually) and the cross-peer identity the producer keyed the neighbour with.
FFComponents.Knn.KnnVisionSelect: "Best by (metric, rank)" — the consumption-side guarantee for the metric-ranked vision consumers (targeting, projectile hit, defense-platform override).
FFComponents.Knn.KnnVisionSelect.ArgMax(: Index of the candidate with the LARGEST metric (rank breaks exact ties), or -1.
FFComponents.Knn.KnnVisionSelect.ArgMin(: Index of the candidate with the SMALLEST metric (rank breaks exact ties), or -1.
FFComponents.Knn.KnnVisionWitness: One holder's ACTUAL `AssignVisionJob` inputs and outcome, recorded by the job itself at the moment it wrote the vision buffer.
FFComponents.Knn.KnnVisionWitness.Count: Neighbours actually written, or `SkippedCount` when the job took its out-of-slice guard and left the PREVIOUS heartbeat's buffer standing — a retention the end-of-heartbeat roster reports as if it were this heartbeat's answer.
FFComponents.Knn.KnnVisionWitness.Holder: The holder the query slot belongs to. Local handle; resolved to a cross-peer combat id by the instrument.
FFComponents.Knn.KnnVisionWitness.Range: The range that cut the result walk. `IKnnVision.Range`, read mid-heartbeat.
FFComponents.Knn.KnnVisionWitness.Skippe: Sentinel for `Count`: this holder was not written this heartbeat.
FFComponents.Knn.KnnVisionWitness.Unwrit: Sentinel for `Count`: no witness was recorded for this slot at all.
FFComponents.Knn.KnnVisionWitness.Viewer: The viewer position `AssignVisionJob` measured every candidate against.
FFComponents.Legacy.LegacySaveTypes: The public face of the shim above, for the upgrade step that lives in another assembly. Handing out a `System.Type` keeps the shim itself internal.
FFComponents.Legacy.LegacySaveTypes.Disa: Key for the pre-f853e7e38 movement marker. Drop on sight.
FFComponents.Lights.LightColors: What a light's stored `LightStructure.Color` means. It is a linear colour, the form the lamp's emission takes. A colour picked in the panel is stored as it is, each channel 0..1, so its brightness is the picker's value.
FFComponents.Lights.LightColors.BulbShar: The share of a lamp's peak its own emission carries; LightGlowSystem's inner glow adds the rest at the centre, so the middle of the lamp is a little brighter in the same colour.
FFComponents.Lights.LightColors.DefaultR: A new light's colour, in sRGB: a warm white, about 4500 K. The light prefab bakes it.
FFComponents.Lights.LightColors.Emission: The lamp's emission when it is on and powered: its share of the lamp's peak.
FFComponents.Lights.LightColors.FromPack: The stored value for a packed pick; the picker's "Default" (0) is `DefaultRgb`.
FFComponents.Lights.LightColors.FromRgb(: The stored (linear) value for an sRGB colour picked as 0xRRGGBB.
FFComponents.Lights.LightColors.Hue(1): The linear colour a stored value stands for, each channel 0..1.
FFComponents.Lights.LightColors.HueOfEmi: The hue (linear, 0..1) a lamp's `Emission` stands for: the colour of the light it casts.
FFComponents.Lights.LightColors.PeakInte: How bright a lamp of this colour is at its centre, as a multiple of its hue. The look tonemaps with ACES, which lifts every channel of a bright colour toward the same ceiling, so a saturated colour turns pale and then white as it brightens, while the dim tail of its halo keeps the colour: the lamps peaked at 2.6 times their hue (emission 1.6 plus the glow's 1.0) and their middles read white.
FFComponents.Lights.LightColors.PeakOfEm: The lamp's brightness at its centre (its emission plus the inner glow) for an `Emission`.
FFComponents.Lights.LightColors.Saturate: A fully saturated colour peaks at `SaturatedScale / (luminance + SaturatedOffset)` of its hue, capped at `WhiteIntensity`: about 0.85 for red, 0.4 for green, 1.2 for blue (`PeakIntensity`).
FFComponents.Lights.LightColors.ToPacked: A stored value in the colour picker's packed form (`MassDriverLaserColorPacking`): always a chosen colour, never the picker's "Default" 0, since a light stores the colour itself.
FFComponents.Lights.LightColors.ToRgb(1): A stored value as the sRGB 0xRRGGBB the picker shows (its hue, rounded to bytes).
FFComponents.Lights.LightColors.WhiteInt: How bright a white (or pale) lamp's centre is: the lamp's emission plus the inner glow LightGlowSystem draws over it (`PeakIntensity`).
FFComponents.LogisticsUnits.CargoBargeDo: How long a cargo barge has been docked at its pickup bay. After InserterPickupSystem.CargoBargeMaxDockSeconds a barge carrying anything departs even if it isn't full. Saved so a joining peer resumes the same countdown as the host; a separate component (not an Inserter field) so saves from before it existed keep the Inserter layout and simply start at 0 from the prefab.
FFComponents.LogisticsUnits.Inserter.Dir: This is the direction the inserter is currently facing (equivalent to placeable.Direction). Both the placeable and the Inserter have the direction. The direction is here so we don't have to do a placeable lookup in the Tile Update Job, which we expect to have performance impacts.
FFComponents.LogisticsUnits.Inserter.IsF: An inserter is full when the CurrentSlotIndex (the next place to insert the item) is greater than the carrying capacity. It's not subtracted by 1 because the CurrentSlotIndex is the place the next cargo item would go.
FFComponents.LogisticsUnits.Inserter.Max: Player-set travel limit, in tiles. On an inserter arm it is measured from the unit's origin tile and is symmetric: it caps how far the unit will look for a dock in BOTH directions. On a cargo barge it is the length of its route from the fixed start tile behind it, so it trims only the far end.
FFComponents.LogisticsUnits.Inserter.Tim: Timer used for picking up items
FFComponents.LogisticsUnits.Inserter.Vel: This is the current velocity of the placeable, to allow acceleration and the inserters to slowly speed up
FFComponents.LogisticsUnits.LogisticsUni: Clears the destination entity and resets its grid tile
Clears the source entity and resets its grid tile
Sets the destination entity and its cached grid tile together
Sets the destination entity and its cached grid tile together
Sets the source entity and its cached grid tile together
FFComponents.LogisticsUnits.MinerBotPhys: Physical mining route; LogisticsUnit continues to own work and transit timing.
FFComponents.LogisticsUnits.ResearchBotP: Physical research flight, independent of LogisticsUnit's scalar work timer. Runtime-added at admission; retained inactive across fleet handoffs and saves.
Place the bot at the rail's own fraction of its route, the way `MinerBotPhysicalState.Interpolate` does.
One-way compatibility projection; never recovers physical state from floats.
FFComponents.Loot.LootSpawnCommand: Unsaved bridge from the Burst loot producers to the managed network-operation publisher. Only the local host/standalone simulation authors these entities. The publisher consumes them in the late group and broadcasts one fully baked `LootSpawn` operation; clients never use this component to instantiate gameplay state locally.
FFComponents.Loot.LootSpawnKind: The host-baked kind carried by a transient `LootSpawnCommand` and its authoritative network payload. Values are wire-stable; never renumber or reuse them.
FFComponents.Loot.PickupableVacuum: The vacuum pull velocity of a pickupable toward one player — the ONE definition shared by the mover (`PickupableVacuumSystem`, FFSpaghetti) and the interpolation capture's speed allowance (`WorldEntityInterpolationCaptureSystem`, FFSystems), so the presentation bound can never drift from the simulation rule.
FFComponents.Map.AsteroidWarningStatus: Runtime state of the low-ore warning (FFSystems.Mining.AsteroidLowOreWarningSystem). Deliberately not [Save]: neither is the AttackWarningData nor the marker entity it describes, so after a load the system simply raises the warning again if it still applies.
FFComponents.Map.AsteroidWarningStatus.W: The world marker spawned for the active warning, destroyed when it clears.
FFComponents.Map.AttackWarningData: The one HUD-warning component, shared by every indicator on UI.FactoryDamageWarnings.AttackWarningPanel -- attack, death, overheat and asteroid-low -- with `Source` (and `IsDead`) deciding which one counts it. There is only ever one per entity, so a structure that is both hot and under attack shows as under attack.
FFComponents.Map.AttackWarningData.TimeL: How long the alert stays up after its last refresh. Counted DOWN by FFSystems.Indicators.AttackWarningSystem, which removes the component once it reaches zero.
FFComponents.Map.FFGrid.ChunkMapCapacity: The chunk maps' capacity in a game. ChunkCheckingSystem fills them through ParallelWriters, which cannot grow, so they are sized for the biggest world up front.
FFComponents.Map.FFGrid.CreateGrid(1): The grid with chunk maps of `chunkMapCapacity`. EcsTestBase builds one for every test: at the game's capacity the two maps are about 100 MB to allocate, clear and free each time, 69% of a test world's setup and teardown. A map that overflows still throws "HashMap is full".
FFComponents.Map.OneShotResource: Defines a one-shot resource that can be collected once and then removed from the game world.
FFComponents.Map.TerrainOreOverride: Test-scenario request to pin an asteroid's ore to an exact amount (the optional ore argument of `ffauto:terrain.place`). Applied by `TerrainOreOverrideSystem` on the first heartbeat AFTER the entity's `InstantiationUpdaterMarker` is consumed — `AsteroidPlacementSystem` re-rolls `Asteroid.OreRemaining` while that marker is present, so waiting for the marker to disappear (a heartbeat-driven, peer-id…
FFComponents.Map.TerrainOreOverride.OreC: The ore ITEM the asteroid yields (`Asteroid.OreConfigIndex`), resolved from the prefab's `OrePatchType` at command time with the same mapping `AsteroidPlacementSystem` uses.
FFComponents.MassDrivers.MassDriverLaser: The colour a player picked for this driver's link laser, as `MassDriverLaserColorPacking` packs it: 0 = the laser material's own colour, which every driver from loads with (the prefab bakes it and old saves do not carry the component).

How a mass driver's laser colour is stored in `MassDriverLaserColor.Value` and sent in the `MassDriverConfig` setting: `Default` (0) is the laser material's own colour, which every driver from has; anything else is `0xFFRRGGBB`, the sRGB colour the picker shows, with the top byte set so that black is still a chosen colour.

The colour the "Default" swatch shows: today's laser colour at full value. The material's HDR `_BeamColor` is linear (0.0772, 0, 0.0030); scaled to a peak of 1 and shown in sRGB that is #FF0038 (`MassDriverLaserColorTests` checks it against the material).
The `0x00RRGGBB` colour a value shows as; `DefaultDisplayRgb` for the default.
A stored value or a setting payload value: `Default`, or the flag byte fully set.
"#RRGGBB" of what the value shows as.
Parses "#RRGGBB" or "RRGGBB" (any case, surrounding spaces ignored) into a chosen colour.
FFComponents.MassDrivers.MassDriverTarge: Legacy: the follow memory as 0.50.0.71 saved it. `TargetStructureMemory` replaced it when power distributors gained the same mode. Nothing bakes or reads it now: it stays a saved type only so a 0.50.0.71 save still decodes it, and `Step0_50_0_73TargetStructureMemory` moves it into `TargetStructureMemory` and removes it on load.
FFComponents.Materials.PlayerLiveryColor: Per-ship override of the Standard-LowPoly shader's `_ColorAG`: the colour of the region the mask's A.G channel paints, which on `Player.mat` is the blue livery panels. The hull plates (`_ColorAR`), the emissive engine parts and the particles keep the material's values. Linear RGBA, because Entities Graphics uploads a `[MaterialProperty]` value as is and the project renders in linear space.
Put on the player ship model (the root of `PlayerModel.prefab`, which carries its only MeshRenderer) so each player's ship can show their colour.
FFComponents.MobileStations.ActiveLandin: This marks the set of station the player is currently trying to place for a new landing zone
FFComponents.MobileStations.MobileStatio: Structures that have the ability to move (like RocketAdapters), when placed, will either 1) Create a new entity that acts as the meta data about how the whole station can/will move. This is called a "Hauler" Entity. It contains the HaulerStops, which specify any automatic movement commands issued to the station, as well as this MobileStationData object.
FFComponents.MobileStations.StationGhost: An unbuilt ghost riding a mobile station in flight (, Lothsahn: "Parts that haven't been built yet (ghosts) should move and fly with the station to get built at the destination").
FFComponents.Player.HostPlayer: The player that is hosting the game.
FFComponents.Player.LuminaeBank: The crew's total Lumin Orbs collected over the whole game. Every orb any player picks up adds 1 here AND 1 to every player's own spendable balance (`LuminaeTracker.LuminaeOrbCount`), so for every player balance + orbs spent at Oracles + refund fees = this total. A player created later (a late joiner) starts with this total as their balance.
FFComponents.Player.LuminaeBank.EnsureEx: Creates the bank singleton if this world has none. Called from the OnCreate of BOTH systems that touch it (the persistence owner and the pickup writer) so it exists from world-system creation on every peer, whichever is created first.
FFComponents.Player.LuminaeTracker.Lifet: Still per-player: this player's running total of orbs they personally collected. Feeds the Steam stat (`LumenOrbsCollected`) and the first-orb tutorial objective — a personal achievement counter, not currency.
FFComponents.Player.LuminaeTracker.Lumin: This player's spendable Lumin Orbs. Every orb ANY player collects adds 1 here for every player (parked ones included), and only this player's Oracle purchases and refunds spend from it. A new player starts with the crew's `LuminaeBank.TotalCollected`.
FFComponents.Player.MePlayer: This component should be added to the local player who is currently playing the game on this machine.
FFComponents.Player.OracleUpgrades.MainW: This player's plasma-bolt damage multiplier bonus: 0 at level 1, +0.2 per level above it. A pure function of the saved level, added to the shooter's multiplier at bolt birth, so it is the buyer's alone and needs no restore on load.
Plasma-bolt damage each `MainWeaponDamageLevel` above the baseline adds, in percent of the base damage (the Oracle's "Plasma Bolt Damage Increase").
FFComponents.Player.ParkedPlayer: marks a Player entity whose owner has left the live session — parked (dormant: hidden + invulnerable + fleet holding station), never destroyed. Added and removed ONLY by the ordered `PlayerDeparted`/`PlayerJoined` operations so every peer parks/reclaims on the same heartbeat boundary. Rides `[Save]` so a parked player survives host save/load.
FFComponents.Player.Player: The player's authoritative SIMULATION state. Every field on this component is deterministic, fixed-point / integer simulation truth — never presentation — so it is safe for fixed-step systems to read and for the [Save]/heartbeat-replicated path to carry.
FFComponents.Player.Player.SimulationPos: Authoritative deterministic player position (see the type summary). Written only by the per-heartbeat replication apply; read by every fixed-step consumer. Lives at the END of the struct so older saves (which had no such field) reinterpret cleanly and a future trailing-field change stays low-risk.
The simulation position as a `float3` for presentation/float-math consumers.
FFComponents.Player.Player.SimulationVel: The ship's velocity (u/s) at the instant `SimulationPosition` was sampled, replicated with it on the heartbeat and written by the same single writer.
FFComponents.Player.PlayerAuthoring.Enem: Authored KNN enemy-vision range for the player's simulation object.
