The player's KNN participation lives on the baked `PlayerSimulationObject`, not on the player entity, so this range is consumed by `PlayerBaker` when it authors that object. Replaces the standalone `KnnEnemyVisionAuthoring` that used to sit on the player prefab root.
FFComponents.Player.PlayerColor: The player's colour: it tints their ship's livery and colours their name on the map, in chat and on their name tag. Simulation state, although nothing in the simulation reads it: every peer must show the same colour, joiners must receive it and saves must keep it, and the lockstep path gives all three.
FFComponents.Player.PlayerColor.IsCustom: 1 once the player chose a colour with `/color`; 0 while showing the palette default.
FFComponents.Player.PlayerColor.PaletteI: This player's default palette entry (0–9), kept when they pick a custom colour so `/color default` can return to it; `PlayerColorPalette.Unassigned` until the default system assigns one.
FFComponents.Player.PlayerColor.Rgb: The colour everyone shows, 0x00RRGGBB sRGB. Meaningless while unassigned.
FFComponents.Player.PlayerCombatState: Agreed player combat lifecycle state: whether the player is currently defeated/respawn-pending, and the simulation-time deadline of any active post-respawn damage-immunity grace window. Written only by the `PlayerDefeated`/`PlayerRespawn` ordered-op replay — never by presentation code. Both fields default to "alive, no active grace window", which is correct for every pre-029 save.
FFComponents.Player.PlayerManualDriveInt: Transient (non-`[Save]`) per-frame manual-station-driving intent on a player entity, written every frame by `DriveMobileStationAction` on whichever peer is currently driving.
FFComponents.Player.PlayerPanelRotateInt: Transient (non-`[Save]`) per-frame panel-rotate intent on a player entity, written every held frame by `MoveableStructureComponentPanel`'s rotate buttons and zeroed on release/close.
FFComponents.Player.PlayerProximityData: Singleton component that contains data about entities near the player. Used by other systems to check what items/entities are in proximity to the player.
FFComponents.Player.PlayerSimulationObje: Marks the invisible PlayerSimulation object: a real, KNN-participating entity that stands in for the visible player ship at the player's deterministic `Player.SimulationPosition`.
The visible player entity this simulation object stands in for.

On the visible player entity: a forward reference to its `PlayerSimulationObject`. Deterministic consumers that read the player's own KNN vision by entity lookup resolve it through this ref so they read the simulation object's vision (computed at the deterministic position) rather than the player's removed components.

Single source of truth for the component makeup of a player's `PlayerSimulationObject`. Both the production authoring path (`PlayerBaker`, at bake time) and the EditMode tests build the object through `Author{TSink}`, so the two can never drift.

Authors the full component set of the simulation object plus the player's forward reference. Transform-independence (no `Parent`) and LinkedEntityGroup membership are the caller's responsibility — those differ between the baking and runtime worlds.
Default authored KNN enemy-vision range for the player's simulation object.
Abstracts "add component T to entity" over a Baker (bake time) or EntityManager (runtime).
FFComponents.Player.PlayerWreckLifetime: How long a dead player's wreck stays in the world. The wreck carries a saved `FFComponents.Utils.LimitedLifetime`, which `LimitedLifetimeSystem` advances by the simulation step on every heartbeat, so the hour is an hour of simulated play: time spent paused, in a menu-paused game, or with the save closed does not count. When it runs out the wreck is deleted with everything still in it.
Test and recording knob (the dev-only `combat.wrecklifetime` automation command): when positive, wrecks made from now on live this many seconds instead. It is read by the `PlayerDefeated` apply, which runs on every peer, so every peer of a session must be given the same value before the death. Never set in a normal game.
FFComponents.Player.PlayerWreckOwner: Whose wreck this is: the `Player.Guid` of the player who died, written once by the `PlayerDefeated` apply on every peer. Only presentation reads it (each player's map shows the skull of their own wrecks only); looting a wreck is open to every player and does not look at it.
FFComponents.Player.RemotePresentationSm: Presentation-local smoothing state for a network-replicated remote player: the internal velocity of the critically-damped spring that follows `RemoteLocalTransformTarget`.
FFComponents.Player.SimulationPoseInitia: "This entity's authoritative simulation pose has been placed on every peer."
FFComponents.Power.ChargePulse: Progress of a charge consumer's energy pulse. Energy is in kW·s. Added next to every `ChargeConsumer` (ConfigLoadingUtil; old saves via Step0_50_0_35ChargeEnergy). Written by GridEnergySettlementSystem and the consumer systems; read by the grid calculation to estimate spike demand, so it must stay a pure function of saved state.
FFComponents.Power.GridEnergyState: Per-grid energy budget for spiky consumers. Not saved: every field is recomputed from saved state by the grid calculation (published at phase 5, and in one pass by the post-reset full recalculation) or rewritten every heartbeat by GridEnergySettlementSystem. Kept out of `StationGrid` so that struct's layout, still listed in old saves' type tables, is untouched.
FFComponents.Power.GridEnergyState.Backu: kW·s held by storage that covers factory load, for the time-left readout.
FFComponents.Power.GridEnergyState.Comba: kW taken out of the factory's supply for combat consumers. Combat only.
FFComponents.Power.GridEnergyState.Facto: kW of battery output the grid calculation committed to the factory for this window because generation fell short (phase 3). The settlement debits it every heartbeat.
FFComponents.Power.GridEnergyState.Gener: kW the grid's producers make, power received from other grids included, before the factory, pulses, storage recharge or transmitters take any of it. Battery output is not generation.
kW of `Generation` put to use: the factory, combat and pulse reserves, storage recharge and power sent through transmitters. The rest has nowhere to go this window.
Share of generation in use, 0 to 1: how hard a producer whose fuel or heat follows its output is working. Zero when nothing generates.
FFComponents.Power.GridEnergyState.Headr: kW the settlement may spend on spikes and storage recharge. Never taken from the factory.
FFComponents.Power.GridEnergyState.Pendi: kW of spare generation held for mass-driver pulses (phase 3); left out of GenerationInUse.
FFComponents.Power.PlayerStationGridMail: 062: the typed completion record for the load-time station-grid mailbox repair (`Serialization.PlayerStationGridMailboxRepairSystem`), written exactly once per load as a world singleton — the `Combat.CombatLegacyMigrationReport` shape and for the same reason.
The escaped exception, when `FlagFaulted` is set.
The repair reached its end without an unhandled exception.
An exception escaped the repair; `Fault` carries it.
Players this load had to give an empty mailbox to.
Players that already carried the mailbox — the normal, healthy count.
Players whose repair itself threw. Fail-closed per entity: the rest of the players are still repaired, and a non-zero value here means somebody must look.
Player entities the pass looked at (disabled ones included).
FFComponents.Power.StationGrid.Calculate: The larger the station, the more signal it emits. Every 100 units of stability will incur a % penalty increase to signal strength.
FFComponents.Power.StationGrid.Satisfact: The share of the power drawn that the grid supplies, from its last publish. A grid that has never published (`NumTimesCalculated` 0) reads 0, unpowered: its numbers are all zeros, and "nothing drawn" would otherwise read as fully powered for up to one calculation cycle (15 heartbeats), long enough for a just-placed exploration center with no energy to clear fog.
FFComponents.Power.StationGridAdmission: 062: the ONE answer to "does this placeable belong in a station grid?".
The main-thread form, for callers that have no `ComponentLookup{T}` (it can only be obtained from a system). An entity with no `Placeable` at all is not grid-worthy: it is not a placeable, whatever else it carries.

THE rule. A placeable is grid-worthy when it references a station grid, is not an unbuilt ghost, and occupies real vertical space — `Height == 0` means the `Placeable` was attached for something other than grid occupancy and is not on the grid at all.
The job form, for a caller that already holds the entity's `Placeable` — the load-path regrid gets it from `IJobEntity`, map generation gets it as `PlaceMapItem`'s `prefabPlaceable` parameter.
FFComponents.Power.StationGridInternal.C: The larger the station, the more signal it emits. Every 100 units of stability will incur a % penalty increase to signal strength.
FFComponents.Power.TargetStructureMemory: "Follow destination" for a structure aimed through a `RelativeGridTileTarget`: mass drivers and power distributors. Off: it aims at whatever stands at the stored offset, so moving the destination with a station leaves it aiming at the empty tile. On: it remembers the destination structure itself, and `RelativeGridTileTargetingSystem` links to it wherever either of them stands.
FFComponents.Presentation.ConnectorGhost: The emission a connector's end caps and corner curves show while the connector is still a ghost (a blueprint in hand, a paste preview, or a frame waiting for a construction bot). Those pieces are real meshes with the built connector's own materials, not hologram meshes, so a ghost shows whatever its materials emit.
Marks a ghost connector's cap or curve that currently carries the ghost emission override, and which connector it belongs to, so the override comes off once that connector is built.
FFComponents.Presentation.EngineExhaustM: What `EngineExhaustVfxPresentationSystem` remembers about one exhaust between rendered frames: where it was drawn last frame and its smoothed speed and thrust. Presentation only, never saved.
The afterburner level shown, 0..1: it lights at once and fades out.
Seconds since the afterburner last kicked in.
The drawn speed smoothed over a few frames only: what puts the afterburner out.
The drawn speed (world units per second) that counts as full thrust.
FFComponents.Presentation.EngineExhaustT: Per-instance input of the procedural exhaust shader (FinalFactory/VfxExhaust): x = thrust 0..1, y = a per-entity seed, z = afterburner 0..1, w = seconds since the afterburner last kicked in. Written every rendered frame by `EngineExhaustVfxPresentationSystem`. Presentation only, never saved.
FFComponents.Presentation.EngineExhaustV: Put on an engine's exhaust quad: a child GameObject on the nozzle, -Z pointing out of the engine, with a MeshRenderer drawing the VfxQuad with a FinalFactory/VfxExhaust material (shadows and probes off). The flame then grows with the ship's drawn speed and flares when it accelerates.
A kick-in age long past, so a fresh exhaust shows no ignition flash.
FFComponents.Presentation.ExhaustAfterbu: When an exhaust draws its afterburner.
FFComponents.Presentation.FlatMapMarker: The map and minimap square of a unit (a ship, a bot, an enemy): a child of the unit, drawn flat and axis-aligned whichever way the unit is turned (`FlatMapMarkerPlacement`). A structure's square is not tagged: it turns with its station, so a flying station's outline stays in one piece.
FFComponents.Presentation.FlatMapMarkerP: Where a unit's map square is drawn: at the position and size its unit gives it, with its own authored rotation (face up) instead of the unit's. As a plain child it turned with the unit's heading and tipped on edge with its pitch (a miner aims its hull down its beam), so the squares on the map spun and thinned to slivers.
Launch flag of the "before" arm of a comparison: squares turn with their units, as before.
FFComponents.Presentation.HaulerManualDr: What hand driving did to a station on the most recent heartbeat it moved it: the translation and the turn `HaulerManualDriveApplySystem` applied, stamped with that heartbeat.
FFComponents.Presentation.ImpactHull: What a unit looks like to a shot, seen from above as the camera sees it: its drawn parts' outline on the ground plane of its own frame (the unit's root position and rotation as drawn, without its scale), as a grid of `Cells` x `Cells` cells, a bit per cell. Measured by `ImpactHullCacheSystem` on the frame the unit is shot at, so it is the pose drawn. Presentation only.
FFComponents.Presentation.ImpactHull.Cel: One cell's size along x and z.
FFComponents.Presentation.ImpactHull.Cen: The middle of the grid (x, z) and the radius of a circle around it.
FFComponents.Presentation.ImpactHull.Min: The grid's corner (x, z) in the unit's frame.
FFComponents.Presentation.ImpactHull.Row: One row per cell along z; bit x set where the outline covers cell (x, z).
FFComponents.Presentation.ImpactHull.Tic: The `ImpactHullCacheSystem` update it was measured on.
FFComponents.Presentation.ImpactHull.Top: The height of the unit's highest drawn point, in its frame.
FFComponents.Presentation.ImpactHullCach: The measured hulls, by `VfxImpactSurfaceStep.HullKey`. Presentation only: written by `ImpactHullCacheSystem` on the main thread, read by the impact and beam presentation jobs. Not saved, not read by any simulation system.
FFComponents.Presentation.LocalPlayerMot: The outcomes `LocalPlayerMotionSystem` can have on one rendered frame. Numeric values are part of the CSV contract with `scripts/analyze_rubberband_trace.py` — append, never renumber.

Spec 057 (Design C′) — what `LocalPlayerMotionSystem` did with the local player's root on the frame that just ran. It exists so a trace can tell "clean because the mover works" apart from "clean because the mover never executed": a layer that silently no-ops produces the same visual-equals-root signature as one that is working perfectly.
The dt the mover integrated with this frame (0 when it did not integrate).
FFComponents.Presentation.MassDriverBeam: The per-instance `_BeamColor` of a mass-driver link laser (the MiningLaser shader the mass-driver laser uses): the driver's own laser colour, brightened while the driver is part of the hovered or selected mass-driver network. Absent = the material's own colour, which is what a default-coloured driver shows when it is not highlighted.
From a driver's `MassDriverLaserColor` to its laser's `_BeamColor` override.
Rec. 709 relative luminance of a linear colour.
FFComponents.Presentation.PendingStation: The Move or Land this peer's player just gave a flying station from its panel, kept until the station has done it, so the command answers the click at once instead of a heartbeat (host) or a round trip (client) later: a marker on the target and a path to it (`StationCommandFeedbackView`), the command's button lit on the station panel, and the station setting off along the flight the simulation is…
Presentation seconds since the command was given.
1 once the simulation's flight to the target (the transit) is over.
1 when the station was already flying when the command was given, so the flight can be drawn ahead.
The station's flight-rail position when the command was given: where its flight starts.
1 once the simulation has started flying the command.
The clicked spot (for a Land, the core's position on the pad).
How far along the flight the station is drawn (units), advanced by the simulation's speed rule.
FFComponents.Presentation.PickupCompanio: On the root of a pickup whose visible parts are managed companion objects (a VisualEffect, a ParticleSystem) rather than Entities Graphics meshes: the Lumin Orb, which is nothing but `vfx_Electricity_Loop_v3`. Baked by `PickupableBaker` from the prefab's own hierarchy, so a new pickup prefab drawn that way gets it without being named anywhere.
FFComponents.Presentation.PilotedStation: How the station the local player is piloting is drawn this frame: its simulation pose moved by a rigid offset (a turn about `Pivot`, then a translation) so it answers the pilot's keys in the frame they are read, the way the local ship does, instead of a heartbeat or a round trip later.

True when this changes how the station is drawn this frame: the offset, or the pose under it. A shared station is drawn on `BaseOf(float3)` for as long as this peer rides it, lift-off, landing and scheduled flight included, so the pose never changes under a moving station.
Where a point of the station whose base pose is `basePosition` is drawn.

A static-index mutation. `Remove` sorts BEFORE `Add` at the same key so a retire-then-republish inside one heartbeat resolves to the republished record, which is what "the provider moved or changed class" means.
FFCore.Combat.DeterministicSpatialIndexM: The pure fixed-point kernel of the shared deterministic spatial index: cell lattice math, overflow-safe delta/midpoint/bounds arithmetic, and the ONE total candidate comparator.
The hash-map key for a packed cell: a BIJECTIVE SplitMix64 finalizer, not the packed cell itself.

The inclusive cell span a range query around `centreRaw` must walk on one axis. Derived from SATURATING bounds rather than a cell radius: a radius computed as `(range + cell - 1) / cell` overflows for a large range and is asymmetric about a cell boundary, whereas flooring the two saturated bounds is exact for every input.

The centre cell of a span, computed through `Midpoint` so that a span whose raw bounds sum overflows still yields the true middle. Used when a span has to be narrowed symmetrically rather than truncated from one end.
Right shift applied to a raw delta magnitude before squaring.

True floor division of a raw `fp` coordinate by the cell edge. Plain integer division truncates toward zero, which folds the two cells straddling the origin into one — the negative-cell defect spec.md calls out under "negative-cell floor division".

THE TOTAL RANK (spec.md FR-004, contracts "Candidate rank is `(distance, x, y, z, key.W0, key.W1, key.W2, key.W3)`"): squared distance, then the raw fixed-point position words, then the four structural key words.
Largest squared distance the query can produce, = `3 * MaxShiftedDelta^2`.

Largest raw `fp` range the query accepts, = `MaxShiftedDelta` shifted back up. A larger range is clamped to this: beyond it the squared arithmetic is not representable, and no shipped vision range comes within three orders of magnitude of it.
Largest shifted per-axis delta admitted into a squared distance. `2^30`, so three squared terms sum to at most `3 * 2^60` and can never overflow a `long`.

`floor((a + b) / 2)` for EVERY pair of `long`s, including two values whose sum overflows. The naive `(a + b) / 2` wraps, and `a + (b - a) / 2` truncates toward zero and so is not the floor for negatives; this identity is exact for both.
Injective packing of a signed cell coordinate pair into one 64-bit word.
The squared bound a candidate's distance is compared against. A negative range admits nothing; a range past `MaxRangeRaw` is clamped there.
`a + b` clamped to the `long` range instead of wrapping.
`a - b` clamped to the `long` range instead of wrapping. Used before any bound is derived from two raw coordinates.
The squared distance between two authoritative fixed-point positions in the shifted domain, or `false` when any axis is beyond finite range.

The shifted magnitude of `a - b`, or `false` when the pair is further apart than `MaxShiftedDelta` admits — the "clip deltas beyond finite range before squaring" rule of the KNN contract, expressed as a rejection rather than a clamp so a too-distant candidate can never masquerade as a bounded one.
FFCore.Combat.DeterministicSpatialIndexV: The read-only bundle a query runs against: the static CSR pair, its overlay, and this heartbeat's dynamic map. ONE entry point, `QueryNearest`, so every consumer — the C3 vision system and the legacy float shim alike — reaches candidates through the same comparator and the same pruning, which is what makes their agreement a property of the code rather than of two implementations staying in step.
`DeterministicSpatialProviderFlags` bits a candidate may NOT carry. Zero — the default, and what every C3 query uses — excludes nothing.
Resolves an encoded provider reference from a query result.

The nearest `DeterministicSpatialIndex.ResultsPerHolder` providers of the admitted classes within `range`, nearest first under the total rank. A negative range, an empty class mask and an empty index all yield a zero-count result.
FFCore.Combat.DeterministicSpatialKey: Package-neutral 256-bit structural identity for C3 KNN ordering and fingerprints. Four unsigned words compared lexicographically `W0, W1, W2, W3`. Every field is either a bounded provider field packed losslessly or an injectively allocated `CombatObjectId`; it is never a truncated hash.
FFCore.Combat.DeterministicSpatialKey.Co: Unsigned lexicographic comparison over `W0, W1, W2, W3`.
FFCore.Combat.DeterministicSpatialKey.Cr: Enemy key: metadata + the enemy's saved `CombatObjectId`.
Fleet-ship key: metadata + the ship's saved `CombatObjectId`.
Player simulation object key: metadata + the player's saved `CombatObjectId`.
Projectile key: metadata + emitter `CombatObjectId` + 64-bit shot ordinal + 32-bit authored pattern subordinal; the low 32 bits of `W3` are reserved-zero.
Static placeable/defense key: metadata + owner `CombatObjectId` + 32-bit item identity + signed `int3` grid coordinate. Re-derived, never saved.
FFCore.Combat.DeterministicSpatialKey.Cu: Schema version stamped into every packed key's top byte.
FFCore.Combat.DeterministicSpatialKey.Ob: The packed 64-bit object identity word: the object's own `CombatObjectId` for player/fleet/enemy keys, the owner's for static keys, the emitter's for projectile keys.
FFCore.Combat.DeterministicSpatialKey.Pa: The projectile packing with NO validation, so a Burst job can call it — the `PackStaticGridObject` shape, extracted for the same reason and on the same evidence: `CreateProjectile` throws a formatted `ArgumentException` on the reserved zero emitter, which Burst cannot compile, and the T029 `CanonicalDynamicKey` precedent showed that the alternative — a second hand-typed copy of the bit layout — is…
The static-grid packing with NO validation, so a Burst job can call it.
FFCore.Combat.DeterministicSpatialKey.Pr: Projectile schema only: the authored pattern subordinal from `W3`'s high half.
Projectile schema only: the emitter's saved 64-bit shot ordinal (`W2`).
FFCore.Combat.DeterministicSpatialKey.St: Static schema only: the signed grid coordinate, full 32-bit two's complement per axis (x from `W2` low, y from `W3` high, z from `W3` low).
Static schema only: the 32-bit item identity from `W2`'s high half.
FFCore.Combat.DeterministicSpatialKey.Un: The reserved owner word for a static grid provider that has no owning combat object — an enemy-camp spawner, a map-generated derelict, or any placed structure whose station carries no `DeterministicCombatObjectId`.
FFCore.Combat.DeterministicSpatialKeyLoc: Where a published key currently lives: a CSR slot, or an overlay slot when the reference carries `DeterministicSpatialIndex.OverlayRefFlag`.
FFCore.Combat.DeterministicSpatialProvid: One provider in the shared index: an authoritative fixed-point position, its versioned structural key, its class, and a same-world `Entity` lookup handle.

Per-provider VISIBILITY bits (`DeterministicSpatialProviderFlags`), not identity. Never packed into a key, never persisted, never a sort term — the total rank still uses position and key only, so two providers that differ ONLY here still order identically. Added 055 T043 for the legacy family's `DisableKnnMarker` exclusion.

A provider's class, i.e. the bit it occupies in a query's class mask. Values 1-5 mirror `CombatSpatialKeyKind` so a key's kind byte IS its class; the non-admitted float movers get a class OUTSIDE the enum so that admitting them to the index costs no change to the T013-frozen key schema.
Every class, admitted or not — the mask the legacy float shim queries with.
The mask bit of a class, or zero for a class no 32-bit mask can address.
Highest class index a 32-bit mask can carry.

A float mover the 055 admission manifest does NOT admit (construction bots, drones, haulers). Keyed from its H-1 projected pose and masked out of every C3 query, so a float-derived key can affect memory layout only, never a C3 result.

Which per-family index a delta or a query belongs to. The families are the two the legacy `KnnSystem` already partitions on — `KnnFleetEntity` sources are seen only by fleet-vision holders and `KnnEnemyEntity` sources only by enemy-vision holders — and they carry different cell edges.

Which QUERIES a provider is hidden from. Visibility, deliberately separate from `DeterministicSpatialProviderClass`: a class says WHAT a provider is and is the term a C3 query masks on, while these bits say which consumer may not see it. Folding the two would mean losing a provider's kind in order to hide it from one family.
The provider carries `DisableKnnMarker` and is therefore invisible to the LEGACY float family — and only to it.

Orders providers by their structural key alone — the canonical order the index's stored arrays are kept in, so that index CONTENTS are a function of the live provider SET and not of the order the providers arrived in. Total because the key is injective over its declared live identity domain.
FFCore.Combat.DeterministicSpatialQueryR: One query's ranked result: parallel squared-distance and encoded provider-reference lists, nearest first, at most `DeterministicSpatialIndex.ResultsPerHolder` long.
FFCore.Combat.DeterministicSpatialStatic: The persistent per-family STATIC provider index: a cell-sorted CSR pair (dense per-cell offsets + a provider-index array) plus a small delta overlay of pending adds and tombstones, compacted at a deterministic element-count threshold.

Publishes a provider. Re-publishing a live key is an UPDATE (the old record is retired first), never a silent duplicate — a duplicate would make the key non-injective, which is the premise the whole total rank rests on.
Indices into `Providers`, grouped by cell in `CellStart` order.
Dense per-cell start offsets, `CellsX * CellsZ + 1` long.

Rebuilds CSR from the index's live contents. A PURE FUNCTION of those contents: the live providers are sorted by key, the grid bounds and cell edge are derived from their positions, and the cell grouping is a stable counting sort over that key order. Nothing about the order providers arrived in survives.

The read-only POINT-LOOKUP bundle over this static half, for a job that has to answer "is this entity a published static provider, and where is it?" — which `DeterministicSpatialIndexView` deliberately cannot, because a view carries only what a spatial QUERY needs (cells and provider arrays) and not the two identity maps.
The read-only bundle a query runs against, over this index and one heartbeat's dynamic map. The dynamic map must be created; an empty one is the correct way to query statics alone.
The same view, excluding every provider carrying any of `excludedFlags`. The legacy float shim is the only caller that passes a non-zero mask.
The CSR cell edge chosen by the last compaction; a power-of-two multiple of the family's.
Tombstoned CSR slots awaiting compaction.
Entity to published key, a same-world lookup handle for the ordered removal sites.
The family's cell edge, raw.
1 while the matching `Providers` slot is live, 0 once tombstoned.
Published, live providers.
Key to encoded provider reference. Looked up only, never iterated.
Adds not yet compacted into CSR.
Tombstoned overlay slots awaiting a seal or a compaction.
1 while the matching `Overlay` slot is live, 0 once tombstoned.
Overlay entries plus CSR tombstones — the quantity the compaction threshold measures.
Live providers from the last compaction, in key order; a removed slot stays in place.
Retires a published key. Returns false when the key was never published.

Drops tombstoned overlay entries and restores the overlay to key order, so the index's stored contents are canonical between compactions too. Cheap: the overlay is bounded by `DeterministicSpatialIndex.CompactionElementThreshold` in steady state, and a bulk load compacts instead of sealing.
The key an entity was published under, for the ordered removal sites — which know the entity being destroyed but not the provider key it was published under.

The live record published under a key, wherever it currently lives — the sealed CSR arrays or the delta overlay. For a reconciling publisher, which has to answer "does the index already hold exactly this?" before deciding to re-publish; re-adding an unchanged provider every heartbeat would churn the overlay and drag the index through compaction for no change in contents.

A read-only point lookup into ONE static half: entity to published key, and key to the live provider record. It is the STATIC counterpart of `DeterministicSpatialSnapshotMap.TryResolve`, which answers the same question for the dynamic half.

The live record published under a key. A tombstoned key is absent from `Locations` — `Remove` erases the entry — so a hit here is always live and no `Live`/`OverlayLive` test is needed, exactly as in `DeterministicSpatialStaticIndex.TryGetProvider`.

The record an ENTITY is published under in this half, or false when it publishes nothing here. Fails closed on `Entity.Null` rather than trusting the map: the null entity is never published, but a caller that reached this with one has a bug, not a miss.
FFCore.Combat.FixedPointGridRay: The pure fixed-point ray-vs-tile cell walk: the deterministic replacement for the float `CollisionWorld` raycast the legacy avoidance path probes with. It answers ONE question — which lattice cells does the segment `start → end` cross, in order, and through which face — and knows nothing about entities, blockers, ignore policy or response.
FFCore.Combat.FixedPointGridRay.CellLowe: The lower world coordinate of `cell` on one axis.
FFCore.Combat.FixedPointGridRay.MaxCells: Hard bound on cells emitted by one walk. The production probe is one heartbeat of travel plus a 1/60-second margin, so even a 1000 u/s mover at 16 UPS crosses ~9 tiles; the cap only exists so a pathological segment cannot spin, and truncation is deterministic (the walk simply stops, which reads as "no blocker beyond here").
FFCore.Combat.FixedPointGridRay.ToCell(2: Signed world-to-lattice conversion: `floor(world / tileLength)`, correct on both sides of the origin. `GridHelper.SnapToGrid(fp3)` does the same floor for the production tile lookup; this is the scalar form the walk needs, kept here so FFCore owns the arithmetic the traversal is defined in terms of.
FFCore.Combat.FixedPointGridRay.Traverse: Convenience form for tests and any caller that wants the whole ordered crossing list rather than the allocation-free `GridRayWalker` the production adapter uses. Returns the number of cells appended.
FFCore.Combat.GridRayCell: One cell a `GridRayWalker` crossed, in ray order.
FFCore.Combat.GridRayCell.Cell: Tile coordinate: `x`/`z` are floor-divided lattice indices, `y` is the walk's grid height level.
FFCore.Combat.GridRayCell.EntryFraction: Where along the segment this cell was entered, as the parametric fraction of `end - start` in `[0, 1]`. Monotonically non-decreasing over a walk, so comparing fractions orders cells by distance from `start` without a square root. The origin cell is entered at `fp.zero`.
FFCore.Combat.GridRayCell.EntryNormal: The OUTWARD normal of the cell face the ray crossed to get here: exactly one of `(±1,0,0)` or `(0,0,±1)`. `fp3.zero` for the origin cell, which was never entered through a face — a caller that treats the origin cell as a hit is in the "already inside" case and must synthesize its own normal, exactly as Unity Physics does for a ray starting inside a hull.
FFCore.Combat.GridRayWalker: Allocation-free forward enumerator over the cells of `FixedPointGridRay`'s walk. Burst-compatible and copyable by value, so a parallel job can create one per mover on the stack and abandon it the moment it finds a blocker — which is what makes the ordered "nearest blocker wins" scan free.
FFCore.Combat.RollbackGatedSystemAttribu: Marks a system whose enablement is owned by `CombatVisionRollback` and by NOTHING else.

Every type in the FF assemblies carrying this attribute, ordered by full name so the result does not depend on assembly load order. Scanned once per domain — the answer cannot change without a domain reload, which resets this static.

Read LIVE every time, never cached. The editor session key (`CombatVisionRollback.EditorForceC3SessionKey`) resolves at `SubsystemRegistration`, and an EditMode fixture flips the same static mid-session through `SetForTests`; a cached answer would strand either one.
FFCore.Config.AbilityProjectilePrefabs: The ability-projectile prefabs a fixed-heartbeat system needs to BIRTH an ability projectile. Before this, the Plasma bolt's prefab lived only in the managed `FFConfig.Instance.AbilityLookup[…].AbilityEffects[0]`, reachable from the MonoBehaviour cast action and from nothing inside ECS — which is precisely why the ordered birth was deferred at T017.
FFCore.Config.AbilityProjectilePrefabs.P: The Plasma bolt projectile prefab entity (`AbilityEffects[0]`).

The bolt's KNN vision range. The shared spawn helper derives this from the weapon's `SizeFp`, but the Plasma cast has always used the ABILITY radius — carrying it here keeps the ordered birth behaviour-identical to the cast it replaces instead of silently re-scoping every bolt's collision search.
`BlittableAbilityConfig.WeaponType` as an int — the key into `ItemConfig.ProjectileToWeaponConfig` the local cast used.
FFCore.Config.CraftConfigData.RecipeIsAn: This property is confusing but handles the case where an item can be crafted with any of the items in its recipe list. As of time of writing, this only apples to Ancient Tech Trash, which can be created with any artifact.
FFCore.Config.EntityConfig: Represents the immutable configuration for a single entity in the game. Not all the configs need to be filled out for every entity. For example, if you're adding a new entity that is not a terrain item, you don't need to fill out the TerrainConfig.
FFCore.Config.FleetConfig.AlertRadius: A second, larger advisory radius. Authored non-zero on the defense platform alone, where it draws a ring and gates nothing. Renamed from `AlertRange` alongside `EffectRadius`.
FFCore.Config.FleetConfig.EffectRadius: The radius, in WORLD units, over which this structure has its effect — link radius for a mass driver or power distributor, engagement radius for a defense platform, reveal radius for the exploration centre. Resolve it through `StructureRangeResolver`; never snapshot it onto an entity.
FFCore.Config.FleetConfig.SignalCost: Signal spent to fund one unit in the deterministic enemy-camp economy. A zero authored value is filled from the unit's owning spawner config during the managed post-config-load hook.
FFCore.Config.ItemConfig.LegacyNameToIdL: Names items used to have, mapped to the id they resolve to now — see `LegacyNames`. Only consulted when `IdToNameLookup` has no match, so a live name always wins. Exists because a saved blueprint stores item NAMES and carries no version, so a renamed item would otherwise make an old blueprint unplaceable forever.
FFCore.Config.LegacyNames: Old names of things whose DISPLAY name is also their PERSISTENCE key, mapped to what they are called now.
FFCore.Config.LegacyNames.Items: Old item `_name` to current item `_name`. Keys must be names that no live item uses any more; a live item always wins over an alias (see ConfigLoadingUtil.RegisterLegacyItemNames).
FFCore.Config.LegacyNames.ResolveTechnol: The current name for a technology name read out of a save. Unknown names are returned unchanged, so this is safe to run over an entire saved list.
FFCore.Config.LegacyNames.Technologies: Old technology `_name` to current technology `_name`. The save stores learned/queued/active technologies as these strings.
FFCore.Config.LogisticsUnitConfig.ItemsP: How many items this unit moves in a single load/unload transfer. 0 or 1 means one item at a time, which is what inserter arms use. Cargo barges batch a larger number so that filling up doesn't cost one heartbeat tick per item -- the load/unload timer is driven by the fixed timestep, so a unit can never perform more than one transfer per tick no matter how small LoadTimeMs gets.
ItemsPerTransfer, floored at 1 so that a config that never set it still moves one item per transfer.
FFCore.Config.LogisticsUnitConfig.StackS: How many normal stacks of an item this unit's own inventory slot can hold. A cargo barge keeps its whole load in a single slot, so without this the carried item's ordinary stack limit -- not CarryCapacity -- is what stops it filling, and a barge would quit at 100 ore however large its hold is.
StackSizeMultiplier, floored at 1 so that a config that never set it holds one ordinary stack.
FFCore.Config.MapGenerationData.WorldObj: Tracks what's been placed in each tile. This is to track issues where an object has been placed into a tile but its colliders aren't initialized yet and we want to avoid placing objects on top of it. Even if the colliders were working, however, we want a buffer zone around objects.
FFCore.Config.RenderingData.ModelPath: When creating new entities, you can either use an existing model or a new model that you added to the rendering Asset Bundle. If you want to use an existing model, you can use the name of the item from the game that you want otherwise use the name of the game object you added to the Asset Bundle
FFCore.Config.StructureRangeResolver: THE single resolver for a structure's DERIVED range — feature 063's "one meaning, one number" rule.
FFCore.Config.StructureRangeResolver.Con: The construction tower's build radius — pattern E, a boolean encoded as a distance: the "limit construction range" checkbox writes `FleetConfig.VisionRange` when ticked and 0 when not (`LogisticsNetworkPanel`), and `ConstructionTaskAssignerSystem` reads > 0 as "limited".
FFCore.Config.StructureRangeResolver.Def: The defense platform's alert radius. Player-configured and drawn as a second ring; it gates no behaviour today, which is exactly why it must not be confused with the attack radius above — different ceiling, different meaning.

The defense platform's engagement radius: the player's saved value, clamped to the config ceiling at READ time (the `InserterHelper.GetEffectiveReach` pattern), so a balance change to `FleetConfig.EffectRadius` can never be overridden by a stale saved value and no caller has to trust what the file held.
FFCore.Config.StructureRangeResolver.Exp: The radius an exploration center actually reveals, in fog TEXELS — the value written to `FogObserver.VisionRange` and compared by `FogOfWar.compute`.
`ExplorationVisionRadiusTexels` converted to world units, for the range ring.
FFCore.Config.StructureRangeResolver.Lin: A structure's derived link/effect radius in TILES — the unit `MassDriverSystem.IsDestinationWithinNetworkRange` takes.
`LinkRadiusTiles` in world units — the unit the range ring is scaled from and the unit `FleetConfig.EffectRadius` is authored in.
FFCore.Config.Technologies.TechnologyCon: One reward attached to a technology, as plain delegates so this config layer stays independent of the reward ScriptableObject types (which live in FFConfiguration).

Restores this reward's target to its un-researched baseline. Null / no-op for rewards that already write an absolute value. Paired with `RewardFn` so the whole reward set can be recomputed as a pure function of the learned technologies rather than accumulated onto whatever the target already held — see `ResearchController.RecomputeAllTechnologyRewards`.
FFCore.Config.WeaponConfig.AoeImpactDama: a splash instead of a flat area hit. When above 0, a hit deals this share of the shot's own damage to every OTHER valid target within `AoeImpactRadius` of the hit target (the shot's target keeps its full hit), and `AoeImpactDamage` is not used.
FFCore.Config.WeaponConfig.PlayerLeadFra: how far an enemy with this weapon leads a moving player when it fires, as a share of a full first-order intercept (0 = straight at the ship, 1 = where it will be if it holds course). Straight shots only: homing projectiles and beams ignore it.
FFCore.Controller.DisposableController: This Controller ensures that objects passed to it will be destroyed when the game is stopped including in the editor. On some systems (web/mobile), this may not actually destruct the objects, as the OS sometimes destroys backgrounded processes without giving them a chance to run any shutdown functions.
FFCore.Crafting.CraftItem.Count: The immutable base cost of the item. This is the cost of the item before any crafting modifiers are applied.
FFCore.Crafting.CraftItem.GetFinalCost(1: In game, players can adjust the crafting cost of items. This method returns the final cost of the item given the crafting modifier.
FFCore.Crafting.CrafterRateMath: Mirrors the effective-rate math in CrafterUpdateSystem.UpdateCraftProgress so any presentation surface can compute "what this crafter produces right now" without a second, independently-drifting formula. Satisfaction and overdrive scale craft SPEED; ProductionMultiplier and config.ProductionBonus add OUTPUT via the simulation's separate additional-production timer.
FFCore.Crafting.CrafterRateMath.ComputeC: How long one craft takes right now: the recipe's craft time over the same speed factor, the time CrafterUpdateSystem's craft progress needs to reach the recipe's BaseCraftTimeFP (UpdateCraftProgress, StartCraftingIfPossible). One craft makes the whole batch (countWhenCrafted items), so this is the batch's time, not an item's. The additional-production timer does not shorten it.
FFCore.Extensions.Ecs.Ready: True only when there is a World whose native side is still alive. A disposed World keeps its managed wrapper (`World.IsCreated` is `WorldUnmanaged.m_Impl != null`, nulled in `WorldUnmanaged.Dispose()`), so a plain null check is not a liveness test.
Seeds a freshly spawned entity's `LocalToWorld` from the `LocalTransform` just written to it, using the same root compose rule as `LocalToFFWorldSystem` (`localTransform.ToMatrix()`, then `PostTransformMatrix` when present).
Converts milliseconds to a fixed-point representation of seconds.
FFCore.FixedPoints.FpRailMath: Shared fixed-point rail math for the fp movement channels. Lives in FFCore so both FFSystems and tests reach it without duplicating the overflow guards.
FFCore.FixedPoints.FpRailMath.MassSpeedF: Deterministic replacement for the transit speed ramp's `math.log10((float)mass + 1)` (platform-variant transcendental — audit Class 2). fp has no log10 (`fpmath.log10` throws), so this derives it as `log2(mass + 1) / log2(10)`, pure fp end-to-end. Negative mass (should not occur) clamps to zero so the log argument stays >= 1.
FFCore.FixedPoints.FpRailMath.RailDistan: fp is Q31.32: squaring a component magnitude above ~16384 overflows inside `length`. Segments longer than that get scaled down, measured, and scaled back.
FFCore.Fleet.CombatUpgrades.Unmodified: The un-upgraded value of every multiplier here. Owned by the container's initial fill and reset (`CombatUpgradesSystem`) and by the technology rewards' baseline restore (`HitpointsUpgrade`, `CombatDamageUpgrade`, `UnitSpeedIncreaseReward`), which must agree or a reward recompute would silently shift every unit's stats.
FFCore.GameRunning.AttackData.RaidClockS: the simulation time the countdown started. Raids may launch once `MinElapsedTimeBeforeAttacks` minutes have passed since it.

where the raid countdown stands, one of the `RaidClock` states. Saved through `AttackPriorityCalculatorSystem`'s payload (v2); 0 (`RaidClock.Unresolved`) is a new game or a pre-v2 save, resolved on the scheduler's first run.
FFCore.GameRunning.AttackData.RaidClockT: which trigger started the countdown (`RaidClock` `Trigger*`); 0 until then.
FFCore.GameRunning.GameEdition: Which edition this process is: the demo or the full game. Set once at boot from the scene's `DemoController` (StartController), and readable from assemblies that cannot see it (FFNetcode's lobby and handshake code). Demo and full-game players never share a session: the lobby list and the connection handshake both compare this.
FFCore.GameRunning.GameplaySettings.Aste: Adjusts how much ore asteroids have. Each int represents the percent of the base asteroid resource.
FFCore.GameRunning.GameplaySettings.Atta: Adjusts how often enemies attack. Each int represents the percent of the base attack frequency.
Adjusts how many enemies attack. Each int represents the percent of the base number of attackers.
FFCore.GameRunning.GameplaySettings.Camp: Scales the camp-placement density curve: 100 = the curve as authored, 0 = no camps (explorer mode). Each int represents the percent of the base camp density.
FFCore.GameRunning.GameplaySettings.Craf: Adjusts the cost of crafting. Each int represents the percent of the base crafting cost.
FFCore.GameRunning.GameplaySettings.Disa: Whether or not all enemy spawning is disabled in the game.
FFCore.GameRunning.GameplaySettings.Enem: RETIRED: super-chunks retired with the runtime camp-generation cascade — density is now CampDensityByDistance × CampSpawnProbabilityMultiplier. Field kept for save compatibility.
Adjusts how strong enemies are in the game. Each int represents the percent of the base enemy strength.
FFCore.GameRunning.GameplaySettings.Expl: Whether or not the game is in explorer mode, which means enemy camps don't spawn and extra enemies spawn around asteroids.
FFCore.GameRunning.GameplaySettings.Hide: Whether or not the initial planet and oracle are hidden.
FFCore.GameRunning.GameplaySettings.Infi: Asteroids never run out of resources when this is true.
FFCore.GameRunning.GameplaySettings.Sign: The signal penalty per 100 stability. So if this is.1, then each 100 stability incurs a 10% penalty to signal strength.
FFCore.GameRunning.GameplaySettings.Spaw: Whether or not loot boxes should spawn in inactive chunks.
FFCore.GameRunning.GameplaySettings.Stab: Adjusts the stability required for stations. Each int represents the percent of the base stability requirement.
FFCore.GameRunning.GameplaySettings.Stac: Adjusts the size of stacks. Each int represents the percent of the base stack size.
FFCore.GameRunning.GameplaySettings.Tech: Adjusts the cost of technology. Each int represents the percent of the base technology cost.
FFCore.GameRunning.LocalViewSettings: This player's own view choices. Each peer holds its own copy, kept in PlayerPrefs, so it is never saved in the world, never sent to other peers and never hashed. Simulation must never read it: two players with different settings run the same game.
FFCore.GameRunning.LocalViewSettings.App: Keeps `settings` in PlayerPrefs and in this world's singleton.
FFCore.GameRunning.LocalViewSettings.Hid: Hides cargo barges' meshes (CargoDroneVisibilitySystem); the barges keep flying.
FFCore.GameRunning.LootBoxChunkData: Singleton component that tracks loot box spawning data per chunk
FFCore.GameRunning.RaidClock: the raid countdown. Raids (signal-funded attack waves from enemy camps) may launch only `CombatSettings.MinElapsedTimeBeforeAttacks` minutes after the countdown starts, and it starts at the first of three triggers, for the whole session: any player's Ship Assembler is built, the tutorial's combat steps are done, or Asteroid Science is researched.
FFCore.GameRunning.RaidClock.CountdownEl: True once the countdown has started and run its full length.
FFCore.GameRunning.RaidClock.TriggerFixt: Started by a test or automation fixture.
FFCore.GameRunning.RaidClock.TriggerLega: A save that already had raids, or was past the old countdown from game start.
FFCore.GameRunning.RaidClock.TryResolve(: Settles `Unresolved`. A save that already raided, or whose game is past the old countdown (which ran from game start), keeps raiding: its countdown is already over. Anything else waits for a trigger, a new game included. With a countdown of 0 minutes (test configs) every game counts as past it, so it starts at once.
FFCore.GameRunning.RaidClock.TryStart(3): Starts the countdown at `now`; false when it already started.

FFCore.Time.HeartbeatMath.ForwardDistanc: Forward circular distance from `from` to `to`: the number of heartbeats you advance, stepping forward, to get from `from` to `to`. FFCore.Time.LootSimulationSchedule: Pure simulation-time identity for loot decisions. The saved monotonic simulation clock, rather than wall time or the wrapping heartbeat counter, is quantized into fixed windows that remain stable across peers, saves, and joins.
FFCore.Time.SimulationRate: Rate-independence helpers for simulation behaviour that was written against a heartbeat COUNT instead of simulated seconds. Every helper is pure fp/integer arithmetic on values that are identical on every peer (the fixed step `Dt`, the configured updates-per-second, the deterministic simulation clock), so the result is lockstep-safe.
FFCore.Time.SimulationRate.BalanceRefere: The heartbeat rate single-player ran at before 057 US4, which the per-heartbeat balance numbers in the codebase and configs were tuned against. Not the live rate: never use this as `Dt`.
FFCore.Time.SimulationRate.EventsDueAtHe: The heartbeat-counter form of `EventsDueThisStep`, for a cadence that was written as "every Nth heartbeat": `floor(h·r/ups) − floor((h−1)·r/ups)` in exact integers. At the reference rate with `r = 60/N` it reproduces `h % N == 0` exactly; at any other rate it pays out `eventsPerSecond` per simulated second (1 or 2 per heartbeat for 20/s at 16 UPS).
FFCore.Time.SimulationRate.EventsDueThis: How many events a steady schedule of `eventsPerSecond` owes in the fixed step that ended at simulation time `now`: `floor(now·r) − floor((now − dt)·r)`. Stateless (nothing to save), deterministic, and exact over any run of steps — the per-step counts telescope to `floor(now·r)`, so the long-run rate is `eventsPerSecond` at any heartbeat rate. `now` is `FFTimeData.simulationElapsedTime`.
FFCore.Time.SimulationRate.ReferenceHear: How many reference-rate heartbeats one heartbeat at `updatesPerSecond` spans: exactly 1 at 60 UPS, exactly 3.75 at 16 UPS. Taken from the configured rate (`HeartbeatData.UpdatesPerSecond`, identical on every peer) rather than from `Dt`, because `Dt` at 60 UPS is 2^32/60 truncated and would make the reference rate itself scale by 1 − 2^-28 instead of exactly 1. Returns 1 for a non-positive rate.
FFCore.Time.SimulationRate.ScaleReferenc: A heartbeat count tuned at the reference rate (a stride, a phase group), converted to the count that spans the same wall-clock time at `updatesPerSecond`: rounded to nearest, never below 1. 12 at 60 UPS → 3 at 16 UPS. Inputs ≤ 1 stay 1 (run every heartbeat).
A per-heartbeat probability tuned at the reference rate, rescaled so its expected number of successes per simulated second is unchanged (and so is the mean wait, `dt / p`). Clamped to 1.

FFCore.Utils.ClosestByTileSelector.TileD: Planar (x/z) squared tile distance — the deterministic primary key.
FFCore.Utils.CriticallyDampedSpring: The critically-damped spring used by every presentation smoother — the Game Programming Gems 4 form, which is the algorithm behind `Vector3.SmoothDamp`.
