FFCore.Utils.CriticallyDampedSpring.Adva: Advances `position` toward `target` over `dt`, carrying the spring's internal velocity in `velocity`. `smoothTime` is the time constant: the steady-state tracking lag behind a target moving at a constant speed is roughly speed * smoothTime.
FFCore.Utils.EntityCommandBufferWrapper: Provides a simple abstraction around the EntityCommandBuffer and EntityCommandBuffer.ParallelWriter so that we can use the same code for functions that are shared between concurrent and non concurrent systems.
FFCore.Utils.FpCurve: Piecewise-linear evaluation of a fixed-point curve stored as SmallBuffer control points (X ascending). Clamps to the first/last Y outside the domain. All math is fixed-point, so results are identical on every peer.
FFCore.Utils.GridHelper.FloorToIntSafe(1: This method tries to deal with floating point imprecision. It will round to the nearest integer, but if the result is within epsilon of the rounded value, it will return the rounded value, to account for cases where the float is reallllllllllly close to the upper boundary of a tile, so it should not be floored and instead should be rounded.
FFCore.Utils.GridHelper.GetAdjacentModul: The distinct modules on the tiles around a footprint, in the order the tile scan first meets them. Never a hash set's order: that follows Entity indices, which are World-local, and StationConnectionsSystem appends connections in this order, so a strut taking both of its neighbours as inputs listed them differently on each peer and each kept a different grid object when that strut joined two grids.
FFCore.Utils.GridHelper.GetChunkFromPos(: Chunk lookup from a fixed-point simulation position (e.g. Player.SimulationPosition). The chunk-exploration trigger path must use this or `GetChunkFromTile` — never the float overloads, whose inputs are presentation transforms.
FFCore.Utils.GridHelper.GetChunkFromTile: Integer-only chunk lookup from a grid tile — no float round-trip.
FFCore.Utils.GridHelper.GetEntitiesInTil: Gets the list of entities contained within the following tiles based on the given parameters. Used in Gherik's mod. Do not change or delete for now.
FFCore.Utils.GridHelper.GetFpWorldPositi: Fixed-point twin of `GetWorldPositionCenterFromGridTile` — same center semantics from the lower-left grid tile. All inputs are integers scaled by half-tile (5) / tile (10) units, which are exactly representable in both float and fp, so for a tile-snapped structure this equals the float derivation (and the LocalTransform placement sets from it) bit-for-bit.
Obtains the world position from the bottom left of the given tile
FFCore.Utils.GridHelper.GetOccupiedTiles: Gets the occupied tiles from the provided placeable
FFCore.Utils.GridHelper.GetPlaceableBoun: Obtains the minimum and maximum grid tile that the given placeable (by its fields) will occupy based on the provided world position. Thee worldPosition is in the center of the localTransform, so need to adjust to the upper left of the item to get the tileGrid (based on the placeable length and width).
FFCore.Utils.GridHelper.GetWorldPosition: Obtains the world position of the center of a placeable with a given width and length with the grid tile that is the lower-left corner of the object.
Obtains the world position from the bottom left of the given tile
FFCore.Utils.GridHelper.IsWithinCamera(2: Returns whether the given GridTile is within the view of the camera, if the camera is at the given position
FFCore.Utils.GridHelper.IsWithinCamera(4: Returns whether any part of a multi-tile footprint is within the view of the camera. Multi-tile placeables are keyed by their LOWER-LEFT tile, so testing only that single tile (the overloads above) reports "off-camera" for an object whose origin corner is off the bottom/left screen edge while most of its footprint is still visible — camera-gated presentation (child transforms, animations) then fre…
FFCore.Utils.GridHelper.RoundToGrid(2): Rounds the x and z values of the inputted vector to the nearest multiple of 5. Determines the y value based on the heightPosition, which is a PlaceableConfig value.
FFCore.Utils.Int2LexicographicComparer: Deterministic lexicographic ordering for chunk/tile coordinates (x, then y). Use this whenever simulation iterates a set of chunks — unordered-collection enumeration order is not peer-stable.
FFCore.Utils.InterceptAim: first-order intercept aiming in fixed point. A straight shot at `projectileSpeed` meets a target moving at a constant velocity after the smallest positive t with |toTarget + velocity·t| = speed·t.
FFCore.Utils.InterceptAim.AimPoint(5): Where to aim: the target's position moved along its velocity for `leadFraction` of the intercept time (1 = a full intercept, 0 = straight at it). With no intercept solution it aims straight at the target.
FFCore.Utils.InterceptAim.TryInterceptTi: The time until a straight shot from the shooter meets the target, or false when it never can (the target outruns the shot, or the speed is not positive). A stationary target gives distance / speed.
FFCore.Utils.LinkedEntityGroupHygiene: Keeps a `LinkedEntityGroup` free of dangling references. A group that names a destroyed entity makes the next `Instantiate` of its owner assert ("The srcEntity's LinkedEntityGroup references an entity that is invalid") — inside a Burst job that is a hard abort of a built player.
FFCore.Utils.LinkedEntityGroupHygiene.Re: Removes every entry (except the owner at index 0) whose entity no longer exists. Returns the count removed.
Removes the named entity from the group wherever it appears (index 0, the owner, is never touched).
FFCore.Utils.MathHelper.CompareTilesLexi: Lexicographic (x, then y, then z) total order over grid tiles: -1 if a < b, 1 if a > b, 0 if equal. Used as a peer-stable deterministic tiebreak when two candidates are otherwise equidistant (tiles are unique per placed structure), so container-iteration order can't decide the winner differently across peers.
FFCore.Utils.SmoothedUiValue: Spec 057 — the per-surface smoothing state behind a UI readout bound to a value the simulation only moves on the heartbeat. At 16 UPS a slider assigned straight from simulation state visibly ticks 16 times a second; these two rules present the SAME value continuously at render rate without ever writing it back.
FFCore.Utils.SmoothedUiValue.PresentCont: Presents a value that moves in both directions (charge, temperature, power rates) as a one-heartbeat lerp from the previous authoritative value to the current one. No monotone hold and no backward snap: falling is normal here, so treating a decrease as a reset would make every drop tick instead of glide.
FFCore.Utils.SmoothedUiValue.PresentProg: Presents a monotone progress value. `fraction01` is how far the rendered frame has travelled toward the next heartbeat, in [0, 1] — the CLAMPED `PresentationClock.SecondsSinceHeartbeat` over the heartbeat interval, which is what makes a pause or a lockstep stall freeze the bar instead of extrapolating into the void.
FFCore.Utils.SmoothedUiValue.Reset(0): Drops all smoothing state, so the next present snaps to the authoritative value. Call this on any discontinuity the struct cannot see: the panel retargeting to another entity, a pooled row being reused, the tracked recipe/tech changing.
FFCore.Utils.TileCandidate: A candidate entity with its peer-stable tile, for `ClosestByTileComparer`.
FFCore.Version.FFVersion.IsGameVersionCo: Returns true if the two FFVersions are compatible with each other, even if their versions differ. We guarantee binary compatibility only for RC changes.
FFCore.Version.FFVersion.IsSaveCompatibl: Save compatibility is a bit more lenient than mod compatibility. We load any save from `MinimumSaveVersion` up to and including `FinalFactoryVersion`, because upgrade fragments migrate older saves forward. Saves written by a NEWER game version than the one running are rejected.
FFCore.Version.FFVersion.MinimumSaveVers: The oldest save this build will load. Saves below it are refused outright rather than migrated forward.
FFCore.Version.FFVersion.ReleasedUtc: When this version was released, in UTC (ISO 8601): the moment its release bump was made. The main menu shows it beside the version. The bump writes it together with the line above (scripts/trigger-ci-release.sh, and BuildCommand2's UpdateMinorVersion), so every player, platform and edition of a release shows the same time whatever its clock and time zone.
FFCore.Version.FFVersion.ToGameVersionCo: Returns just the portion of the FFVersion that denotes compatibility. Since changes to patch and rc don't break compatibility for mods (function definitions don't change, etc), sometimes systems only want the major mod revisions.
The HOST's candidate POOL for the ordered-ability validator, built off an `EntityManager` on the main thread outside any system: the ability's unit tag, a cooldown component and no active marker — deliberately WITHOUT the ownership half of `InactiveAbilityShape{TUt,TAt}`.
FFSystems.Abilities.CombatAbilityCommand: The every-peer applier for the mover-command abilities. It replaces `MultiCastJob`'s selection — spec.md FR-015 amendment, isolation-manifest.md §8 fork 2.

The Obliterator disc's spawn shape, lifted verbatim from the legacy local cast (`ObliteratorAbility.CreateObliteratorDisc`): the disc is born far above the cast point and ObliteratorDiscJob drops it onto the point once a Krillo is in position; the charge is a 2 s scale-up from a tenth to double size, slowed by missing Krillos.
FFSystems.Abilities.FrenzyISystem.Frenzy: The mover's own rail. This job is `Schedule`d single-threaded, so the lookup needs no parallel-restriction waiver.
The op-carried release edge; see the release branch in Execute.
Agreed `FFTimeData.simulationElapsedTime` raw, never a per-peer clock.
FFSystems.Abilities.GoToSpotAbilityJob.R: The rail approach speed: 150 u/s, or the whole remaining distance in this step if that is less.
The mover's own rail; see `ReturnSystem.ReturnJob.Rails`. This job is scheduled BOTH ways — `Schedule` from and `ScheduleParallel` from — so it carries the waiver the parallel case needs.
The op-carried release edge, when the commanded ship has one. See the release branch in `Execute` for why it outranks both legacy gates.
FFSystems.Abilities.GoToSpotAbilityJob.S: Agreed `FFTimeData.simulationElapsedTime` raw, never a per-peer clock.
FFSystems.Abilities.PlayerAbilityStateIn: Installs the ordered player-ability state on every player entity, on every peer.
FFSystems.Artifacts.AncientPortalCollisi: Fires once per heartbeat with the ancient portal the local player is currently flying into, or `Entity.Null` when it is not in one. The raw state is reported every heartbeat rather than only the moment of entry so consumers can tell "still in the same portal" apart from "flew out and back in again".
FFSystems.Artifacts.AncientPortals.Ancie: Names are a pure function of peer-stable identity — master seed + the portal's tile — never of generator call order, entity handles, or process randomness: the result lands in [Save] NamedEntity and (in multiplayer) in the mining activation payload, so every peer and every run-twice replay must derive the same name for the same portal.
FFSystems.Artifacts.PendingStructureActi: Lands pending activations on the heartbeat they are due. Main thread and unbursted on purpose: it is idle unless a structure was mined in the last few seconds, and landing one makes structural changes and raises the presentation hook. Runs before `ActivatableStructureActivationSystem` so the model swap follows on the same heartbeat.
FFSystems.Artifacts.StructureActivation: Scheduling and landing of a mined activation (`PendingStructureActivation`). The networked mining completion schedules; `PendingStructureActivationSystem` lands it on the heartbeat the simulation clock reaches the due time. Everything here reads and writes simulation state only; the sound, narration and map label hang off `Completed`.
The activation itself: production's writes from after its wait, in the same order.
Lands every activation whose due time has been reached, in tile order: the rewards are instantiated here, and chunk order is each peer's own load history.

Raised on every peer right after an activation has landed, with the structure and the schedule it carried. Presentation only: the handler must not write simulation state. A throwing handler is logged and swallowed.

How many Ancient Portals this world has opened, counting the ones whose activation is still pending. The world's fact behind the first-portal voice line: it comes from the saved portal states alone, so it is the same on every peer and in a save from before this existed.
One activation schedule as an audit detail: identical text on peers that agree.
The simulation time at which an activation scheduled now takes effect.
True once a structure is activated, or its activation is scheduled and the burst is playing. Either way it is no longer a mining target.
FFSystems.Blueprints.BlueprintMirror: The integer math of flipping a held blueprint: every value a structure in a blueprint carries that has a handedness, and what it becomes in the mirror image. Pure functions over existing component values, so the held-blueprint flip (`BlueprintFlipSystem`) and its tests share one copy.
FFSystems.Blueprints.BlueprintMirror.IsE: `IsExactMirror` loosened to edges: every singled-out slot lands on the edge its mirror image is on, though not necessarily on the same tile of it.

Whether `placeable` turned to `mirroredFacing` is the exact mirror image of itself across `axis`: the same footprint extents, and every slot its config singles out (allowed, blocked, required for a direct connection, the special input and output) sitting on the mirror image of where it sat.
FFSystems.Blueprints.BlueprintMirror.Mir: Mirrors a held structure's anchor (`BlueprintItemMarker.RelativeTilePosition`, the bottom-left tile of the footprint at its origin) and its body offset (`OriginalTileOffset`, body minus origin, non-zero for inserter arms and cargo barges) about the centre of the held footprint, whose bounds on the mirror axis sum to `boundsMinPlusMax` (min tile + max tile, so the centre is half of it).
The mirror image of a facing (or of a world edge, which uses the same enum).

The facing a structure takes in the mirror image: the plainly mirrored facing when its connection slots line up there, else the first quarter turn from it whose slots do and whose footprint has the same extents.

mirrors a junction's per-side levels (`JunctionSidePriority.Levels`, one byte per base-frame side slot of a 1x1): each side's level moves to the slot of the mirror image of its edge, so "west input 1" becomes "east input 1" on an X flip. Its turns are not carried: a placed junction starts with none.

Mirrors an output priority (`RoundRobinOutputToConnector.PriorityIndex`, a base-frame slot; -1 for none) by EDGE: the priority moves to the mirror image of the edge it names, at that edge's first slot, which is how the output priority panel stores an edge (`StationConnectionsSystem.GetSlotForEdge`).

Mirrors a mass driver's or power distributor's target offset (`RelativeGridTileTarget.Value`: target tile minus the source's bottom-left tile). The result names the mirror image of the tile the original named, measured from the mirrored source's bottom-left, which is inside the mirrored target whatever its size (the targeting system accepts any of the target's tiles).
The world perimeter slot that is the mirror image of `worldSlot` on a footprint `worldWidth` x `worldLength` tiles.
FFSystems.Blueprints.BlueprintMirror.Rot: One clockwise quarter turn of a target offset, for a source whose world width before the turn is `sourceWidthBeforeTurn`: `(x, z) -> (z, -x + W - 1)`, the rotated image of the named tile measured from the rotated source's bottom-left (see `MirrorRelativeTarget`).
FFSystems.Blueprints.MirrorAxis: Which way a held blueprint is mirrored. `Horizontal` swaps left and right (the mirror line runs up the screen, x changes); `Vertical` swaps top and bottom (z changes). Factorio's names.
FFSystems.Bosses.AncientGuardianRegenSys: The Ancient Guardian heals a fraction of its max health per second (its config's HealingRateFP) continuously, in and out of combat, so it cannot be whittled down across repeated deaths and retreats. Unlike `FFSystems.Combat.HealthRegenSystem` there is no post-damage delay, and the Guardian carries no HealthRegenData, so the two never both heal it.
FFSystems.Bots.NetworkedStorageCacheQueu: Drains the `NetworkedItemUpdate`s a parallel job produced into the "real" list that `NetworkedInventoryCacheUpdaterSystem` applies to `NetworkedItemsCache`.
FFSystems.Combat.C3PoseSource: Where a C3 consumer's pose for one entity came from. The point of naming the four cases is that only ONE of them may ever be a transform read, and it is the case that is not a mover at all.
FFSystems.Combat.C3StaticIndexMaintenanc: The SOLE mutator of the shared deterministic spatial index (isolation-manifest.md §5). Once per heartbeat it: drains `C3StaticIndexIntake`, sorts the deltas by family and structural key, and applies them to the static halves; retires any indexed provider whose entity now carries `DeletionMarker` — the ordered removal signal; seals or compacts each static half, whichever the frozen element-count th…

The rollback gate re-evaluated on EVERY resume, not just at world creation. `OnCreate` runs once per World, so its verdict was silently overridden by anything that enabled this system afterwards — `SystemManager`'s blanket `"FFSystems."` substring pass being the one that actually happened in production.
FFSystems.Combat.C3VisionProvisioningSys: Puts the C3 vision records ON the entities that are allowed to have them, and keeps each record's query range equal to its legacy twin's.
The enemy-family twin of `MirrorFleetRangeJob`, deliberately a separate type so each declares write access to exactly its own C3 component and read access to exactly its own legacy one.
Copies one holder's legacy fleet query range into its C3 twin.
FFSystems.Combat.C4CombatTargetKeyBridge: The single named C4 -> C3 handoff. It runs in fixed-POST after `TargetingSystem`, translates that heartbeat's selected `Targeter.TargetEntity` through the provider/key registry, and writes `CombatMoverTargetReferences.TargetKey`. Because the C3 resolver already ran in fixed-PRE, a key published at H is first visible to C3 at H+1 — that one-heartbeat delay is the contract, not a defect.
FFSystems.Combat.CombatIdentityAssignmen: 055 T026(d): the serial early-fixed assigner for deferred birth reservations. Entities created OUTSIDE the fixed groups (player join claims, new-game bootstrap) carry `PendingCombatIdentity` provenance stamped at a peer-converged point; once per heartbeat this system drains ALL pending records, passing the ones that do not yet carry an id as one named batch through `CombatObjectIdentityReservation…
FFSystems.Combat.CombatIdentityHealSyste: gives a combat identity to every enemy spawner station and every enemy ship that has none, on every peer, in the same heartbeat, from provenance every peer shares.
FFSystems.Combat.CombatLoadPathProvision: The one place a freshly applied world is given its combat identities, rails and C3 vision holders — synchronously, at the end of the load, BEFORE the world is handed to the heartbeat.

Runs the three passes in their declared order and completes their jobs, so the caller can keep making structural changes immediately afterwards. Records a census either side of the pass: "the provisioning ran and this is what it found" is then a read in the audit stream rather than an inference from a downstream fingerprint.
FFSystems.Combat.CombatMoverRailAvoidanc: The FFGrid blocker adapter: the FFSystems half of the deterministic grid query. It turns the pure ordered cell walk `GridRayWalker` produces into the legacy avoidance OUTCOME — which occupant blocks, whether it is ignored, and what displacement replaces this heartbeat's travel — reading nothing but simulation truth.
The discrete FFGrid height level to probe at. `FFGrid.EntityMap`'s `int3` key carries a LEVEL in `y`, not a third lattice axis, and the world height of each level is a fixed table.

The exact fixed-point reading of `LinearMotionStep.WorldCollisionLookaheadSeconds` (`1f/60f`): the avoidance margin expressed in seconds of travel, so it is heartbeat-rate-invariant. Built from integers rather than converted from the float constant, so no float round trip reaches the probe.
The exact fixed-point reading of `LinearMotionStep.TangentSlideSpeed` (`60f`): the tangential slide speed while deflecting, frozen by 057 at 60 u/s at every heartbeat rate (tolerance-manifest §1).
The FFGrid lattice pitch the walk floor-divides world coordinates by.
Resolves this heartbeat's displacement for a rail mover with world collision enabled, and updates the mover's avoidance latch/sign in place.
FFSystems.Combat.CombatMoverRailMirrorSy: While a mover's rail is NOT the position authority, this system rewrites that rail's pose from the legacy float authority every heartbeat — the standing discharge of the re-seed obligation `CombatMoverRailExclusion.AuthorityFlagAtLegacyMigration` has recorded since T031.
FFSystems.Combat.CombatMoverRailProjecti: The ONE place a fixed-point rail becomes a float `LocalTransform`.
FFSystems.Combat.CombatMoverRailProvisio: Installs a C3 rail on every admitted mover the load-only migration cannot reach — a new game's bootstrap population and every runtime spawn — so the rail population is IDENTICAL on every peer regardless of which path that peer took into the world.
FFSystems.Combat.CombatMoverSimulationSy: The fixed-point enemy/fleet integrator: the heartbeat step that turns rail velocity and the prior heartbeat's forces into the rail's authoritative position (data-model.md §2, contracts/simulation-and-vision.md). A mover whose rail owns its position integrates HERE and is skipped by `LinearMotionSystem` — one authority, never two (`CombatMoverRailExclusion.OwnsPosition` is the shared predicate).
FFSystems.Combat.CombatMoverSpatialSampl: Resolves the persisted semantic references of every rail-backed mover and projectile against this heartbeat's `DeterministicSpatialSnapshotMap` (data-model.md §2 and §5; contracts/simulation-and-vision.md "Chase/homing target-sample contract").
FFSystems.Combat.CombatObjectSequenceBoo: 055 T026(a): bootstraps the world's `DeterministicCombatObjectSequence` singleton at world creation with `NextObjectId = 1` (zero is the reserved "no object" id — `CanonicalAssignmentCore` fails closed on a zero sequence). Every peer creates the identical singleton at the identical point, so the allocator itself is never a divergence source.
FFSystems.Combat.CombatObjectSequencePer: Carries the world's combat-id allocator watermark (`DeterministicCombatObjectSequence.NextObjectId`) through every save and every multiplayer join / desync-recovery snapshot.
Payload v1: one little-endian uint64, the live `NextObjectId`.
True between a load's system-deserialize phase and the migration consuming it.
Stages a watermark as if a save had carried it (tests and explicit load paths).
Read-and-clear: the value the save being applied carried, or null for a save written before this system existed. Cleared on read so a later load of an old save can never inherit it.
FFSystems.Combat.CombatRailProvisioning: The ONE definition of "what a freshly seeded C3 mover rail contains", shared by the two construction sites so they cannot drift.
Writes one admission class's clauses into a query description. The caller supplies its own family clauses (which components make it a rail candidate or a vision holder) and calls this for each class, chaining with `EntityQueryBuilder.AddAdditionalQuery`.

The rail a mover starts with, from its legacy float record plus the ALREADY-QUANTIZED simulation pose its caller read. The pose is a parameter rather than a lookup because the two callers read it from different places for the same value: the migration from the restored `LocalTransform` during the load, the provisioner from the live one on a heartbeat.

The three admission classes the two C3 provisioners share. An entity is a candidate for provisioning under exactly one of them, and `Admit` writes that class's clauses into an `EntityQueryBuilder` description.

A pre-C3 mover has no authoritative heading field, so it is derived in fp from the quantized velocity. A stationary mover gets world-forward; behaviour rewrites the heading on the first heartbeat it moves, and presentation facing is projection output, never a rail input.

The ONE float-pose quantization for a rail seed. `CombatLegacyMigrationSystem.Quantize` delegates here (and `SaveGameManager`'s projectile migration reaches it through that delegate), so the two record families cannot quantize the same saved float differently — which would be a cross-peer desync between entities that took different paths.
The DERIVED half of a rail's flag word for a mover that still carries a legacy `LinearMotion`, i.e. exactly what `CombatLegacyMigrationSystem.ReconcileRailAuthority` stamps at every load.
The flag word of a fresh seed: the one eligibility grant, plus the legacy float toggles and latches carried across as bits.
The pose a fresh rail is seeded from, and the fail-closed refusal to seed one from a pose that is not yet real.
FFSystems.Combat.DeathSystem.DeathEntiti: The entity each `DeathMarkersThisFrame` entry belongs to, index-aligned with it. Presentation readers (the per-player Steam achievements) use it to tell the local player's death from a teammate's. Written only here; no simulation system reads it.
FFSystems.Combat.DeathSystem.DeathListVe: Counts the heartbeats this system has run, so a presentation reader that runs every frame (`DeathExplosionCaptureSystem`) takes each batch of `DeathEntitiesThisFrame` once. Written only here; no simulation system reads it.
FFSystems.Combat.DefensePlatformDefenseS: Whether a parked, platform-owned ship is close enough to be sent at an enemy.
FFSystems.Combat.DefensePlatformKnnRange: Restores the defense-platform KNN query range from saved authoritative state before the heartbeat's KNN refresh. `KnnEnemyVision` is a derived cache and is intentionally not saved, while `ConfiguredRange.AttackRange` is saved.
FFSystems.Combat.DeterministicCombatVisi: The C3 vision producer: the ONLY writer of `C3KnnFleetVision` and `C3KnnEnemyVision`.
Generic per vision type so each instantiation declares write access to exactly its own component — the `KnnSystem.AssignVisionJob` shape, for the same reason.
The other family's static half. A holder published there resolves its ORIGIN and nothing more: it is not a provider of the family being queried, so it gets no self record.
The static half of the family this job answers — the one that can earn a self record.

The per-family resolution tally, summed across threads. `NativeDisableParallelForRestriction` because every write is an atomic ADD into a four-int window this job owns — the restriction exists to stop two workers writing the same INDEX with plain stores, which is not what happens here, and the value is a sum, so the order the adds land in cannot reach it.
Clears every record of one family and stamps why (the whole-graph fault path).

The rollback gate re-evaluated on EVERY resume, not just at world creation. `OnCreate` runs once per World, so its verdict was silently overridden by anything that enabled this system afterwards — `SystemManager`'s blanket `"FFSystems."` substring pass being the one that actually happened in production.
Copies the pass's resolution tally into the `C3VisionProducerReport` singleton and zeroes it for the next pass.
FFSystems.Combat.DeterministicEntityPosi: Deterministic position source for fixed-group combat/AI reads of an arbitrary entity. A player's `LocalTransform`/`LocalToWorld` is PRESENTATION: predicted per-frame on its own peer (`LocalPlayerMotionSystem`) and projected on remote peers (`RemotePlayerLinearMotionPresentationSystem`), so it differs across peers by construction.

The entity's position for simulation decisions: `Player.SimulationPosition` for players, `LocalToWorld.Position` otherwise. The caller must have verified the entity has `LocalToWorld` (the existing has-checks in every call site).

The simulation position behind a physics hit: the hit collider is mapped to its `ColliderParent` when it has one, a player resolves to `Player.SimulationPosition` (its collider sits at a per-peer presentation pose), anything else is derived by `EntityWorldPose`. The caller must have checked the hit entity has a pose.
`Resolve` for consumers that hold a `LocalTransform` lookup instead of `LocalToWorld` — same contract, same player substitution.

True when a physics hit resolves (through `ColliderParent`) to a player entity. Player colliders sit at per-peer presentation positions, so a fixed-group raycast consumer must never let a player-collider hit influence simulation state — skip it.
FFSystems.Combat.DeterministicRailPositi: The C3 half of `DeterministicEntityPosition`, split into its own file so that neither half has to carry the other's permit.

The fail-closed replacement for the T044j `ResolveRail` helper, which fell through to `LocalToWorld` for anything without a rail and so made a presentation transform an input to a simulation decision for the whole railless population.
The entity's authoritative heartbeat-boundary `fp3` pose, or false. False means "no CURRENT rail sample", never a guess.
FFSystems.Combat.DeterministicSpatialSna: The shared gather/acquire logic behind `DeterministicSpatialSnapshotMap`. One implementation, two callers: `DeterministicSpatialSnapshotSystem` calls `PublishForHeartbeat` once per heartbeat and owns the published singleton. A C3 consumer calls `Acquire`, which returns that published snapshot.

The heartbeat snapshot for a consumer. `ownedByCaller` is true when no producer published one and this call gathered a private copy: the caller must dispose it (after its jobs complete) and must not retain it past its own update.
Descriptive provider category. It is deliberately NOT part of the lookup key (`DeterministicSpatialSnapshotMap.CanonicalLookupKey`).
Gathers this heartbeat's snapshot and publishes it as the singleton, disposing the previous heartbeat's map. Consumers hold the returned struct only for the duration of their own update.

Gathers the ONE start-of-heartbeat `DeterministicSpatialSnapshotMap` every C3 consumer resolves against (data-model.md §5, contracts/simulation-and-vision.md "gather named fixed-point providers from heartbeat-H rails").
FFSystems.Combat.ExecuteShipSpawnCommand: Applies every pending spawn command in a peer-stable order.
FFSystems.Combat.IncomingHealthChangeSys: How long the attack (and death) HUD alert stays up after the last hit, counted down by FFSystems.Indicators.AttackWarningSystem. Long, because this system only refreshes the warning when damage actually lands -- a defended attack should stay flagged for a beat rather than blinking out between volleys.

the damage sources an enemy's weapons produce (shots, their splash and impact AoE, beams, turret lasers). Only enemies can aim these at a player ship -- a player's weapons pick targets from enemy vision -- so on a `Player` they are enemy damage. Environment and self damage (comets, black holes, heat, self-destruct, other) is left alone.
FFSystems.Combat.NewShootingSystem: Fires weapons at whatever `Targeter` already names, and spawns the projectiles. ⚠️ **This system does NOT read KNN vision** — a recurring misreading worth stating once. Targeting input is `Targeter` (`Execute`'s `in Targeter target`); the only `KnnFleetVision`/`KnnEnemyVision` references in this file are WRITES that seed a newly created projectile's own vision component.
FFSystems.Combat.NewShootingSystem.Creat: Spawns one projectile from a prefab and stamps every birth-time component on it. Returns the spawned (command-buffer) entity so a caller can override a prefab-derived value the shared path cannot know about — 055 T017's ordered Plasma birth scopes KNN vision from the ABILITY radius rather than the weapon's `SizeFp`. The AI/normal callers ignore it.
FFSystems.Combat.NewShootingSystem.Playe: where an enemy aims a straight shot at a moving player: the weapon's `WeaponConfig.PlayerLeadFraction` of a first-order intercept of the player's replicated `SimulationPosition` / `SimulationVelocity`, solved in fp (`InterceptAim`). Shared by this system and `OldShootingSystem`.
FFSystems.Combat.PlayerCraftedShipDeploy: Sim-side deploy loop for PLAYER-crafted ships.
