FFSystems.Fleet.FleetCommanderSystem: Publishes each fleet commander's position and velocity into `FleetCommander`, which `FleetIdleSystem` and `FleetIdleStationSystem` read on the heartbeat to steer every ship in that commander's formation.
FFSystems.Fleet.FleetCommanderSystem.Der: A player commander's velocity: the heartbeat delta of its replicated simulation position (see the type summary). It is the player's real velocity, a station's included when the player rides one (`Player.SimulationVelocity` is the ship's own input velocity, about zero while riding), so the formation can keep up at any speed.
FFSystems.Fleet.FleetCommanderSystem.Pla: Past this many times its `BaseMoveSpeed` (and past `StationShipCarrySystem.StructureMaxSpeed`, for a player riding a station) a player's step in one heartbeat is a jump, not motion. The afterburner flies at 4x (`AfterburnerConfig.asset` Speed).

How many times the jump speed (`PlayerJumpSpeedFactor`) a step may read and still be fast motion sampled unevenly, not a jump. A client's simulation position is the latest report the host holds when it builds the heartbeat, so the time it was taken wanders around the heartbeat's due time by both peers' frame times and the network's jitter, and the host's own player reads the same way while it ride…
FFSystems.Fleet.OrphanedShipSystem: Holds an orphaned ship still, ages it toward self-destruction and, on a throttled roll, asks `ExecuteShipSpawnCommandSystem` to re-home it.
FFSystems.Fleet.PlayerEntityProximitySys: What each player stands near, recomputed on the final grid calculation step of every cycle.
FFSystems.Fleet.StationShipCarryArmSyste: Arms `StationShipCarrySystem` for the heartbeat the fixed late group is running: that system has to run after the late command buffer, where it cannot be in a fixed group itself.
FFSystems.Fleet.StationShipCarrySystem: Carries the ships parked at a structure with the structure: a Defense Platform's Bats while its station flies. Once per heartbeat, after every station mover has run, each parked ship is moved by the step its platform took in that heartbeat, so a ship at its slot is still at its slot.
FFSystems.Fleet.StationShipCarrySystem.A: Set by `StationShipCarryArmSystem` in a frame the fixed late group ran in; taken down here.
FFSystems.Fleet.StationShipCarrySystem.S: The fastest a structure is taken to move, u/s (25 u in a heartbeat; a fuelled station flies at 74 to 82 u/s, and a platform far from the pivot of a turning one somewhat faster). A larger change of position is a load, a join or a landing snapped onto its tile, not motion.

The step a structure took: from where it was (`lastPosition`) to where it is, on the ground plane. Height is left out: a station that lifts off or lands does not push its ships up or down, they fly at one height. Nothing for a change of position faster than `StructureMaxSpeed`.
FFSystems.Heat.HeatWarningAlertSystem: Raises the HUD overheat alert (the heat indicator on UI.FactoryDamageWarnings.AttackWarningPanel) as soon as a structure crosses the overheating warning threshold, rather than only once it is already taking heat damage.
FFSystems.Heat.HeatWarningAlertSystem.Ov: How long the overheat HUD alert stays up after its last refresh, counted down by FFSystems.Indicators.AttackWarningSystem. Much shorter than IncomingHealthChangeSystem.AttackLingerSeconds because this system re-stamps it every heartbeat the structure is still too hot, so it is only ever the delay between the structure cooling and the HUD going quiet.
FFSystems.Heat.MassDriverHeatSystem: Loaded, aimed drivers heat while working. A denied charge tick produces no heat and follows the existing idle cooling path; power-limited rearm keeps its existing behavior.
FFSystems.Heat.OverheatingStateInitializ: Establishes the overheating-glow invariant for every heat producer: the glow mesh is parked out of sight, and the structure carries an `OverheatingState` that says so.
FFSystems.Indicators.ActiveItemDisplaySy: The icon's pose under its structure: `ActiveItemDisplay.YOffset` above it, and turned so it faces the camera's way whatever way the structure faces.
FFSystems.Indicators.AttackWarningSystem: Expires every HUD warning, whatever raised it. The linger is NOT one shared constant: each producer stamps `AttackWarningData.TimeLeft` with its own value when it raises or refreshes the alert (FFSystems.Combat.IncomingHealthChangeSystem.AttackLingerSeconds, FFSystems.Heat.HeatWarningAlertSystem.OverheatLingerSeconds), and this only counts it down.
FFSystems.Inserters.InserterHelper.GetFi: Obtains the fixed position for a single tile. This is simply relative to the full range of an inserter and a tile and doesn't consider other attributes (like inserter size). This is the position to the closest edge of the given tile from the provided start tile.
FFSystems.Inserters.InserterHelper.GetLo: The smallest limit that may be STORED on this unit. For an arm it is `GetMinimumRangeLimit`, as before. A barge's stored limit is not raised by where it happens to be when the player sets it: a barge out at its far dock would otherwise keep a long route for good, which reads as "I set the limit lower and it did not take".
FFSystems.Inserters.InserterHelper.GetMa: The largest limit that means anything on this unit, and the value stored as 0 ("no limit"). An arm's limit is tiles each way from its origin, so its configured reach; a barge's is the length of its whole route from the fixed start tile, so twice that.
FFSystems.Inserters.InserterHelper.GetMi: The smallest range limit that may be set on this unit right now. The endpoint search walks outward from the unit's CURRENT tile until it lands exactly on the range edge tile, so an edge tile behind the unit is never reached: the walk would run to its iteration bound and log a "position is really messed up" warning every frame.
FFSystems.Inserters.InserterHelper.GetPo: Returns the position to right before the edge of the provided tile, considering the direction of the inserter, the full range of the inserter, and the bottom left offset of tile alignment (a 0 position puts it at the bottom or left of a tile)

Returns the position for the center of the grid tile associated with this inserter. The position is: 1) Always based on the center of the inserter 2) Adjusted by half because the inserter is positioned in the middle of the tile when originally placed First, we calculate the position based on the center of the inserter by calculating how many tiles the center of the inserter is away from the full r…
FFSystems.Inserters.InserterHelper.GetRa: How much bigger a stored range limit is than the number worth showing the player, for this unit. The stored limit is measured from the unit's origin CENTRE tile, but the endpoint search starts at its lower-left tile -- half a body-length behind the centre -- so half the stored limit is spent covering the unit's own hull before the search sees anything.

The tiles a range limit bakes into FullRangeStartTile/FullRangeEndTile, for every kind of unit. An arm's are symmetric about its origin, as they always were. A barge's start is the full-reach start whatever the limit, and the limit is how far its route runs forward from there, so each step of the limit moves only the far end and moves it by one tile.
FFSystems.Inserters.InserterHelper.GetSt: How far ahead of its body a unit's origin (Placeable.OriginalTile) must sit for its route to start `StartAnchoredTilesBehindRear` tiles behind its rear and run its full length forward, instead of reaching `reach` each way from where it was placed.
FFSystems.Inserters.InserterHelper.GetTi: Obtains the tile of the center of the inserter based on the given position. Does not need the length or width of the inserter because this is the center, and the position is based on the center.
FFSystems.Inserters.InserterHelper.IsFro: Whether this unit's range limit trims only the FRONT of its route. True for cargo barges, the units placed with their route starting behind them (PlayerDataController takes exactly these into the hand through BlueprintTool.AnchorHeldUnitRouteBehindIt). Inserter arms sit between the two buildings they serve, so their limit keeps shrinking both ends alike.
FFSystems.Inserters.InserterHelper.SetGh: The same positioning data for a blueprint PREVIEW ghost, which has no placement to derive an OriginalTile from yet: its own tile is the best answer, and BlueprintPlacementSystem overwrites both the moment the player's cursor moves the ghost.
FFSystems.Inserters.InserterHelper.SetRa: Applies a player-chosen range limit: clamps it into what this unit can actually accept, stores it, re-bakes the range tiles from it, and rebases Position so the unit does not move. Everything downstream reads the tiles, so this is the only write path the limit needs.
FFSystems.Inserters.InserterHelper.Settl: Brings a barge's route end to its stored limit as far as the barge allows: never behind one tile past its nose (the endpoint walk must land on the end tile ahead of it, see GetMinimumRangeLimit), and never further out than it already is.
FFSystems.Inserters.InserterHelper.Start: How many tiles behind its rear a freshly placed cargo barge's route starts. The start tile is where the pickup dock is looked for, so the building a barge loads from may stand right behind it or with a one-tile gap; either way the barge flies back and parks against it.
FFSystems.Inserters.InserterPickupSystem: A cargo barge (any tier) that has been docked at its pickup this long departs with whatever it carries, even if it isn't full. An empty barge keeps waiting: it would only turn straight back (InserterMovementSystem reverses an empty unit toward its pickup). So does a barge with no destination, for the same reason: it stays docked with its cargo until it has somewhere to deliver it.
Decides whether an inserter/cargo barge docked against `placeable` may transfer items. The rule is direction-agnostic: anything a unit may load from, it may also unload into.

057 US4: how many load/unload transfers one unit may make in this heartbeat. A transfer shorter than a heartbeat (an Express arm's 20 ms, a barge's 5-10 ms unload) used to run once per heartbeat, 16/s at 16 UPS instead of the configured 50/s. The cap is the 60-per-second ceiling single-player had at 60 UPS, paid out by the heartbeat counter: exactly 1 at 60 UPS, 3 or 4 at 16.
FFSystems.Inserters.LogisticsBayOutputPo: Decides which logistics bay output ports (`LogisticsBayOutputPort`) take overflow. Each heartbeat it finds every bay that is the pickup (start) endpoint of a cargo barge, records those barges' filters in `BargeSources` and marks those ports enabled for the bay's panel.

One filter per cargo barge whose pickup end is a bay, keyed by the bay's inventory entity (after resolving a ProxyInventoryReference, which is where the port lives). A bay with no entry takes no overflow.
FFSystems.Inventory.NetworkedInventoryCa: Applies the heartbeat's queued container changes to `NetworkedItemsCache`, which the construction-bot assigner reads: simulation state, so it runs on the heartbeat. Only fixed systems fill the queue, so in `FFControllerLateGroup` it already did work only on heartbeat frames; the move makes that a guarantee instead of a coincidence.
FFSystems.Knn.DebugKnnDisablerDisplaySys: Shows a debug indicator over the entity when a Knn is disabled. Currently does not work.
FFSystems.Knn.EntityWorldPose: The `ComponentLookup`-shaped sibling of `KnnChunkPoses`: the world position of one entity, derived the way the transform pass would compose it, for a heartbeat system that runs BEFORE that pass in the frame.
FFSystems.Knn.EntityWorldPose.HasCompone: Whether the entity has a world pose at all — the same probe the replaced `LocalToWorld` checks made.
FFSystems.Knn.EntityWorldPose.Position(1: World-space position; the caller must have checked `HasComponent`.
FFSystems.Knn.FriendlyKnnDisablerSystem: Puts idle fleet ships to sleep (out of KNN) when no enabled enemy is within a chunk, and wakes them when one comes near.
FFSystems.Knn.KnnChunkPoseHandles: The five chunk handles `KnnChunkPoses.Read` needs, as ONE field: create in `OnCreate`, `Update` every `OnUpdate` (or re-`Create` per schedule, as `KnnSystem` does), then `Read` per chunk. Keeps the plumbing — and the change-version rule that goes with a derived pose, `DidChange` — in one place instead of one copy per consumer.
FFSystems.Knn.KnnChunkPoseHandles.DidCha: Whether anything the derived pose is built from changed since `sinceVersion`. A consumer that re-reads only changed chunks must ask THIS, not `LocalToWorld`'s version alone: `LocalToWorld`'s version only moves when the per-frame pass runs, which is a frame-count question — the very dependence the derived pose removes.
FFSystems.Knn.KnnChunkPoses: The one place the legacy KNN path decides WHERE an entity is — for the tree's sources and for the vision holders it answers queries for.
FFSystems.Knn.KnnChunkPoses.ComposedPosi: THE ONE COPY of the pass's rule for an entity that carries a `PostTransformMatrix`: the post matrix may carry a translation, so the composed position is NOT the LocalTransform's. Shared with `EntityWorldPose` so the two reader shapes cannot drift; `EntityWorldPoseTest` and `HeartbeatTransformComposeSystemTest` pin it bit-exact against what the pass writes.
FFSystems.Knn.KnnChunkPoses.Read(6): Binds one chunk. The three `chunk.Has` probes are type-index checks against the ARCHETYPE, so a population carrying none of the optional components costs a handful of integer comparisons per chunk and no per-entity work — the same argument `KnnSystem.GatherSourcesJob`'s identity handles already rely on. The returned arrays are chunk views: owned by the chunk, never disposed here.
FFSystems.Knn.KnnSystem: Builds the two KD-trees (fleet, enemy) and refreshes every vision holder's 8-nearest-within-range neighbor list. CADENCE IS A PROPERTY OF THE GROUP: `FFFixedEarlyGroup` is heartbeat-cadenced by `FinalFactorySimulationRateManager`, so this system runs exactly once per simulation advance and not at all on a frame without one — the same mechanism every other fixed system gets from its group.
FFSystems.Knn.KnnSystem.KnnSourceEntry: One gathered source: its cross-peer ordering key plus the two values the tree and the assign job actually consume. Sorted as a unit so the point array and the entity array are permuted together and `AssignVisionJob`'s index-into-Points/Entities mapping stays exact.
FFSystems.Knn.KnnSystem.OnStartRunning(0: The rollback gate re-evaluated on EVERY resume, not just at world creation. `OnCreate` runs once per World, so its verdict was silently overridden by anything that enabled this system later — `SystemManager`'s blanket `"FFSystems."` substring pass being the one that actually happened. Unity calls this whenever a stopped system resumes, which is exactly the moment the verdict has to hold again.
FFSystems.Knn.KnnSystem.TryGetBuildWitne: The ACTUAL retained build input of the last refresh — not an `EntityManager` re-query.
FFSystems.Knn.LegacyKnnLoadPathWarmup: Gives the LEGACY KNN index the same inputs on every route before the first fixed pass after a world apply. Sibling of `CombatLoadPathProvisioning` (R22b) and called from the same place for the same reason; kept in its own file because that one owns the C3 surface and this one owns the legacy float path, and the two families have exactly one writer each.
FFSystems.Knn.LegacyKnnLoadPathWarmup.Ru: Places every simulation object and projects it into world space, with a census either side so "what the index would have seen" is a read in the audit stream rather than an inference from a downstream fingerprint. Idempotent: a second call recomputes the same values.
FFSystems.Knn.LegacyVisionShimSystem: The float boundary shim: it fills the UNCHANGED legacy vision components from the shared deterministic index, so that comets, targeting, defense firing, projectile collision, AOE/splash, aggro, black holes and the mouse/debug selectors keep the exact component family and semantics they have today while the KD-tree stops running.
FFSystems.Knn.LegacyVisionShimSystem.Ass: Generic per vision type so each instantiation declares write access to exactly its own component (the `KnnSystem.AssignVisionJob` shape).
FFSystems.Knn.LegacyVisionShimSystem.Cle: Clears one family's buffers — the shim's equivalent of `KnnSystem`'s empty path.
FFSystems.Knn.LegacyVisionShimSystem.OnS: The rollback gate re-evaluated on EVERY resume, not just at world creation. `OnCreate` runs once per World, so its verdict was silently overridden by anything that enabled this system afterwards — `SystemManager`'s blanket `"FFSystems."` substring pass being the one that actually happened in production.
FFSystems.LifecycleManagement.DeletionSy: This system runs as part of the Cleanup Group, and it runs on every frame. It deletes any and all entities marked for deletion on that frame.
FFSystems.LifecycleManagement.StarPlacem: Gives a new star its saved `StarSlot` buffer and Dyson rotator, which the Dyson placement systems read: simulation state, so it runs on the heartbeat. Stars come from the fixed map generator or a load, so in `FFControllerLateGroup` it already worked only on heartbeat frames or at load; the move makes that a guarantee. OrderLast is where it ran on a heartbeat frame before.
FFSystems.LogiNetwork.NetworkItemsRecalc: Recounts `NetworkedItemsCache.ItemCountCache` (the per-item totals) when the cache is flagged. simulation reads those totals (`ConstructionTaskAssignerSystem`, supply bots), so the recount runs at the start of each heartbeat's fixed step, not every frame: an op that changes the cache at apply (`InventoryTransferNetworkOperation`) and the next heartbeat applied in one frame used to leave that heart…
FFSystems.Logistics.LogisticsNetworkCons: This system is responsible for processing all the structure that consume logistics units from the network and sets up transfer commands to pull the ships from the network. This ONLY happens for ships that are in the logistics network staging areas, like the Ship Yards.
FFSystems.Logistics.ResearchBotPhysicalM: Fixed-point physical flight; research progress is advanced by its existing owner.
The rail length for a research leg from `origin` to `endpoint`: how far the rail must advance, at config speed, before the bot arrives.
Travel along the route the rail is already measuring.
FFSystems.Logistics.TerrainExtractorArro: Owns whether a MINING STATION's route arrow is on screen. The rule, in one place: visible while the player is holding the placement preview, visible while the mouse is hovering the placed station, hidden otherwise.
FFSystems.Logistics.TerrainExtractorBeam: Physics may refine the visible beam end, never the research flight pose.
FFSystems.Loot.LootBoxChunkSpawningSyste: System that spawns loot boxes in inactive chunks when SpawnLootboxes is enabled.
FFSystems.Loot.LootDropHelper.TrySelectL: Selects from one biome's authored cumulative-weight table. Multi-hash-map bucket order is an allocation/container detail and changes across save/load/join, so values are gathered by their stable biome key and restored to cumulative-weight order before rolling. Item id is a deterministic tie-break only; positive authored weights make cumulative thresholds unique.
FFSystems.Map.EntityGridPersistenceSyste: Carries the world's tile-occupancy grid (`FFGrid.EntityMap`: tile → occupant) through every save and every multiplayer join / desync-recovery snapshot, so a loaded world holds the SAVING peer's grid rather than a re-derivation of it.

Pure: the grid's blocks, sorted by occupant; identical grids give identical blocks. The grouping runs in a Burst job: the managed version (a list of tiles per occupant) was ~80-100 ms of every autosave's main-thread stall on a 230k-tile world.
Payload v1: count:int32 of blocks, each Index:int32 Version:int32 Min:int3 Max:int3 bitsLength:int32 bits:byte[bitsLength]. A -1 count is the null (not carried) payload.
One bit per box tile, index = ((x-Min.x)*ny + (y-Min.y))*nz + (z-Min.z), LSB first.

Pure: replaces `grid` with the saved blocks, remapping every occupant through `entityMap` (saved entity → this world's entity). A block whose occupant the load did not recreate is dropped whole and counted.
Null = not carried (a payload that predates this system); empty = an empty grid.
FFSystems.Map.GasGiantSwap: biome generation picks one in three of the Terra Worlds it scatters to become Gas Giants. Only `WorldObjectGeneratorJob` applies it; the Terra World every new game places near the start (`MapGeneratorSystem.GenerateStartArea`) never goes through it and stays a Terra World.
FFSystems.Map.GasGiantSwap.Apply(3): The item biome generation actually places for `itemId` at `cell`.
FFSystems.Map.GasGiantSwap.IsActive: False when either item, or the gas giant's world-object config, is not loaded (test fixtures, mods).
FFSystems.Map.GasGiantSwap.OneIn: One Terra World in this many becomes a Gas Giant.
FFSystems.Map.GasGiantSwap.Swaps(2): Whether a Terra World generated at `cell` becomes a Gas Giant.
FFSystems.Map.MapGeneratorSystem: This system is responsible for generating the start area of the map and placing? original things (oracle, planet, etc). Once the start area is generated, then MapGeneratorSystemV2 takes over and handles future chunk generation. MapGeneratorSystem is a managed system that keeps track of the map generation data singleton, the stuff that needs to be saved from the map generation data singleton.
FFSystems.Map.MapGeneratorSystem.Current: v2 appends `MapGeneratorSystemData.WorldObjectTiles`: the occupied-tile set the world-object generator produced on the peer that SAVED. `GenerateMapFromSaveFile` regenerates it on every load from the loading world's entity grid, so a joining client (whose grid is not yet the host's) derived a different set — and `EnemyCampBuilderSystem` then grew camps where the host was blocked.
FFSystems.Map.MapGeneratorSystem.FirstEn: Where the tutorial's Urso camp spawns: on the diagonal between two of GenerateStartArea's start squares, just outside the three starting asteroids.
FFSystems.Map.MapGeneratorSystem.LegacyF: The tutorial camp's spot before 2026-10-07, where a save made during the camp step still has it.
FFSystems.Map.MapGeneratorSystem.MapGene: v2+; null when the payload predates it (see `CurrentVersion`).
FFSystems.Map.MapGeneratorSystemV2: This system is responsible for assigning biomes and generating chunks as the player explores the map.
FFSystems.Map.MapGeneratorSystemV2.Resol: Camp-prefab lookup shared by the runtime and new-game generation paths.
FFSystems.Map.MapGeneratorSystemV2.TryRe: Resolves a MapExplorer carrier to its deterministic chunk anchor. Players use their fp simulation position, placeables (Exploration Center) their grid tile, and fleet ships (explorer bots) their owner's anchor — a bot's own transform is float formation flight and must not trigger generation.
FFSystems.Map.MapItemGridding: 062 R14: map-generated structures are gridded AT CREATION, on every peer.
FFSystems.Map.MapItemGridding.ForPrefab(: The single-prefab, main-thread form: resolves the gridding decision eagerly with `EntityManager.HasComponent` and yields a struct whose mailbox is live only when the prefab really is a gridded structure.
FFSystems.Map.MapItemGridding.MailboxMis: Burst-safe drop record, length 1: how many Adds this generation pass refused to queue because `Mailbox` carried no `StationGridUpdateCommand` buffer. A `Debug.LogError` cannot be raised from inside the Burst-compiled job, so the count travels out on the job and the scheduling system logs it once per pass — never a silent drop.
FFSystems.Map.MapItemGridding.Mailboxes: The mailbox existence check. `EntityCommandBuffer.AppendToBuffer` verifies at PLAYBACK that the target carries the buffer and throws `InvalidOperationException: Buffer does not exist on entity … cannot append element` from inside the buffer system when it does not — which destroys the whole frame's command buffer, not just this one command, so an entire generated chunk is lost.
FFSystems.Map.MapItemGridding.PrefabDeci: Set when the caller already answered "is this prefab gridded?" itself and the lookups are absent. `ComponentLookup` can only be obtained from a system (SystemAPI / SystemState) — `EntityManager` has no `GetComponentLookup` — so the main-thread callers that place exactly ONE known prefab go through `ForPrefab` instead. Both routes evaluate the same `StationGridAdmission.IsGridWorthy` rule.
FFSystems.Map.TutorialCampSpot: Where the tutorial's Urso camp goes. `MapGeneratorSystem.FirstEnemySpawnerPos` is the first choice, but by the camp step a player may have built there (or anything else may stand there), so the camp takes the first spot whose footprint and a `Clearance`-tile margin are empty at every grid height and hold no world object.
FFSystems.Map.TutorialCampSpot.CampFootp: The camp's footprint in tiles (StingerSpawner, 3x3), for callers that have no prefab to ask.
FFSystems.Map.TutorialCampSpot.Candidate: World x/z of every spot, in the order they are tried.
FFSystems.Map.TutorialCampSpot.Clearance: Empty tiles kept around the camp's footprint, so it is not jammed against whatever is beside it.
FFSystems.Map.TutorialCampSpot.Find(5): `preferred` if a `width` x `length` camp fits there, else the first of `Candidates` that is clear, at `preferred`'s height. When none is clear the camp goes to `preferred` anyway: the step must still have a camp to destroy. An uncreated map (a test world without the grid) counts as empty.
FFSystems.Map.TutorialCampSpot.IsCampSpo: Whether a spawner at `position` is the tutorial camp: it stands on one of its spots.
FFSystems.Map.TutorialCampSpot.IsClear(5: Whether a camp centred on `centreTile` and its margin touch nothing: no entity at any grid height, no world object.
FFSystems.Map.WorldObjectGeneratorJob: This is the job that's called by MapGeneratorSystemV2 to generate the world objects.
FFSystems.Map.WorldObjectGeneratorJob.Gr: 062 R14: queues the station-grid Add for every gridded structure this job spawns.
FFSystems.Map.WorldObjectGeneratorJob.Pl: which generated Terra Worlds become Gas Giants.
FFSystems.Map.WorldObjectGeneratorJob.Re: Draws the placement rotation. This is the ONLY thing the spawning half of a placement takes from the shared biome `rng`, so it is exposed separately from `PlaceMapItem`: the generator has to advance the stream identically whether or not it is actually spawning entities (see `PlaceWorldObject`). Keep every rng draw in the spawn path here, or the two passes drift apart again.
FFSystems.MassDrivers.MassDriverCyclePha: A mass driver's cycle as its panel shows it: `MassDriverSystem.CyclePhase`.
FFSystems.MassDrivers.MassDriverStatusSy: Rebuilds the en-route map from the restored in-flight `MassDrivenItem` entities. The map mirrors LAUNCHED quantities exactly (incremented at fire, decremented by the launched quantity at delivery/loss), so per-destination sums over the in-flight items are the authoritative truth.
FFSystems.MassDrivers.MassDriverSystem.C: Where a driver is in its cycle, as the panels show it (presentation only), and how far through that phase it is: Rearming while the timer climbs to the rearm time, then Charging, which reads 0% while the driver waits for or pays its launch pulse and then follows the load, then ReadyToFire. `hasBurst` is false for a driver with no launch pulse, whose load needs no payment.
FFSystems.MassDrivers.MassDriverSystem.I: THE deterministic mass-driver range predicate — shared by the fire gate and `MassDriverAnimationSystem`'s laser in-range indicator so simulation and visual can never disagree. Exact squared comparison of tile-derived integer world centers: no float transforms, no sqrt. Fires iff distance <= NetworkRadius (a target exactly at the radius is in range).
FFSystems.MassDrivers.MassDriverSystem.L: The launch chamber is the first slot of the Primary inventory range (which always starts at slot 0); the Secondary range is the landing pad for received cargo.
Where a charged driver's timer fires: the load time less the pulse, never less than the rearm. The timer rearms to the rearm time, holds there while the pulse is paid, then loads to this.
FFSystems.MassDrivers.MassDriverSystem.W: Deterministic world-unit distance for an in-range launch. The even-shift rescale keeps the fp sqrt input inside fp's integer range for arbitrarily large radii (unreachable with shipped configs, whose distances always fit directly).
FFSystems.Mining.AsteroidLowOreWarningSy: Drives the asteroid crack glow and the "low on resources" warning: the orange world marker (a LowOreWarningEntity parented through the asteroid's LinkedEntityGroup) and the HUD alert, which UI.FactoryDamageWarnings.AttackWarningPanel counts off the asteroid's `AttackWarningData` with `Source.AsteroidLow`.
FFSystems.Mining.AsteroidPlacementSystem: The single source of the OrePatchType → ore-item mapping. The Burst placement job below consumes it through the indices cached in `PostConfigLoadHook`; test tooling pinning an asteroid's ore (`ffauto:terrain.place`) calls it directly so the two paths cannot drift when a patch type is added.
FFSystems.Mining.ScalableLaserSystem.Hid: Disables a laser's beam and impact effects and rewinds the impact's scale-in, so the next time the laser turns on it grows from the start again.
FFSystems.Mining.TerrainOreOverrideSyste: Applies a test-scenario `TerrainOreOverride` once the instantiation pipeline is done with the asteroid: `AsteroidPlacementSystem` re-rolls `OreRemaining` while `InstantiationUpdaterMarker` is present, so this waits for the marker to be consumed instead of racing that system with cross-group ordering.
FFSystems.MobileStations.CorelessStation: A station without a Command Core keeps none of the core's settings. The core's panel is the only place that sets them, so a station whose core was destroyed or deconstructed could never undo them: "Stay Separate" in particular kept it from merging with anything, for good.
FFSystems.MobileStations.HaulerKey: The three ints a network op, a drive snapshot or a panel-rotate report names a mobile station by.
FFSystems.MobileStations.HaulerKey.IdKey: The y of an id key. Grid heights are single digits and `TileKeyedTargets.FlyingKeyOffsetY` (1 << 20) plus a height stays below this.
FFSystems.MobileStations.HaulerKey.TryGe: The key to send for `hauler`: its id if it has one, else its reference structure's tile. False for a hauler with no placeable reference structure, which no sender addressed before either.
FFSystems.MobileStations.HaulerKey.TryRe: Resolves an id key to its hauler: exactly one live hauler carries the id, or nothing resolves, on every peer alike (ids are saved simulation state). Out-of-play haulers are skipped, as the tile scans skip them.
FFSystems.MobileStations.HaulerReference: This runs whenever any placeable gets deleted (which can be a mobile station)--so everything except inserters When you have a station and delete something from it, it needs to figure out what was deleted so it can tell the other system to recalculate the haulers.
Rebuilds the hauler of any station whose structures point at a hauler that no longer exists.
FFSystems.MobileStations.MobileStationGh: The unbuilt ghosts a mobile station takes with it when it flies.
Everything on the map edge to edge with `placeable`, at every height it occupies (an empty tile adds nothing; an entity may appear more than once).

Claims the riders' landing tiles in the map, as the buildings' are claimed for the descent. Adding a tile a rider already holds is a no-op, so the descent re-claims every heartbeat (a save taken mid-descent loads without the claim: flying placeables are not put on the map).
The ghosts that ride with a station lifting off, by the rule in the class header, sorted by tile. Call it before the station's buildings leave the map: it walks the map from them.

Whether every tile of every rider's `landing` placeable is empty or the rider's own: the riders' half of the landing claim (`MobileStationUtils.TryClaimLandingZone` is the buildings'). A landing that has no room for a rider waits in the air, as one with no room for a building does.
An unbuilt ghost on the map that may ride: placed and confirmed, not deleted, not riding already.
The riders of the station whose Command Core is `core`, from `allRiders` (sorted by tile, so these are too).

Where a rider is while its station flies: its tile's place against the Command Core's tile, carried wherever the core is and turned as far as the core is turned from its tile's facing. While the core is not turned the rider is moved by exactly the core's step (no rotation is applied at all), so a station flying straight carries it exactly.
Riders in tile order (x, z, y, then height position): the order every peer commits them in.
FFSystems.MobileStations.MobileStationPr: Turns heartbeat-to-heartbeat presentation interpolation on and off for every item of a moving station (the `WorldEntityPresentationInterpolation` pipeline), so a station that moves only on the 16/s simulation heartbeat is drawn gliding between them instead of stepping.
Disables interpolation on every grid item that has it enabled.
Enables interpolation on every grid item that does not already have it, seeding the snapshot with the item's current pose so the first blend starts where it is drawn now.
True once `entity`'s captured pair has stopped moving, i.e. the drawn pose has reached the simulation pose, so switching interpolation off no longer shows as a jump.
True when `entity` is currently being interpolated.
FFSystems.MobileStations.MobileStationUt: A temporary stop is deleted the moment the station reaches it, and only one may exist at a time (see HaulerCommandOperations.AddStopNoWait), so there is nothing worth copying about one.

Re-claims the landing footprint from the current placeable data of the station grid items. Adding tiles the station already owns is a no-op, so this is safe to run every descent frame. It exists to restore the claim after a save/load mid-descent: flying placeables are skipped when the entity map is rebuilt on load, so the claim made at descent start would otherwise be lost.
One heartbeat of hand driving: every grid item is turned by `turnRadians` about `pivot` (the reference structure) and moved by `translation`, in ONE write per item.

Whether this hauler's flight state means its grid's `StationGrid.IsStationMoving` is true: in transit and able to move (`CheckICanMove` — a switched-off station in transit stands still and the transit system never asserts the flag), docking, or on the undock lift rail.

`TryGetLandingZoneHeadedFor` for a station that can still get there. Taking the controls of a flying station switches its automation off and leaves its state and its resolved stop as they were (`HaulerCommandOperations.PrepareForDriving`); the transit and queue systems then stand still for it (`CheckICanMove`), so it never arrives and never joins the queue.

Which way a stop lands its station: the Direction its reference structure (the Command Core) takes on touchdown. A scheduled Land stop's `HaulerStop.StopDirection` is its turn from the facing of the zone it picked, Up meaning "as the zone faces", so every zone of a name turns its ships its own way while ships at one zone can still land different ways.

Where one building of a station lands on a landing zone: its placeable with the tile and facing the landing gives it, when the station's reference structure (`reference`, its placeable before the landing) comes down on `zoneTile` facing `stopDirection`.

Presentation-side formation move: advances every grid item's float transform by an exact, already-decided distance. Feature 011: the distance comes from the fp rails advance (`HaulerFlightRails`), so the float transforms are a pure projection of simulation state — nothing simulation-side may read them back.

Presentation-side formation rotation: rotates every grid item by an exact, already-decided angular step about the reference structure's xz origin. Feature 011: the step comes from the fp rotation rail (`HaulerFlightRails.RotationTraveled`), and phase completion is gated there — never on the float angle remainder.

Attempts to claim the landing footprint described by `newPlaceables` (the already-computed landing-position placeables for every station grid item, in buffer order) in the entity map. If any target tile is occupied by an entity outside this station, nothing is claimed and false is returned.

Inserts a copy of the stop at `index` directly after it, so a route that has to pass the same point on the way out and on the way back only needs the point entered once. The copy gets its own `newStopIdentifier`: `StopGotDeletedFromHauler` recognises the stop a station is currently flying to by identifier, so two stops sharing one would make a deleted stop look alive.

The landing zone a station's current stop was resolved to, when that stop is a scheduled Land stop: the zone the station is flying to, waiting at or docked on. False for a coordinate stop, a move-now or land-now, and a stop that was replaced since the pick (`Hauler.CurrentStopEntity` then still names the zone of the old one).
`facing` turned clockwise by `turn` (Up: not at all).
FFSystems.MobileStations.MoveableStructu: Recalculates the Haulers when something changed (due to Hauler Reference Deletion System)
FFSystems.MobileStations.StationGhostRid: Carries the unbuilt ghosts riding a station in flight with its Command Core, once per heartbeat, after every station mover has run.

A ghost riding a station that no longer carries it. The touchdown sets a rider down with its station (`MobileStationDockingSystem`), so this is for a station that ends its flight some other way: Its Command Core is destroyed or deleted (a black hole, a deleted core): the ghost is cancelled, as a ghost whose spot is gone is. It has nowhere to be built.
FFSystems.MobileStations.StationLockOper: The station lock switch, applied by the `SetStationLocked` hauler command on every peer during the heartbeat drain. It reads and writes simulation state only, and nothing it does depends on query order, so every peer ends with the same world.

One above every lineage id in the world, locks and hints alike, so a new lock never shares a lineage with an older station or with a ghost still waiting to be rebuilt. Read from the world, never from a counter kept in memory: a host that has been running and a client that just loaded its snapshot pick the same id.

Locking gives the station a lineage id and changes nothing else: the connections it already has stay (a lock blocks new connections only). Unlocking removes the lock and asks every landed structure of the station for a connections update, so a station unlocked while it sits flush against other buildings connects to them now, as an unlocked station landing there would have.
FFSystems.MobileStations.StationMovement: Finds the rideable structure nearest the local player for the ride-a-vehicle prompt/action. Determinism scope: LOCAL-ONLY presentation — the result feeds `RideableStructureDetector` (UI prompt) and `VehicleRideAction` (the local player's mount), both per-player fleet-lane concerns; no factory-simulation system consumes it, so the physics-hit enumeration is acceptable here.

heal: haulers from saves that predate `HaulerFlightRails` get the component added here, zeroed (`HaulerFlightPhase.None`), on their first heartbeat. The flight state systems treat a None-phase rail as "re-anchor me" and arm it from a one-time float-transform sample.
Gives every hauler that has no `HaulerId` one, on the heartbeat it appears.
The whole assignment, callable on a world's queries from a test.

The order the station state machine walks its stations in, wherever one station's step changes what the next one sees on the same heartbeat: picking a landing zone, joining a zone's queue, claiming landing tiles. Query order is chunk order, which differs between a host that has been running and a peer that loaded its snapshot, so it must never decide those.
Drops landing zone queue entries that are no longer a live station: the entity is gone, is not a hauler, or is marked for deletion.
Lands a building that still flies although its station has landed.

Where each station waiting in a landing zone's queue holds. They used to hold wherever their flight ended, 50 units short of the pad on the line they came in on, so every station coming from the same place waited on the same spot.

How far from its pad position the first station in the queue starts its descent run: the 50 units every landing flight has always ended short of the pad (`MobileStationUndockingSystem`), so the landing itself (`MobileStationDockingSystem`) is unchanged.
Where the first station in the queue starts its landing: `ApproachLength` out from its pad position `padPosition`, on the line from there to where it is, at its own height.
How far past `ApproachLength` a station may be and still start its landing from there.
Whether a station at `position` is close enough to its pad to start landing.
The world centre of a placeable's tiles.
The space between one waiting station and the next, and between the first and the pad, world units.
Decides whether a waiting station may hold at a place, and hears of every place given out.
Whether the station at `index` in the queue may hold with its centre at `centre`.
The station at `index` holds at `centre`, taking `box`.

Gives each waiting station of one zone its place. `footprints` are the queue's stations in queue order; index 0 is the station on or coming down onto the pad and is not given a place. The pad, and that station, take up `padReach`[side] along each side.
How far from the zone's centre one side of the queue may reach, world units.
Speed limits of a station moving up its queue, world units a second.
An axis-aligned box on the ground plane, world units.
The box around a circle.
The box grown by `margin` on every side.
How far the box reaches from `origin` along `along`.
The box's extent along `axis`, measured from `origin`.

A station's buildings as they are drawn while it flies, relative to the centre of its reference structure, in world units: the box of every building's tiles and the largest distance from that centre to a corner of one. A station turned by hand (`HaulerManualHeading`) is drawn turned off its tiles, so it gets the circle of that radius instead (`Circle`).
The box at `centre`.
Adds one building's tiles (lower-left tile, width and length in tiles) seen from `centre`.
How far the footprint reaches along `along`, ahead of the centre (`ahead`) and behind it (`behind`), and the middle of its width across that line.
How far the footprint reaches along `axis` from the centre: back (min) and forward (max).
The footprint turned clockwise (seen from above) by `quarterTurns` about its centre, as a landing turns a station from its placeables' facing onto its pad's.
How far a waiting place moves out when something is in its way, world units (one tile).
The line a side of the queue runs along, out from the zone, and the axis across it, for a zone facing `facing`. Side 0 is behind the zone, 1 its left, 2 its right, 3 in front of it.
The sides a queue fills, in order, as quarter turns from the zone's facing: behind, left, right, in front.

How fast a station moving up its queue goes, `traveled` along a move of which `remaining` is left: it speeds up out of its old place and slows into its new one, never below `MinSpeed` (so it always arrives) nor above `topSpeed`.
How quickly a station moving up its queue speeds up and slows down: speed per unit of distance.
Direction → one-tile step on the ground plane (x, z): Up = +z, Right = +x, Down = -z, Left = -x.

The terrain hazard's scan (`MobileStationQueueSystem`, "put your station somewhere better"): cosmic terrain on the tiles ahead of `placeable`'s facing, about Length×9.5 units out from the tile under `origin`, on grid layer `layer`. A station waiting there is destroyed.
The box of a placeable's tiles.

The station's buildings as drawn in flight, around the centre of its reference structure (placeables only: their tiles keep the layout of the last landing while it flies). False while its station grid cannot be read.

Where a waiting station heads next on its way to `place`, its place on `side`. Straight there, unless that would take it over the pad or another station's place (`taken`: its first `padBoxes` are the pad with the station standing on it or coming down, the rest the other places): then it goes round the line, as a ship joining a queue does.

Pre-sampler convergence that CLEARS a stale `StationGrid.IsStationMoving`. The flag is not saved, and a loading peer derives it (`StationGridPostResetRecalcSystem`) from the haulers' flight state, but live it is only transition-written, and some transitions leave it set: a flying station whose automation is off loses its temporary stop (`HaulerCommandOperations.PutHaulerInUndocking`), then `Mobile…
Returns the index of the given entity in the provided queue, -1 if not present

pre-sampler convergence for the undock lift's `StationGrid.IsStationMoving`. The other three flight phases re-assert the flag from `FFFixedPreTransformGroup` every heartbeat, so a restored peer converges before the determinism fingerprint samples in `FFFixedPostTransformGroup`.

Performs the undocking of stations in the case where the station is being automated. Feature 011: lives in the FIXED late group — undock state (lift progress, grid-membership teardown, stop selection) must advance only on heartbeat ticks; the old controller-group placement integrated the lift at each peer's own frame rate, which made lift-off land on different heartbeats per peer (the measured mod…

One job over every undocking station, in `HaulerId` order. It was an `IJobEntity`, which walks the query in chunk order: that order differs between a long-running host and a peer that loaded its snapshot, and since a stop pick now counts the picks made before it on the same heartbeat (`CountInbound`), the walk order decides who gets which landing zone. The per-station body is unchanged.
FFSystems.Players.LuminaeBankSystem: Persistence for `LuminaeBank`, the crew's total Lumin Orbs collected. The bank is a bare singleton entity, so `MarshallingSystem`'s root-type capture never sees it — it rides the `ISerializableSystem` channel instead, which is also what a joining client receives, so the total arrives with the world transfer.
FFSystems.Players.LuminaeBankSystem.Lega: A v1 payload, read back: the old shared spendable balance.
FFSystems.Players.LuminaeBankSystem.Pend: The shared balance a v1 payload carried, waiting for the players to exist; null when the loaded payload was v2 or absent. Consumed by `TryTakeLegacySharedBalance`.
FFSystems.Players.LuminaeBankSystem.Rese: Zeroes the bank on the world wipe that precedes every load and exit-to-menu (`SaveGameManager.ResetGame` → `FinalFactoryGrid.ResetGameEntitiesAndObjects`). Load-bearing, not hygiene: an older save's payload is not a total (v1) or is missing, so nothing would overwrite the previous session's total, and the migration takes the larger of the bank and what the players hold.
FFSystems.Players.LuminaeBankSystem.TryT: Hands over (once) the shared balance a v1 payload carried.
FFSystems.Players.PlayerColorDefaultSyst: Gives every player without a colour the first palette colour nobody else in the game uses. Simulation: a Fixed-group heartbeat system, because the result is saved state every peer must agree on.

Assigns, in array order, every unassigned entry the lowest palette index that no other entry holds as its `PlayerColor.PaletteIndex` or shows as its `PlayerColor.Rgb` (a custom colour counts even before its own seat is assigned). When every index is taken (more than `PlayerColorPalette.Count` players counting parked ones) it takes the index held by the fewest players, lowest on a tie.
FFSystems.Players.PlayerSimulationObject: Takes a parked player's `PlayerSimulationObject` out of play with its player. That invisible stand-in, not the player root, is what the legacy KNN index, the friendly chunk map and so projectile hits, enemy targeting and unit overlap find the player through, so marking only the root with `OutOfPlay` left a parked ship a KNN neighbour: shot at, hit, pushed against and keeping its chunks awake.
Marks or clears the player's simulation object; a no-op when it has none (test entities).
Every player's simulation object follows its player's `ParkedPlayer`.

Drives each `PlayerSimulationObject` to its player's deterministic `Player.SimulationPosition` every heartbeat. Because the object only moves on the heartbeat — never per rendered frame — the player's KNN participation is heartbeat-quantized and identical across peers, satisfying the simulation-channel read invariant for the KNN path.
FFSystems.Players.PlayerSimulationPositi: Bridges the dependency-free `PlayerSimulationPositionReplication` wire format to ECS player state. Used by the heartbeat system to apply the authoritative per-heartbeat player positions to `Player.SimulationPosition`. See Documentation/Player-Position-Determinism.md.

Single-player / local path. Builds the snapshot from the local player's transform and applies it through the same `ApplyPayload` writer used in multiplayer, so there is exactly one place that writes `Player.SimulationPosition` (no separate sampler system, no single-player vs multiplayer gate). See Documentation/Player-Position-Determinism.md.
Client path. Writes `Player.SimulationPosition` for every player whose GUID appears in the decoded payload.

Where a ship drawn at `drawn`, moving at `velocity`, was `lateSeconds` ago (see `BuildHostSnapshot`). Only the horizontal plane moves; a lateness outside 0..`MaxSampleLateSeconds` (a stall, a clock reset) or a non-finite result leaves the drawn position as it is.

Host path. Produces the encoded payload to broadcast on the heartbeat, without mutating any state. For every player: the host's own player(s) (MePlayer) are sampled from their transform; remote players use their latest reported position, falling back to their current simulation position if none has arrived.
The largest lateness `AtDueTime` corrects: the production accumulator banks at most one interval past the due time, which is 62.5 ms at the slowest rate the game runs (16 UPS).

The owning peer's velocity sample for its own ship: the `LinearMotion` velocity that moves the drawn ship (`LocalPlayerMotionSystem`), crossed into fp at the same sampling boundary as the position. Zero for a ship without one.
FFSystems.Power.MiningStationSignalEmiss: Mining stations only emit signal while they are actively mining. A miner bot carries a `TerrainExtractorStateMarker` for exactly as long as it is locked onto a live asteroid; the marker is stripped the moment the asteroid is gone (depleted) or the bot goes idle.
FFSystems.Power.ResearchStationSignalEmi: Research stations only emit signal while research is actively being consumed -- i.e. a technology is selected (`ResearchState.IsResearching`) and the station has research bots working. Signal scales by the active-bot ratio and power satisfaction, the same factors `ResearchStationPowerSystem` uses for the station's power draw and heat, so signal tracks how hard the station is actually working.
FFSystems.Power.StationGridMembershipSys: Performs logic to assign membership of modules in the map to connected station grids SINGLE THREADED Does a depth-first search to find everything that's connected to each other to determine what placeables all make up a single station grid.
What a grid publishes and where its calculation stands, with the member count behind it.

What one grid shows after taking over the others, worked out from all of them at once: the result is the same whatever order they are listed in. That matters because they are absorbed in the order a search walks the connection buffers, and peers can hold those in different orders.
The lowest member of the grid these numbers were read from, in tile order (then item): replicated state that tells two grids of equal size apart the same way on every peer.

Whether the published sums, and separately the calculation's running sums, were made over the grid's own members rather than taken over from another grid. Only own sums are ever added to another grid's.
FFSystems.Power.StationMoverSignalEmissi: Thrusters are the one structure that is definitionally working while a station is in the air, so they are what makes a moving station audible. While a thruster is firing -- the station is moving, the fuel consumer is on, and it has fuel -- it emits its full rated `PowerConfig.SignalStrength`.
What a thruster emits when it is not firing. Matches the per-structure contribution of a moving station, so a thruster is never quieter than the connector bolted next to it.

Whether a thruster is actually burning: the station is under way, the fuel consumer has switched on, and there is fuel to burn. One definition rather than two, because the flame the player sees (RocketAdapterAnimationSystem) and the noise that draws attacks are supposed to be the same event, and two copies of the same three-way test in unrelated files drift the moment either is given a fourth cond…
FFSystems.PowerTransfer.HeatReceiverSyst: Publishes each heat receiver's production: the heat carried by the transmitters whose `PowerTransferEdge` targets it, the same direction power transfer resolves (PowerTransmitterPowerDistributionSystem).
FFSystems.PowerTransfer.PowerTransferLin: The two halves of a transmitter-to-receiver link: the transmitter's `PowerTransferEdge` names the receiver it targets, the receiver's names the transmitter feeding it. Every writer of the receiver half goes through here, single-threaded, so that a release can never wipe a newer claim.

Peer-independent claim order: the transmitter's grid tile, x then z then y. Two in-play transmitters never share a tile, and a tile is the same on every peer, unlike an entity index or a chunk position after a join.
True when the receiver's back-link names a live transmitter other than `transmitter` that still targets it.

`transmitter` stops feeding `receiver`: clear the receiver's back-link and the power and heat it was delivering, unless another live transmitter holds it. A back-link that is already Entity.Null or stale still gets the delivery cleared, so a half-link cannot strand a receiver's output.

`transmitter` takes `receiver` unless another live transmitter holds it. Callers that resolve several claims in one pass order them with `ClaimOrder`, so the first claimant in that order wins on every peer.
A transmitter that lost a claim targets nothing: no edge and no alignment, so the grid sends it nothing to carry. Its next endpoint pass tries again, and loses again while the holder stays.
FFSystems.PowerTransfer.PowerTransmitter: Re-aims every transmitter when the station grids change. The parallel pass only scans: each transmitter finds the receiver in front of it and writes its OWN edge and alignment. Every change to a receiver's back-link is collected and applied afterwards by one single-threaded job, releases before claims, claims in `PowerTransferLinks.ClaimOrder`.

Scans the line in front of the transmitter for the first in-play structure and sets the transmitter's alignment and hit position. Returns that structure when it is an aligned receiver of the same module type, Entity.Null otherwise. Writes nothing but the transmitter.

The single-threaded form, for callers that re-aim one transmitter at a time (MobileStationUndockingSystem, RotateInPlaceControllerSystem): scan, then apply the link change in place through `PowerTransferLinks`.
FFSystems.Presentation.BargeFieldVfxInst: One cargo barge's route field, for the shader FinalFactory/VfxBargeField, laid out to match its `BargeInstance` StructuredBuffer element (64 bytes).
0 waiting.. 1 under way, from the barge's drawn speed.
World units the haze has drifted along the route (start to end is positive).
The route's start: the start dock's tile centre, as the route arrows draw it.
0..1: fades the field in when a barge first shows.
FFSystems.Presentation.BargeFieldVfxPres: Draws the electromagnetic field each cargo barge rides along its route: a heat-haze that gently blurs and wobbles the space background along the route, from the dock it loads at to the one it delivers to, strongest around the barge. Every barge is drawn in one instanced `Graphics.RenderPrimitives` call. See Documentation/Combat-VFX.md, "Cargo barge field".
Half the hull's length (CargoBargeHull.asset spans about 42 units).
Whether this device can draw the field at all; the tests skip on the same condition.
Barge fields drawn last frame (for the capture rig).
The haze's half-width around the barge: about three units past the hull's sides (the hull is about 11.5 units wide), so the barge sits in it. Along the route it narrows to _RouteSpread of it.
The instances drawn last frame (for tests and the capture rig).
The route a barge's arrows show, in world space: tile centres at the start tile's height, exactly as LogisticsRouteDisplaySystem places the route arrow and its two end markers.
Dev switch for before/after captures and perf runs.
Whether the one invisible warm-up draw has been submitted, so the shader's first-use compile happens at game load rather than when the first barge comes into view (as for the hover field).
FFSystems.Presentation.BeamVfxInstance: One instance of the procedural beam shader (FinalFactory/VfxBeam), laid out to match its `BeamInstance` StructuredBuffer element (48 bytes).
FFSystems.Presentation.BeamVfxInstance.A: x = extend (0..1), y = retract (0..1), z = seconds since the beam turned on.
FFSystems.Presentation.BeamVfxPresentati: Draws every mining laser and research beam with the procedural beam shader (Assets/Art/Shaders/Vfx/VfxBeam.shader): one instanced `Graphics.RenderPrimitives` call per beam type, however many beams are firing. See Documentation/Combat-VFX.md, "Continuous beams".
FFSystems.Presentation.BeltCornerPath: The drawn path of a belt item going round a curved connector. Presentation only.
FFSystems.Presentation.BeltCornerPath.Ad: The drawn parameter for a new heartbeat: the simulation's, unless that is more than `maxStep` ahead of the last drawn one, in which case the drawn item falls behind and catches up over the next heartbeats. Never ahead of the simulation.
FFSystems.Presentation.BeltCornerPath.Ca: How far the drawn parameter may run ahead of the belt's own travel per heartbeat (x2): the simulation crosses the curve tile's 10 units of path in the time of 5, so the drawn item covers the curve at twice belt speed in path terms, about 1.6 times in world distance.
FFSystems.Presentation.BeltCornerPath.Co: Called by every capture after it shifts Curr into Prev. Clears the corner state, then carries it on to the new Curr while the item is still on the same path and either the pair still touches the curve or the drawn parameter is still behind. Once the item is past the curve and caught up, the plain Prev → Curr blend is the same straight line, so the corner state stops.
FFSystems.Presentation.BeltCornerPath.Di: How far `position` is from the drawn path: the feeding run's last tile, the quarter circle, or the straight run on from its exit edge.
FFSystems.Presentation.BeltCornerPath.En: Starts drawing an item that is on the curve tile along this curve. The Prev end of the pair is projected onto the path (normally the feeding run's exit edge, where the item parked); one that is not on it starts the pair at the simulation's position, a plain snap onto the curve.
FFSystems.Presentation.BeltCornerPath.Ev: The drawn world position at path parameter `s`.
FFSystems.Presentation.BeltCornerPath.Is: True when the snapshot is already drawing round the curve starting at `entry`.
True when the snapshot is drawing round a curve of this connector's tile, turning either way. A curve the item brought from the group before it (still catching up past that curve's exit) is not one.
FFSystems.Presentation.BeltCornerPath.On: Distance (u) within which a position counts as on the belt's line.
FFSystems.Presentation.BeltCornerPath.Ra: The curve runs edge-middle to edge-middle round the tile's inner corner.
FFSystems.Presentation.BeltCornerPath.Ti: One connector tile in world units (`FixedPointConstants.TileLengthInLocalTransformUnits`; `BeltCornerPathTest` pins the two together).
FFSystems.Presentation.BeltCornerPath.Tr: The curve a connector is drawn as, from which of its two curve visuals are shown. A curve shows exactly one of them. Both shown is not a curve: it is the connector prefab as instantiated, before `ConnectorEndsDisplaySystem` first configures its visuals, which is every connector for the first heartbeats after a load, a join or a resync.

The path parameter of a position the SIMULATION put an item at: on the curve connector's own line (which starts at the tile's back edge, so the tile middle is 5), or on the feeding run up to its exit edge (0 and below). False when the position is on neither — a teleport, or an item that has turned off this path.
FFSystems.Presentation.BeltCornerPresent: Puts belt items that are on a curved connector onto their drawn curve: once per heartbeat, right after `WorldEntityInterpolationCaptureSystem` took the new pose, every item on the curve tile of a group whose first connector is drawn as a curve gets `BeltCornerPath.Enter`ed, unless the capture already carried it on round this same curve. See `BeltCornerPath` for why and how.
The curve's entry edge and directions, or false when the connector is not drawn curved.
FFSystems.Presentation.CargoDroneVisibil: Hides or shows every cargo barge for THIS player (`LocalViewSettings.HideCargoDrones`) by switching off the enableable `MaterialMeshInfo` of the barge and everything under it (hull meshes and the cargo models parented to it).
FFSystems.Presentation.CombatVfxPresenta: Feeds the procedural combat VFX shaders (Assets/Art/Shaders/Vfx/) once per rendered frame: advances the VFX clock and publishes it as the global `_FFVfxTime`; stamps `VfxBirthTime` on impacts rendering for the first time, so their animation starts on the frame they appear whatever heartbeat spawned them; writes `ProjectileVfxTravel` (distance flown since the muzzle; for a Plasma bolt, its clearanc…
FFSystems.Presentation.CometVfxInstance: One instance of the procedural comet shader (FinalFactory/VfxComet), laid out to match its `CometInstance` StructuredBuffer element (48 bytes).
x = fade (0..1), y = tail length (0..1), z = seconds drawn, w = landing splash (0..1).
Nucleus radius in world units; every length in the shader is a multiple of it.
FFSystems.Presentation.CometVfxPresentat: Draws the coma and the dust and ion tails of every comet in flight with the procedural comet shader (Assets/Art/Shaders/Vfx/VfxComet.shader): one instanced `Graphics.RenderPrimitives` call per 20-unit slice of height, however many comets there are, so each slice sorts against the fog planes at its own height.
Nucleus radius of a comet diving into a catcher (Resources/ItemEntities/CometCore.prefab: its comet-shard renderer draws the comet-core mesh, ~12.5 units, at 0.6 under a CometModel at 3).
Nucleus radius of an ambient flyby (Prefabs/Comet.prefab: comet-shard, ~10 units, at scale 0.8). CometVfxSizeTest pins both radii against the prefabs.
Coma quad + 14 dust tail segments + 8 ion tail segments, 6 vertices each (see the shader).
FFSystems.Presentation.DeathExplosionCap: Takes each heartbeat's deaths from `DeathSystem.DeathEntitiesThisFrame` while the dead are still there to measure: after `FFLateBufferSystem` and before `DeletionSystem`, which destroys them at the end of the same frame.
One `[DeathExplosion]` log line for a death (`LogFlag`).

Whether a death draws an explosion. Players, black-hole deaths and every self-destruct do not: a worn-out bot carries `SelfDestructMarker` (DeathSystem gives it a small impact), and an orphaned ship that timed out (OrphanedShipSystem, after its station was deconstructed) has only its `DeathMarker`'s `Source.SelfDestruct`. The slot lattice is a Fibonacci spiral about the vertical axis, so turning it about that axis maps it almost onto itself, and seen from above (the game's camera) a vertical spin was invisible (first clip review). About a tilted axis the panels visibly slide across the star.
How fast the shell turns: slow enough to read as a structure, fast enough to see it turn.
Where slot `index` sits on the shell of `radius` right now.
The shell's radius: the middle of the simulated orbits.

The shell's rotation at presentation time `elapsedSeconds`, with a per-star phase so neighbouring stars do not turn in step. A presentation clock: every frame, smooth, and nothing in the simulation reads it. Bots in transit home in on the moving slot point, so they still land on it.

1 once the transit is over (arrival or recall). The anchor is kept until the next heartbeat capture, so the frames that blend the last rail pose into the arrival pose still converge on the destination.
The snapshot's heartbeat frame when the transit ended (compared by inequality only).
The frame this anchor was last seen in transit (anchors not seen are ended, then dropped).
Where the bot was drawn on the heartbeat before its rail began.
Moves a drawn rail pose onto the line from `start` to the destination, at the same progress, facing along that line.
Distance from `point` to the segment origin → destination.

The pose before the first rail pose must be at least this far from the rail for the pair to be the hand-off jump. Well above both the rail's first step and the interpolation's blend allowance for that speed (~28 u), so the pair is always drawn as a snap to the rail pose and the offset is added to that; a bot that was already this close to its segment has nothing to hide.
A captured pose within this distance of the rail segment is on the rail.
How far along origin → destination the projection of `point` is, 0..1.

The rail pose to draw from. On the heartbeat of the jump itself the interpolation snaps to the rail pose (the pair is far apart), which would put the drawn bot a whole heartbeat of its travel ahead at once; that heartbeat is blended from the rail's start instead, so the drawn bot leaves `Start` smoothly.

Detects the hand-off jump in a captured pose pair: the current pose is on the rail and the previous one is well off it. Then `start` is where the bot was drawn before the jump. A load, join or resync mid-transit captures both poses on the rail, and a bot that was already at its segment starts next to the rail, so neither is anchored.
FFSystems.Presentation.EngineExhaustVfxP: Feeds the procedural exhaust shader (Assets/Art/Shaders/Vfx/VfxExhaust.shader) once per rendered frame: each exhaust's thrust follows how fast its engine is DRAWN moving, measured from its own `LocalToWorld` after `WorldEntityInterpolationRenderSystem` has written the smoothed pose, smoothed. A parked ship shows a small idle flame, a cruising one a long, steady flame.
How fast the afterburner lights (per second, exponential) and how fast it fades out: under a tenth of a second once the dash is over, so the plume lasts as long as the dash does.

The lowest afterburner level drawn: under it the afterburner is out and the level is exactly 0. The fade is exponential, so without a floor the level spent about four seconds after every dash far below anything visible but still above 0, and once it was small enough (about 1e-35, some 3.4 s after the dash) the shader's two stages disagreed about whether it was 0: the vertex stage drew the plume's…

Smoothed drawn speed, in multiples of the player's BaseMoveSpeed, past which the player is dashing. The dash flies at 4x (AfterburnerConfig.asset, Speed) and crosses this within a few frames; normal flight never passes 1x.

How fast (per second, exponential) the drawn speed that puts the afterburner out follows the ship: within a few frames of the dash's end. The slow smoothed speed that lights it lags the dash's end by about a tenth of a second, which kept the plume burning past it.
Dev override for captures: 0..1 pins every afterburner's level; below 0 is off.
Dev override for captures and perf runs: 0..1 pins every flame's thrust; below 0 is off.

False when the game was launched with `FlatMapMarkerPlacement.DisableFlag`.

The smallest factor drawn. Zero would give Entities Graphics a singular matrix to invert; at this size a 30 u shield is 0.03 u across, far below a pixel.
Length of the shrink-out: the grow-in's 0.2 s, played backwards.
Seconds from the last heartbeat to the heartbeat that deletes the shield: the first heartbeat whose simulation time reaches the release. Zero once the release is due (the shield is on its way out).

Whether this player has hidden cargo barges.

See Documentation/Combat-VFX.md, "Flying stations". Flying is the station's primary structure's `Placeable.IsFlying`.

The formation-offset weight a fleet ship is eased toward.
Where one of the local player's own formation ships is drawn: at the drawn local ship plus its filtered place relative to the local ship, blended in by the ship's formation weight.

That place changes as fast as the formation reshapes (a turn swings the lead, a stop lets the ships drift in: tenths of a second and slower), while what shakes it is per heartbeat: the ship's steering answering a commander whose simulated steps are uneven (a client's position reports arrive…
False when the game was launched with `DisableFlag`. Managed code only.
False when the game was launched with `NoFormationAnchorFlag`. Managed code only.
Measurement only (`-ffNoFormationAnchor`): keep the drop and hidden-ship anchors but draw the local formation around the simulated ship as before, for A/B.

Time constant (s) of the filter on the drawn-ship offset. A client's simulation position lands unevenly, and a fleet ship's own movement smooths that out, so the raw offset would put the jitter straight back onto the formation. The offset is mostly lead x velocity and changes only as fast as the ship turns, so 0.1 s removes the per-heartbeat noise and little else.
True while a fleet bot (a construction or supply bot) is out on a task at a place in the world: assigned, flying to or working at the build site or the item's source.
The simulated distance at which a drop is collected (`PickupableVacuumSystem`).

Dropped in one frame (a client's ship stopping: its simulated speed falls a round trip later, all at once) the filter hands back everything it was holding in that frame, a visible jump of the whole formation; eased, it hands it back over a few tenths of a second.
The share of `FormationRelativeSmoothTime` the filter aims for at `playerSpeed`.

A player's simulation position is rewritten once per heartbeat, but every interpolated entity is drawn between its last two heartbeat poses. The offset that moves something from "beside the simulated ship" to "beside the drawn ship" must use the player's position BLENDED THE SAME WAY, or it jumps by a heartbeat of travel on every heartbeat. This carries the last two heartbeat values.

0 at or beyond the vacuum range, 1 at or inside the pickup distance, smooth between.

Starts tracking `hauler` from rest. An echo it already carries describes a heartbeat whose step is already in the simulation pose, so it is marked consumed.

Whether a drawn lift-off has reached flight height. From there the pilot's keys are predicted as in flight: the drawn lift ran one input latency ahead of the simulation's, so input from this frame on comes back as the simulation's first airborne steps, just as it does in flight.
Stops drawing a lift ahead; whatever height it still adds eases out as error.
Time constant the error eases away with, seconds.

The latest applied-drive echo, and whether the simulation is driving the station now.
The station's top speed (units/s) and turn rate (rad/s), which bound the lead.
Whether this frame predicts at all (piloting a flying station, no flight rail, not stalled).
Another player rides this station too (`PilotedStationPrediction.Shared`).
The pilot's commanded velocity (units/s) and turn rate (rad/s), exactly as the simulation will apply them.
The share of an applied step the lead must still hold along it for the step to be taken out.
Whether the lead still holds input along `echo`: once this peer's input has all landed, a further step in the same direction is another rider's, however alike.
The simulation has finished the lift-off: flying, with no flight rail carrying the station.
The height the station is drawn at before the lift offset.

The most input the round trip can hold in flight, seconds of full-speed driving: a client's press takes roughly 0.2 to 0.4 s to come back applied (report up, the host's next heartbeat, the heartbeat down, the playout reserve).
