The simulation's hand-turn rate (`HaulerManualDriveApplySystem.RotationSpeedRadians`).

Launch flag for A/B measurement of a parked ship changing frame as it is sent out or comes home: with it the blend snaps over in a quarter second on the idle marker alone (`StationFollowerStep.EaseWeight` and `WeightTarget` are not used).

Where a station structure is drawn this frame, for code that follows it from outside ECS (the camera while riding, the command feedback): the pose `WorldEntityInterpolationRenderSystem` draws when it is interpolated, else its simulation pose, moved by the pilot's prediction (`PilotedStationPrediction`) when it belongs to the station being predicted.
FFSystems.Presentation.PlasmaBoltVfxStep: the pure rules behind how a Plasma bolt is drawn. Presentation only: the bolt's simulation (its pose, speed, hit range and damage) never reads any of it.

How far the bolt's head is out of the shooter's hull, measured so the trail behind it cannot reach the ship (negative while the head is still inside the hull). Head ahead of the ship's centre along its heading: how far it is past the hull's front edge. The trail reaches back to that edge and no further, from any angle the ship has turned to.
The level a bolt is drawn at: `casterLevel`, or the dev override.
What each level above 1 adds, as a share of the level-1 bolt.

Distance (u) from a player ship's centre to its hull's edge: the PlayerEntity model is 10.2 u wide and 9.7 u long (its renderer bounds), so about 5 u in every direction, plus a little margin for the hull's glow.
Electricity at level 1; it rises evenly to 1 at `MaxLevel`.
The level-1 bolt, as a share of the bolt drawn.
Dev only (the `vfx.plasmalevel` automation verb): when above 0, every Plasma bolt on this peer is DRAWN at this level, whatever its caster's real level. Presentation only.
The Oracle shop's last level of "Plasma Bolt Damage" (its asset's `MaxLevel`).

This frame's `_VfxTravel` for a Plasma bolt: x = the clearance, never less than last frame's (the trail does not shrink back if the ship catches up), y = seed, z = size, w = electricity, negative when the shooter is not behind the head. A zero z marks a bolt not drawn yet, whose clearance starts fresh.
Whether the shooter is behind the bolt's head along its heading (the usual case).
Drawn size of the bolt at `level`, as a share of the bolt.
FFSystems.Presentation.PlayerBoltSpawnPr: Measurement probe for where a player's bolt is born against where its shooter is drawn, on the bolt's first drawn frame. Off unless the process was started with `-ffBoltSpawnProbe` (or `Enabled` is set from the editor).

Measurement only (`-ffBoltProbeCaptureDir <dir>`): from the first drawn frame of each of the first `CaptureBursts` probed bolts, save `CaptureFrames` consecutive game frames as PNGs, for a shooter-versus-observer comparison.
Measurement only (`-ffBoltProbeNoAnchor`): no launch anchor, so a bolt is drawn on its simulated path from its first frame and the spawn point itself is visible.
Measurement only (`-ffBoltProbeNoLead`): fire requests carry no lead, so bolts are born at the simulation position as before the lead existed. The "before" arm of a comparison.

The shooter's drawn position and move velocity at the moment it sent a fire request, matched first-in first-out to its next probed local bolt, so the log can also score the alternatives that use click-time state (the stamped drawn position, the input velocity at fire time).
Saves this frame if a capture burst is running; called once per frame.
FFSystems.Presentation.PlayerFireLeadEst: The shooter's own measurement of how far its drawn ship is ahead of its simulation position, as a time: the lead a fire request carries (`PlayerFireLead`).
What the next fire request carries, in whole milliseconds, already clamped.
The running estimate (s), or negative while no heartbeat has been sampled yet; the fire request then uses one heartbeat (`CurrentLeadMilliseconds`).
The last heartbeat interval seen (s): the lead before any sample.
Slower than this (u/s) the gap is too small to divide by; the sample is skipped.
Feeds one heartbeat frame; called by `PlayerFireLeadEstimatorSystem`.
Forgets the estimate (a new session, a reload, a test).
The running estimate after one sample, given the previous one (negative = none).
Weight of a new sample in the running estimate (about the last five heartbeats).

A sample is taken only while the ship still flies the velocity the heartbeat sampled, within this share of its speed. The ship has no momentum, so a turn, stop or start inside the window makes the gap say nothing about the delay; measured, such samples dragged the running estimate off by tens of milliseconds on a scripted maneuvering run.

One heartbeat-frame sample: the lead (s) that places `simulationPosition` advanced along `simulationVelocity` nearest `drawnPosition`, or false when the ship is too slow to measure, is no longer flying the sampled velocity (`drawnVelocity`), or the sample is outside [0, max lead].

Feeds `PlayerFireLeadEstimator` once per heartbeat, on the frame that applied it, with the local ship's drawn position and the simulation position and velocity that heartbeat delivered. Runs after `LocalPlayerMotionSystem`, so the drawn position is this frame's: the one a bolt born on this heartbeat is first drawn beside (`ProjectileParticlePresentationSystem.BeginLaunchAnchor`).
FFSystems.Presentation.PlayerLiveryTintS: Tints each player's ship livery with the player's colour. Presentation: it reads the simulation `PlayerColor` and writes only the Model entity's `PlayerLiveryColor` material override, never anything a simulation system reads.
FFSystems.Presentation.PlayerShipHideSys: Keeps the ship of a player who is not in the world out of view: a parked player (not in the session: `ParkedPlayer`) or a defeated one (`PlayerCombatState.IsDefeated`, dead until the respawn).
Where a hidden ship model sits, relative to its player entity.
FFSystems.Presentation.PredictedBoltMeet: where the local player's bolt is expected to hit, worked out in the frame of the press, so the predicted bolt (`PredictedPlayerBolts`) and the real bolt's hand-off (`ProjectileLaunchAnchorStep.BeginFromPredicted`) can be timed to reach that point as the simulated bolt does. Pure, presentation only: it reads positions and returns a distance; the simulation's hit is decided where it always was.

How far a bolt flies with nothing in its way: its weapon's `range`, or less when its `LimitedLifetime` ends first. `LimitedLifetimeSystem` removes it on the first heartbeat its age is PAST `lifetime`, and it has moved on every heartbeat until then: the Plasma bolt is gone after 12 heartbeats at 16 UPS, 135 u into a 185 u range. A lifetime of zero or less means it has none.

How far along `forward` (a unit vector) from `origin` the simulated bolt will be when it first comes within `hitRadius` of a target now at `targetPosition` moving at `targetVelocity`: the bolt leaves `delay` seconds from now and flies at `speed`. Returns `range` when it never does within its range. A target already in reach when the bolt is born gives 0.
The same for a collider the bolt's ray will stop on, `surfaceDistance` along the heading: the bolt ends within `RayReach` short of it.
`ProjectilePhysicsCollisionSystem` ends a bolt when a collider is within this far ahead of it, so a ray hit lands up to this far short of the hull; half of it on average.
FFSystems.Presentation.PredictedPlayerBo: the local player's Plasma bolts drawn before the simulation births them, and the hand-off to the real bolt. Presentation only: nothing here is read by a simulation system.

Registers a predicted bolt fired now from `origin` along `forward` at `speed`, flying at most `range`; returns its id. `meet` is the distance its speed was timed for (where it is expected to hit); omitted or longer than the range, the range.
The real bolt must fly within this angle of the predicted one to claim it (cosine). The aim is the same fp value on both sides, so a genuine pair matches to rounding.
Raised when a real bolt claims a predicted one (its id), inside `ProjectileParticlePresentationSystem`'s update: the owner hides it in that frame.
The clock predicted bolts are timed on (frame time, the same value all frame).
Adds where every predicted bolt still waiting for its real bolt is drawn now (the impact probe).
How many predicted bolts are waiting for their real bolt.
Weight of a new observed press-to-hand-off delay in the running estimate.
Raised on the first drawn frame of every bolt the LOCAL player fired, with whether it claimed a predicted bolt (the input latency probe's "drawn" event, and the arm with prediction off).
The slowest a predicted bolt flies, as a share of the real bolt's speed (a very late link).
The running estimate of how long (s) a local shot takes from the press to its real bolt being drawn, from the hand-offs seen so far; negative until the first one.
Forgets a predicted bolt that will never be claimed (rejected, timed out, a new session).
Forgets the observed delay too (a new session: another link).

The constant speed for a predicted bolt: it covers `range` in the time the player sees the shot, `expectedDelay` (press to hand-off) plus the real bolt's flight, so it reaches the end of the range together with the real bolt. 92-95% of `speed` on the host, 70-85% on a client at 60-150 ms round trip.
Distance (u) a predicted bolt has flown after `elapsed` s, never past its range.

The oldest predicted bolt flying along `forward`, removed and reported through `Claimed`, where it is drawn now and how fast it flies; false when there is none. Oldest first because one client's shots are applied in the order they were sent. Each claim feeds `ObservedDelaySeconds`.
As above, plus `meetPoint`: where the claimed bolt's speed was timed to arrive.
Where predicted bolt `id` is drawn now; false once it was claimed or removed.
FFSystems.Presentation.PresentationClock: Spec 057 — the pure accumulator rule behind `PresentationClockSystem`, extracted so tests and the fixture harness drive the SAME code the editor runs instead of a hand-mirrored copy that can silently diverge from it (rev 4, review finding 13).
Advances the clock for one rendered frame.

How many heartbeat intervals without a new heartbeat count as a STALL (pause, load, waiting for a peer), and so where `PresentationClock.SecondsSinceHeartbeatUnclamped` saturates and `LocalPlayerMotionSystem` holds the local ship.

Spec 057 — keeps `PresentationClock` current, first thing in the controller pre-transform group so every presentation system in the frame sees the same value. The rule itself lives in `PresentationClockStep` so tests drive the same code this system runs.
Launch flag that turns frame pacing off.
FFSystems.Presentation.PresentationFrame: How much presentation time a rendered frame should represent (`PresentationClock.FrameSeconds`), the pure rule behind `PresentationClockSystem` so tests drive the same code.

Pacing only runs while a heartbeat spans more than this many typical frames. When every frame applies a heartbeat (single-player at 60 UPS and 60 fps) all frames cost alike, the plain delta is already right, and the pacer passes it through unchanged.
Advances the pacer by one rendered frame and returns the presentation time this frame represents.
Weight of each new duration in its kind's running estimate.
Taking back time given ahead never shrinks a frame below this share of its prediction.
A frame lasting more than this many times its kind's estimate (or less than its inverse) is a hitch, and teaches the estimate nothing...
...unless this many frames in a row say so: then frames really do last that long now.
A frame delta at or below this is a paused frame (time scale 0), not a short frame.
Presentation this far ahead of the screen is not pacing error any more: forget it.
FFSystems.Presentation.PresentationRotat: turns the decorative spinners of placed structures every rendered frame instead of once per heartbeat, for every carrier `PresentationRotatorTaggingSystem` has tagged with `PresentationRotator` (which `AutoRotatorSystem` now excludes, so exactly one of the two steps each carrier).

classifies every `RotationParameters` CHILD carrier once: if the prefab root it hangs from is a placed structure (`Placeable`), its spin is decoration and gets `PresentationRotator`, so `PresentationRotatorSystem` takes it over from the heartbeat-cadenced `AutoRotatorSystem` (at 16 UPS a heartbeat-stepped spinner visibly ratchets).
FFSystems.Presentation.ProjectileLaunchA: U7 — the pure rule that makes a player's projectile LEAVE the ship the player sees, instead of appearing behind it. Presentation only: it moves nothing but the drawn pose.

Decides the anchor on the bolt's first drawn frame and records it in `snapshot`. `hasShooterPose` is false when the projectile was not fired by a player, or its shooter no longer exists; `fresh` is false once the bolt has been captured past its birth seed (it was first seen late, so its first drawn frame is not its launch). Either way the anchor is `None` and the bolt draws as it always did.

the local player's own bolt taking over the bolt drawn for it since the shot (`PredictedPlayerBolts`), which flew at `predictedSpeed`. The real bolt is drawn at `predictedPosition` in this frame and keeps one constant speed to the end of its range, where it meets its simulated path: The offset decays LINEARLY over the bolt's range (`ProjectileLaunchAnchorState.ActiveLinear`), so the drawn speed is…

Largest share of the bolt's speed the blend may take away at its steepest point (smoothstep's peak slope is 1.5). 0.4 keeps a 180 u/s plasma bolt above 108 u/s, faster than the ~96-100 u/s cruise of the ship that fired it, so a forward shot never drifts back into the hull while it blends.

Beyond this gap (u) the shooter did not merely move, it jumped (respawn, portal, a load or a join), and anchoring to it would fly the bolt in from somewhere it never was. Such bolts draw exactly as before.

Floor on the blend distance (u), so a small gap is closed gently rather than in a few frames. 40 u is about 0.22 s of plasma flight; the single-player gap (~5 u) then costs the drawn bolt under a fifth of its speed at the steepest point.
Gaps shorter than this (u) are not worth a blend.

The drawn offset for this frame, given where the bolt would be drawn without it. Progress is the bolt's travel along its heading from `start`, so the blend is tied to the flight rather than to frame timing. Retires the anchor once fully blended.

The steady state of `CriticallyDampedSpring` following a target that moves at 1 u/s, advanced every `dt`: how far it trails (s, i.e. u per u/s) and its internal velocity (as a share of the target's). Both scale with the speed. Found by running the spring, since the discrete update settles off the continuous speed × smooth time.
FFSystems.Presentation.ProjectileParticl: Bridges the projectile pose evaluated by `WorldEntityInterpolationStep` into managed ParticleSystem companions. Unity's companion transform copier runs in the SimulationSystemGroup after TransformSystemGroup and therefore sees authoritative stepped LocalToWorld matrices before the presentation overwrite.
FFSystems.Presentation.RocketAdapterPilo: The pilot's half of `RocketAdapterTurnSmoothingSystem`, pure so tests drive the rule the game runs: where the pods of the station this peer pilots point, and whether its plume burns, from the pilot's own reported drive intent instead of the simulation's (which lags it by the input latency).
The drive direction the pilot's keys ask for (world, as reported), and whether any drive key is held.
The hauler whose station is drawn with the pilot's input; Entity.Null when none is.
The station's drawn turn on top of its simulation heading (`PilotedStationPrediction.Turn`).

The pilot to follow this frame: while the prediction draws this peer's own input (or a lift-off it started), with a drive key held or the input of the last one still on its way to the simulation. Not while it draws a Move/Land flight, and not for a rider who is not driving (another rider's drive is the simulation's, drawn as it comes).

Replaces the simulation's target for one part of a piloted adapter. While a drive key is held the part points along the pilot's direction (RocketAdapterAnimationSystem's rule: `LookRotationSafe` of the direction, so a turn in place points where the simulation's will), expressed under the adapter as it is drawn (its simulation rotation turned by the prediction), and the plume frame burns.
FFSystems.Presentation.RocketAdapterTurn: The first half of `RocketAdapterTurnSmoothingSystem`: it must read the parts' matrices before `WorldEntityInterpolationRenderSystem` overwrites them.

Draws a rocket adapter's pods (and the plume frame) turning toward a new heading instead of snapping to it. `RocketAdapterAnimationSystem` sets their rotation to the station's heading on the heartbeat, so a turn used to show as a jump; here the drawn rotation chases it every rendered frame (a factor of `dt *``DefaultTurnRate`: a quarter turn is 90% done in 4 frames at 60 fps, snappy with a touch o…

How fast the drawn rotation chases its target, per second. Twice the player ship's (`LinearMotionStep.RotationInterpolationRate`): once the pilot's pods followed the keys instead of the simulation's late heading, the ship's rate still left them 10 frames behind a hull that answers in one; 30 is 4 frames (67 ms). Measured with scripts/feel/analyze_pilot_turns.py.
Dev switch for before/after captures: off draws the simulation rotation, as before.
Dev switch for before/after captures: off makes the pilot's pods follow the simulation too. The launch flag `NoFollowPilotFlag` clears it.
The rate in force (a factor of `dt * rate` per frame). The launch flag `TurnRateFlag` overrides it, to compare rates on a built player.
FFSystems.Presentation.RocketPlumeVfxIns: One nozzle of a burning (or cooling) rocket adapter, for the shader FinalFactory/VfxRocketPlume, laid out to match its `PlumeInstance` StructuredBuffer element (48 bytes).
x = seconds since ignition, y = seconds since shutdown (< 0 while burning), z = throttle.
FFSystems.Presentation.RocketPlumeVfxPre: Draws every rocket adapter's plume with the procedural shader (Assets/Art/Shaders/Vfx/VfxRocketPlume.shader): one instanced `Graphics.RenderPrimitives` call per adapter style. See Documentation/Combat-VFX.md, "Engine exhaust".
Dev switch for previews and perf runs: every adapter burns as if its station were under way, heading along `ForceHeading` (world). Turning it off plays the shutdown.
Dev switch for before/after captures and perf runs.
FFSystems.Presentation.ScalableLaserPres: Spec 057 (P5) — re-anchors a firing beam's drawn endpoints onto the PRESENTATION poses of its two endpoint entities, every rendered frame.
FFSystems.Presentation.ScaleOverTimePres: The scale a `ScaleOverTime` animation is DRAWN at between two heartbeats.
The drawn scale, or false when the simulation's own matrix should be drawn: a finished or paused animation (it no longer changes between heartbeats) or a mode this step does not know.
FFSystems.Presentation.StationBeltItemPr: The rule `StationBeltItemPresentationSystem` draws with, kept pure for tests.

Where a connector is drawn this frame: the rule of the render systems. Interpolated, its hand-off pose when `PilotedStationPredictionHandOffSystem` set one, else its blend; not interpolated, its simulation pose, moved by the prediction on the piloted station (`PilotedStationPredictionRenderSystem`).

An item's drawn pose: its offset from the connector in the connector's own frame, taken from each captured pair and blended as `WorldEntityInterpolationStep.Evaluate(in WorldEntityPresentationInterpolation, float, float, float, out float3, out quaternion)` blends a pose (position on the unclamped clock with its overshoot budget, rotation clamped), then put on the connector's drawn pose.

Draws the belt items of a moving station on the belt as it is drawn. The station's buildings are drawn through their own interpolation snapshot and, for the station the local player pilots, moved by `PilotedStationPrediction` (`PilotedStationPredictionHandOffSystem`).
FFSystems.Presentation.StationCompanionP: draws the managed companion objects of a station's buildings (the Hydro Power Plant's waterfalls, the Artifact Assembler's, Antimatter Nexus's and Celestral Oracle's effects: every ParticleSystem and VisualEffect) where the building is DRAWN, every rendered frame. Ben: "for the hydro power plants, the 'water' effect inside of it will actually lag behind a mobile station as you move".
Measurement only: leave a station's companions where Unity's copier put them, (the "before" arm of the comparison clips).
FFSystems.Presentation.StationFollowerSt: Draws what rides a flying station (a platform's parked ships) in the station's DRAWN frame, on every peer, pure so tests drive the code the game runs.
Where a follower interpolated to `position` is drawn.
Beyond this distance an idle ship is on its way home and is drawn where it is; between the two ranges the station's frame fades in as it closes on its platform.

Samples the reference structure's simulation pose once per heartbeat. Keyed by INEQUALITY, like the interpolation capture: the heartbeat frame wraps and resets. A pair too far apart to blend is a teleport and starts over.

One rendered frame of the hand-over: an exponential step toward `target`, never faster than `HandOverSlideSpeed` moves the ship across the gap between the two frames (`shift`, u). The first frame a ship is seen takes the target itself.

The tracked pose at `fraction` (unclamped seconds since the heartbeat over its interval), blended as `WorldEntityInterpolationStep.Evaluate(in WorldEntityPresentationInterpolation, float, float, float, out float3, out quaternion)` blends a ship: position on the unclamped clock with its overshoot budget, rotation on the clamped one.
The reference structure's drawn pose this frame.
The reference structure's simulation pose blended between its last two heartbeats.

The most a ship may slide on screen (u/s) while it changes frame. The two frames are apart by the pilot's lead, up to 0.6 s of the station's travel on a client, and a ship that crossed that in a few frames would pop; at this speed the hand-over is a drift well under a Bat's own speed.
Time constant (s) of the hand-over between the station's frame and a ship's own motion.

Whether a ship is parked on its station: it stays parked for as long as it is idle, however far the station's turns leave it behind its slot, and one that was sent out is parked again once it is idle and back within `ParkedRange` of the structure that owns it. The first frame a ship is seen (the station has just taken off) an idle ship within `ApproachRange` counts as parked.
Within this distance of the structure that owns it, an idle ship is parked: wholly in the station's frame.

How much of the station's frame a ship should be drawn with (0 its own interpolated motion, 1 the station's frame). Only a ship parked on the station rides it. A ship that was sent out (no longer idle) is drawn where it is, and so is one flying home from a fight, although the simulation already calls it idle: the station's frame fades in over its last stretch, as it closes on its platform.
FFSystems.Presentation.StationGhostRider: Draws the unbuilt ghosts riding a flying station where they are on it: at their simulated place against the Command Core, carried by the core's DRAWN pose this frame.
FFSystems.Presentation.StationMotionGate: whether any station is drawn off its simulation pose this frame: a station building blended between heartbeats (its `WorldEntityPresentationInterpolation` is enabled only while its station moves, `MobileStationPresentationInterpolation`), or the piloted station moved by the pilot's prediction (`PilotedStationPrediction.Applies`, which can lead the first simulated step).
True while a station building is drawn between heartbeats or a piloted station is predicted.
Whether the systems that follow drawn stations have anything to do this frame. True in a world without this gate (a test world that did not make it), so they behave as before it existed.
FFSystems.Presentation.StationRiderPrese: A remote player who rides a vehicle or pilots a station looks to everyone else as they look to themselves: their ship is not drawn. The rider's own peer hides its ship Model while it rides (`VehicleRideModelVisibility`); this does the same for every other player's ship on this peer, from the agreed simulation state (`PlayerState.CurrentVehicle`), and shows it again when the ride ends, drawn in tha…
False only under `ShowRidersFlag`, and in tests of that arm.

Whether this peer hides that player's ship this frame: a remote player who rides. For what reads the ship before this system runs (the outline, in `LateUpdate`): in the frame a player boards, the Model is still in view there.
Where a rider is held for a seat structure drawn at `drawnVehicle`.
The height a rider is held at (`VehicleRideAction.LateActionUpdate`).
Measurement switch: with it a remote rider's ship is drawn on its seat, as it was before the riders were hidden (the "before" arm of scripts/feel/run_rider_look.py).

Whether a player whose ride has ended gets their ship back: not one who left the session or is dead until the respawn (their Model is `PlayerShipHideSystem`'s), and not the local player, whose own peer shows it (`VehicleRideModelVisibility`).
FFSystems.Presentation.VfxImpactDrawnAnc: The pure rules of `VfxImpactDrawnAnchor`: which entity a projectile's impact is anchored on, and the shift that carries the effect from the simulated hit onto the target as drawn. Presentation only.
Measurement only (`-ffNoImpactDrawnAnchor`): draw impacts where the simulation put them and time the local player's predicted bolt to the end of its range, for A/B.
False when the game was launched with `DisableFlag`. Managed code only.

A target drawn further than this from its simulation was not smoothed, it jumped (a respawn, a portal, a load); the effect stays where the simulation put it. The largest ordinary gap is the local ship's prediction lead: about 80 u at 325 u/s on a 250 ms link.

The entry of a projectile's hit-range neighbours nearest to it: what `KnnProjectileCollisionSystem` hit, up to its tie-break between two targets at the same distance, which does not matter for where an effect is drawn. Keeps `target` when no entry is nearer than `bestDistanceSq`.
The shift for an effect whose target is drawn at `targetDrawn` and simulated at `targetSimulated`; false (no shift) when the two coincide, or are too far apart to be the same motion (`MaxOffset`).
FFSystems.Presentation.VfxImpactSurfaceS: The pure rules of where a shot meets the hull the player sees. The simulation ends a shot where it decides the hit, and that point is not on the hull: a KNN hit fires when the bolt comes within the weapon's size of the target's CENTRE (10-15 u, from any side), and a beam ends at the centre.
Appends the twelve triangles of a box (render bounds) under a part's matrix in the hull's frame.
Whether the outline covers the ground-plane point `point`.
Measurement only (`-ffNoImpactSurface`): draw impacts and beam ends where drew them (the simulated hit carried onto the drawn target, a beam at the target's centre), for A/B.
The cache key of a ship kind's outline: the last one measured of any ship of that kind (they are the same model at the same scale), for a ship the hit killed before its effect was drawn.
False when the game was launched with `DisableFlag`. Managed code only.
A surface point further than this from the hit was not this hit's (a wrong target, a stale hull): the effect stays where put it. The largest units shot at are spawners and Razors, about 40 u across.
An outline smaller than this across is not a hull being drawn: a stowed fleet ship is drawn at scale 0 inside its owner (measured), and a hit on it keeps 's placement.
The effect is drawn this far out of the outline, toward the shooter: its quad is depth-tested, and a quad centred exactly on the edge is partly hidden by the hull around it.

The outline of `triangles` (three points each, in the hull's frame) seen from above: every cell whose middle a triangle covers, or that one of its edges crosses, on a grid with a cell of margin around it. False when there are none, or they cover less than `MinSize`.
The distance along the ray (`origin`, unit `heading`, in the hull's ground plane) to where it first enters a covered cell, refined to the cell's edge; false when it meets none within `reach`.

Where the shot through `hit` flying along `direction` first crosses `hull`'s outline, drawn with its frame at `root`: on the edge, at the hull's top, pulled `StandOff` back toward the shooter. A line that misses the outline (a grazing KNN hit) takes the outline's point nearest it. False when the shot has no direction across the ground or the hull is empty.
The cache key of one unit's own outline, measured afresh on each frame it is shot at.
FFSystems.Presentation.VisualEpisodePres: Opt-in diagnostic read between the feature-057 presentation overwrite and Entities Graphics.
FFSystems.Presentation.VisualEpisodeSmoo: Feature-058 calibration positive control. It resolves the next real local plasma bolt and advances only its hybrid ParticleSystem companions with constant frame-time motion.
FFSystems.Presentation.WorldEntityInterp: Spec 057 US2 (research R3) — snapshots every tagged world entity's authoritative pose once per heartbeat, so the render bracket has a Prev/Curr pair to fill the gap with.

Spec 057 US2 (research R1/R4) — the OVERWRITE half of the render bracket: every rendered frame it composes the smoothed pose of each tagged world entity and writes it into the `LocalToWorld` of that entity and its render subtree, immediately before `EntitiesGraphicsSystem` draws from those matrices.

Within this simulated distance of its owner a returning hidden ship is re-anchored on the drawn local ship (none of the shift at this range, all of it at the pickup distance). The formation's own range (`PickupDrawnAnchorStep.FleetAnchorZeroRange`): a hiding ship closes at up to 640 u/s, and from 60 u it took the whole shift (57 u on a client at half speed) in its last five frames.
Levels of children below the tagged root that the brush recomposes.

Spec 057 US2 (research R1) — the RESTORE half of the render bracket, and the determinism guard of the whole US2 mechanism: every `LocalToWorld` that `WorldEntityInterpolationRenderSystem` overwrote last frame is written back EXACTLY as it was saved, before any simulation system can read it this frame.

Spec 057 US2 (research R2) — the pure, unit-testable rule that turns a captured heartbeat pose pair plus the presentation clock into the pose a frame should draw. Extracted from `WorldEntityInterpolationRenderSystem` so tests drive the SAME code the editor runs instead of a hand-mirrored copy.

Margin on the speed-relative blend allowance: how many heartbeats of travel at the captured speed still count as MOTION rather than teleport. Mirrors the US1 local-player speed-relative snap threshold (max(25, speed x interval x 3)).

Takes the once-per-heartbeat snapshot the render side consumes, shifting the current pose into the previous one. Driven by `WorldEntityInterpolationCaptureSystem`; it lives here so tests exercise the same rule the editor runs.

Pulls `position` back along `flightDirection` (a unit vector, or zero for "no flight end") so it lies no further than `flightLength` past `flightStart`. Only the distance beyond the end is removed: a pose short of it, or off to the side of the line, is unchanged along every other axis.
Convenience overload: no unclamped time available — extrapolation stops at f = 1.

As above, plus a flight that ends at a known point: a mass-driven shot flies from `flightStart` along the unit `flightDirection` for `flightLength` and is gone on the heartbeat it gets there (`MassDrivenItemMovementSystem`).

The DRAWN pose: `Evaluate(in WorldEntityPresentationInterpolation, float, float, float, out float3, out quaternion)`'s result, filtered for Extrapolate mode through a critically-damped spring carried in the snapshot (see `WorldEntityPresentationInterpolation.VisualPosition` for why raw extrapolation jitters under lockstep heartbeat arrival jitter).

As above, plus a projectile's launch anchor (`ProjectileLaunchAnchorStep`): `launchStart` and `launchForward` are the projectile's spawn point and heading. The anchor offset joins the TARGET, ahead of the spring and the snap decision, so the spring state, the cached drawn pose and the particle-translation delta all describe the same drawn bolt.

The Extrapolate-mode spring's time constant. At 180 u/s (plasma) the steady-state lag is ~7 u — well under a heartbeat of travel — while a half-heartbeat target jump from an early lockstep heartbeat is spread over a few frames instead of landing as one visible pop.

Evaluates the pose to draw. Returns `Curr` unchanged — i.e. exactly today's stepped behaviour — whenever there is no usable history: the first capture after a spawn/load/join (`Initialized == 0`), a teleport beyond `SnapThreshold`, or a degenerate heartbeat interval. That is the layer's inert path, and it is what makes every reset case correct by construction rather than by bookkeeping.
How far the rendered frame has travelled toward the next heartbeat, 0..1. A non-positive interval (an uninitialised or paused clock) yields 0 rather than a division by zero.

How far past one interval the Interpolate mode may keep advancing POSITION, as a fraction of the interval. The clamped fraction alone holds a blending entity at `f = 1` for every frame a heartbeat lands late, which at 250 u/s reads as a micro-stall at 16 Hz — the same defect the `ExtrapolationBudget` exists for, one mode over.

THE single snap decision, shared by `Evaluate(in WorldEntityPresentationInterpolation, float, float, float, out float3, out quaternion)`, `EvaluateDrawn` and `ProjectileParticlePresentationSystem` — a caller computing its own copy can silently disagree with the pose path.

Distance between the two captured poses beyond which the entity did not MOVE, it was TELEPORTED (belt re-home, load, join, cross-belt hand-off), and no blend across the gap is meaningful. 25 u is far more than any entity covers in one heartbeat at real speeds, and far less than any teleport.
FFSystems.Selection.CameraFollowSystem: There's an invisible grid that we do raycasts against. We need to keep it moving with the camera so that any ray casts for player abilities hit this grid and have their intended effect.
FFSystems.Selection.FFDisableMovementMar: Presentation: turns `FFLtWToggle.EnableMovement` on for what the camera can see, every rendered frame. Only `LocalToFFWorldSystem` reads it, and only to skip the children of a toggled-off root. The structural half (attaching the toggle) is `FFLtWToggleAttachSystem`, on the heartbeat.
FFSystems.Selection.FFLtWToggleAttachSys: Gives every `LocalTransform`+`LocalToWorld` entity its `FFLtWToggle`, enabled, so `FFDisableMovementMarkerSystem` can cull it by camera from then on. Adding a component moves a simulation entity to another archetype (chunk membership, query order, the fingerprint census), so it runs on the heartbeat.
FFSystems.StationGrid.BurstStore: One storage device as the pulse readout sees it.
FFSystems.StationGrid.BurstStore.Bulk: Bulk tier (batteries): the settlement draws fast storage (capacitors) first.
FFSystems.StationGrid.BurstStore.MaxDisc: kW the device can give; zero means uncapped (capacitors).
FFSystems.StationGrid.GridEnergyMath: Fixed-point energy splitting shared by the settlement. Burst-compatible and pure so tests can drive it directly.
FFSystems.StationGrid.GridEnergyMath.Cap: A per-device rate cap applied to one heartbeat; zero means uncapped.
FFSystems.StationGrid.GridEnergyMath.Dra: Takes `amount` from storage, fast tier (0, capacitors) before bulk tier (1, batteries), spread across each tier's devices by `WaterFill` up to `limits`, adding to `taken`. `mask` is scratch.
FFSystems.StationGrid.GridEnergyMath.Pul: One heartbeat's slice of a pulse: what is left of it, at most the peak rate for one Dt. A peak of zero means uncapped.
FFSystems.StationGrid.GridEnergyMath.Rep: Plays a pulse out heartbeat by heartbeat the way the settlement pays it, from `progress` kW·s on, and returns its progress at the end. The one test of whether a pulse can be paid, shared by the settlement (before it starts a mass-driver pulse) and the power panel (whether a driver can ever fire), so the two always agree.
FFSystems.StationGrid.GridEnergyMath.Wat: Spread `amount` across devices as evenly as their limits allow, adding each device's share to `allocated`. Callers pass devices in tile order: each pass splits what is left evenly between the devices that still have room, and the leftover raw units of the division go one each to the earliest of them, so the result never depends on entity ids.
FFSystems.StationGrid.GridEnergySettleme: Pays every charge consumer's energy each heartbeat. Energy is in kW·s. The only owner of stored-energy debits and credits; consumers act on this heartbeat's receipt (`ChargeConsumer`) and pulse state (`ChargePulse`).
How long a laser keeps its engage progress after losing its target.
FFSystems.StationGrid.GridPulseProbe: Read-only lookups for asking whether a consumer's grid can pay one full pulse (`PulseDeliveryMath.OnePulse`). Presentation only: GridWarningCheckerSystem uses it for the mass driver's insufficient-power icon. Burst-compatible.
FFSystems.StationGrid.GridPulseProbe.Eva: Plays one of `consumer`'s pulses against its grid, given that grid's storage. False when the consumer has no pulse or no live grid.
FFSystems.StationGrid.GridPulseProbe.Gat: Appends every storage device on `grid` to `stores`.
FFSystems.StationGrid.GridWarningChecker: A power or stability icon (low power, no power, unstable) appears, changes and clears only after the structure's state has asked for that for this many heartbeats in a row: 250 ms at 16 UPS. A shortage that is over within a quarter of a second never shows, a real one shows a quarter of a second late, and an icon at a threshold does not blink.
The icon prefab of each `StationWarningType`, indexed by its value, read from the live `EffectsContainer`; Entity.Null for None and for any icon the container leaves unset.
FFSystems.StationGrid.PulseDelivery: What a grid can put into one all-or-nothing pulse.
FFSystems.StationGrid.PulseDelivery.Deli: kW·s the grid can pay into the pulse within its window, at most the pulse energy.
FFSystems.StationGrid.PulseDelivery.Fund: Every heartbeat's slice of the pulse can be paid in full.
FFSystems.StationGrid.PulseDeliveryMath: Presentation-only arithmetic for the power readouts: peak demand, max delivery, and whether a mass driver's launch pulse can ever be paid. Nothing in the simulation reads it. Whether a pulse can be paid is `GridEnergyMath.ReplayPulse`, the settlement's own start test, so what the panel says matches what the settlement does.
kW a device can sustain over a pulse lasting `seconds`: everything it holds spread over the pulse, never more than its discharge cap.

Every burst lasts exactly this long: four 16 UPS heartbeats. Each pulse consumer's PulsePeakPower is four times its PulseEnergy (pinned by StorageDrawsNoPowerTest.EveryBurstLastsExactlyFourHeartbeats), and every readout of what a grid can deliver in a burst uses this window.

The grid's raw generation before the grid calculation carved out spike, combat and transmitter shares. `StationGridCalculationSystem` subtracts those from `CurrentPowerSatisfaction` (ReserveGridEnergy, CalculatePowerGoingToTransmitters) and adds the battery backup; PublishGridEnergy puts the reserve plus the untransmitted leftover in `HeadroomPower`. Undoing those steps gives the generation back.

Whether a driver can ever fire, and what the grid can put into one pulse. Pass the grid's `HeadroomPower` as `sparePower`. Storage counts at capacity when there is spare to refill it while the driver waits, otherwise at what it holds now.
The highest draw a pulse consumer makes: its peak, or the whole pulse in one heartbeat if uncapped.
Seconds a fully paid pulse takes: `energy / peak`, or one heartbeat if uncapped.
Generation a pulse can use in the best case: everything above the factory's draw. Transmitters and storage recharge give way to an armed pulse, and no laser is fighting.
FFSystems.StationGrid.RelativeGridTileTa: Resolves each heartbeat what a structure aimed through a `RelativeGridTileTarget` links to: a mass driver's `MassDriver.Destination` and a power distributor's `PowerTransferEdge`. Both take the same path (`ResolveDestination{TKind}`): in tile mode (the default) the structure of their kind at the stored offset; with `TargetStructureMemory.Follow` on the remembered structure wherever it now stands.

Whether a link from `source` reaches `destination`: the structure's link radius (`StructureRangeResolver.LinkRadiusTiles`) by `MassDriverSystem`'s exact tile-derived predicate, the one its fire gate uses. A structure with no authored radius has no range to enforce (its reach is a directional beam), so it is always within.
FFSystems.StationGrid.StationGridCalcula: Processes each StationGrid and distributes power to connected modules

Whether a structure is one of the ones that get louder when their station moves. Not thrusters (see `MovementSignalFor`), and not items configured with `PlaceableConfig.NoMovementSignal` -- armor blocks, which are plating rather than machinery and would otherwise punish armoring a moving station.

What one structure adds to its grid's signal because the station is under way. Thrusters are excluded: StationMoverSignalEmissionSystem already reports their whole contribution through their own emitter, firing or not, and their rated number is a total rather than a bonus on top of this one.

Signal every structure aboard adds while its station is under way. A parked station is only as loud as what it is actively doing, which left a station in flight all but silent: the work that normally makes the noise (mining above all) stops at takeoff. Moving is itself the activity now, and the bigger the station the harder it is to miss.
FFSystems.StationGrid.StationGridPostRes: On the first fixed tick after a heartbeat reset, queues a station-grid Add for every structure the load-time regrid would grid that has no grid on this peer, so a live peer starts the new session with the grids a peer that loaded the same world has.
Republishes every StationGrid's outputs in ONE update on the first fixed tick after a heartbeat reset.
FFSystems.Stations.CrafterInputFill: A crafter's connector slots feed both its input and its outputs. This moves every item the recipe needs from the connector slots into the input, as much as the input has room for, so only what the input cannot take is left to pass on.
FFSystems.Stations.StationConnectionsSys: Runs anytime a placeable appears on the grid (mobile station landing, blueprint constructed, etc) and recalculates the attributes of a station
Which world-space edge a base-frame slot sits on — the inverse of `GetSlotForEdge`, for showing a stored slot back to the player as a direction.
The base-frame slot of the first tile on the world-space edge facing `worldEdge`.

Re-expresses a base-frame slot after the placeable has been turned, so the slot keeps naming the same WORLD edge it named before. Base frame is defined relative to `Placeable.Direction`, so a stored slot silently changes meaning when the direction changes and anything that rotates a placeable without re-deriving its connections has to carry its slots across with this.
FFSystems.SystemManager: Manages all enabling/disabling of systems. Ensures that system enable/disable state remains persistent across loading/saving games, main menu, and pausing. State resets when the game is restarted.
FFSystems.SystemManager.DisableAllSystem: Disables all systems that contain the systemName substring in their system name.
FFSystems.SystemManager.DisableLocalToWo: This re-enables the built-in unity versions of LocalToWorld
FFSystems.SystemManager.EnableAllSystems: Enables all systems that contain the systemName substring in their system name.
FFSystems.SystemManager.EnableLocalToWor: This switches to use the custom LocalToFFWorldSystem and FFSmoothRigidBodiesGraphicalMotion system instead of the ones built into unity. These have performance improvements by disabling movement for all items that are offscreen.
The healing rate with no healing technology unlocked. This lives on the system rather than in the world's entity data, so it survives a `ResetGame` — which is exactly why `LogisticsStationHealingRateReward` must restore it before a reward recompute instead of accumulating onto it.
FFSystems.Transforms.FFSmoothRigidBodies: A system that can smooth out the motion of rigid bodies if the fixed physics tick rate is slower than the variable graphics framerate. Each affected body's `Unity.Transforms.LocalToWorld` matrix is adjusted before rendering, but its underlying `Unity.Transforms.LocalTransform` component is left alone. THIS IS CUSTOMIZED FROM THE BUILTIN UNITY SYSTEM.
Registers the physics world for smooth rigid body motion described by physicsWorldIndex.
An entity query matching dynamic rigid bodies whose motion should be smoothed.
Unregisters the physics world for smooth rigid body motion described by physicsWorldIndex.
FFSystems.Transforms.HeartbeatTransformC: The transform pass, run ONCE MORE at the start of every heartbeat, so that a heartbeat system reading `LocalToWorld` before this frame's `TransformSystemGroup` sees the pose the simulation last wrote — regardless of how many engine frames happened to elapse since.
FFSystems.Transforms.LocalToFFWorldSyste: This system computes a `LocalToWorld` matrix for each entity
FFSystems.UnitStateMachine.ChaseSystem.P: How far a player's fleet ship may chase from its player, in world units, before the leash sends it home in a passive spell (`FleetIdleMarker.TempPassive`). `TargetingSystem` ends the spell once the ship is back within half of it.

Copies the pass's pose-source tally into the `ChaseC3FallbackReport` singleton and zeroes the per-pass half for the next pass. Single-threaded over a one-entity query, scheduled behind the chase job, so it sees every add and no chase job of the NEXT heartbeat can start before the zeroing lands — the same dependency chain enforces both halves of that.
FFSystems.UnitStateMachine.DisabledKnnWa: Stops a wandering ship whose KNN was disabled. It writes the saved `LinearMotion.Disable` that `LinearMotionSystem` reads, so it runs on the heartbeat. It used to run every frame in `FFControllerPreTransformGroup`: a fast client set the flag in a frame between heartbeats, a host at one frame per heartbeat only after the next heartbeat's `LinearMotionSystem`, so the host's ship moved one step more.
FFSystems.UnitStateMachine.FleetIdleStat: This performs fleet idle operations for bots and ships that are at a station (shipyard, defense tower, etc) Player fleet idle is handled differently in FleetIdleSystem

Where a docked ship is put this heartbeat, before its platform moves: toward its slot, no faster than `maxSpeed`, and left there once it has arrived. The platform's own step is added after every station mover has run (`StationShipCarrySystem`), so a ship at its slot stays at its slot.
How fast a docked ship closes on its slot, per second of the distance left (plus `DockMinSpeed`).
The least speed a docked ship closes on its slot at, u/s: it arrives instead of creeping.

Within this distance of its slot, a ship of a station in the air is docked: its own motion is off, it is eased onto the slot (`Dock`) and carried with its platform (`StationShipCarrySystem`). Beyond it the ship flies home under its own motion.

Where a station-parked ship of this formation index is flown to, as an offset from its commander's fleet position. The grid is unchanged — this only gives the layout a single name so it can be read from somewhere other than the job that applies it.
FFSystems.UnitStateMachine.FleetIdleSyst: Proportional approach gain (1/s) toward the slot — replaces the fleet-size damping that left the pull ~3000x weaker than the repel.

Inside this radius of its own slot, neighbor repel is ignored (slots are spaced `FormationSlotSpacing` apart, so settled ships can never overlap). Must be larger than `FormationSettleRadius` so repel cannot re-agitate a settled ship — the stateless hysteresis band that breaks the pull-vs-repel cycle.

Commander speed (u/s) at which the moving catch-up cap is fully engaged. The cap ramps in with commander speed rather than switching on a float.Epsilon comparison, which handed a mid-approach ship a discontinuous target-velocity drop (e.g. 80 → 25 u/s at 40 u out) the instant the commander twitched.

Cap (u/s) on the slot pull ON TOP of the commander's velocity. Uncapped, the proportional pull chases a formation target that steps ~30 u (FleetIdleOffset) the moment the commander moves, slingshotting settled ships ~100 u/s past the player. 25 u/s reads as a glide, and it never binds during settling (inside the calm band the pull is at most gain x 8 = 16 u/s).

Distance scale for the cubic far-catch-up boost: negligible inside the formation but grows cubically beyond it, so ships stranded far away (post-combat regroup) still rush back like the legacy farPull.

How far from its slot a ship of this lead offset only glides toward it, at `FormationCatchUpSpeed`, while the commander moves: twice the lead (`FleetConfig.FleetIdleOffset`), the most a turn or a reversal moves a settled ship's slot, and at least `FormationMinGlideDistance`.
Golden angle in radians — uniform, organic-looking spiral packing.
How much faster than its moving commander a returning player-fleet ship may close, as a multiple of the commander's speed (`PlayerFleetMaxSpeed`).
Exponential rest-decay rate (1/s) for residual velocity inside the settle radius.
Inside this radius of its own slot a ship is settled and comes to rest.

every player-fleet ship idles at its OWN formation slot instead of the single shared FleetPosition — one shared target for ~100 ships is a structural limit cycle against `UnitOverlapPreventionSystem`'s inverse-square repel.

The fastest a player-fleet ship flies: its commander's speed plus a closing speed of `FormationReturnSpeedRatio` times it (at least `PlayerFleetSpeedBonus`), and never below the old `BaseMoveSpeed + PlayerFleetSpeedBonus`. It was that fixed ceiling alone so a player faster than it left the fleet behind until they slowed down.

How much faster than its commander a player's fleet may fly to hold formation. Named and shared because `FFSystems.Fleet.FleetCommanderSystem` bounds the derived commander velocity by the same ceiling — a bound the formation could not exceed anyway, so two copies of a bare `100` would only be able to drift apart.
A player-fleet ship's formation target: the commander's fleet position, led forward along its velocity by `fleetIdleOffset`, plus the ship's own slot.
FFSystems.UnitStateMachine.PlayerDisable: System that handles showing/hiding the player's fleet of ships. This system has several responsibilities: 1. Responds to the player's HideFleet toggle from GameMetaState 2. Automatically hides construction bots when there are more than 1 3. Automatically hides combat bots the first time the player exceeds 10 combat bots 4. Uses PersistentData to track if combat bots have been auto-hidden 5.

Whether a hidden ship `distance` from its owner is in once it has flown `stepDistance` toward it this heartbeat: judged after the step, against the owner's position of this heartbeat, so a moving owner does not leave it one heartbeat behind for good.
Sets up the system's entity queries and requirements.
Updates the system each heartbeat, handling visibility of fleet ships based on settings and auto-hide rules.
The owner's speed a hidden ship flying home adds to its closing speed (0 for a non-player owner), so it outruns a moving owner instead of trailing it (see ReturnStepDistance).
Closing speed per unit of distance to the owner (u/s per u): 480 u/s at 150 u.
Fastest a returning ship closes on its owner (u/s), on top of the owner's own speed.
Slowest a returning ship closes on its owner (u/s), so it always arrives.
How far a hidden ship flies toward its owner this heartbeat: the owner's own speed plus a closing speed that grows smoothly with the distance, never past the owner.
Within this distance of its owner a hidden ship flying home goes in (u).
FFTechnology.ResearchController.AddToQue: Adds a queue entry with an already-decided target level — the shared mutation core for the networked ResearchQueue op: the host bakes the level once and every peer replays it here, so the per-peer level computation the UI used to do at click time can never diverge.
FFTechnology.ResearchController.ApplyRes: Raw local write of the shared research pool — a [Save]d simulation component on the host player. ONLY the apply leg of the ordered `ObjectiveResearchReward` operation may call this (it runs on every peer at the same heartbeat boundary).
FFTechnology.ResearchController.ComputeQ: The level an Add issued NOW would research the tech to: for infinite techs the completed level plus the active research plus entries already queued; 0 for regular techs.
FFTechnology.ResearchController.LearnTec: Call to research a set of `Technology` at one time.

Call to learn a single technology. If learning a batch of technologies, consider using `LearnTechnologies(System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyList{string})` or `LearnTechnologies(System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyList{string})` instead.
FFTechnology.ResearchController.MoveInQu: Moves the queue entry at `fromIndex` so it ends at `toIndex`. The caller (the ResearchQueue op's Move apply) has already validated the indices and the resulting order.
FFTechnology.ResearchController.NotifyLi: Notifies all listeners of the Research Controller after a technology has been researched. Must be called exactly once after a technology or chunk of technologies is researched.
FFTechnology.ResearchController.TryRecom: Recomputes EVERY technology reward as a pure function of the currently-unlocked set: restore each reward's target to its un-researched baseline, then apply each unlocked technology's rewards once (infinite technologies once per completed level).
FFTechnology.ResearchController.UnlockTe: Unlocks the requested technology, updating the tech tree and specifying the rewards. Does NOT notify users that the tech was researched, play the sound, etc. For that, you need to call `ResearchController.NotifyListenersAfterTechResearch`
NetworkOperations.Settings.StructureSett: One structure-setting kind's mutation logic, shared by BOTH legs of the operation: the host request handler calls `Validate` before broadcasting (reject = no broadcast, contract C5), and the apply handler on every peer calls `Validate` defensively then `Apply` (single-player has no request leg, so the apply leg must be self-sufficient — the SetCrafterRecipe pattern).
Replays the setting onto the target via the SAME data path the panel's old direct write used (research D5 — extract-and-share, so op-applied and pre-migration writes cannot drift).
Deterministic check that `target` carries the kind's component(s) and the inner-json payload is well-formed/in-range. False = skip (never throw).

Registry mapping `StructureSettingKind` to its applier. Kinds register in the static constructor as their story phase lands; an unregistered kind is rejected on the request leg and skip-and-logged on the apply leg (fail closed). `Register`/`Unregister` are public so EditMode tests can install stub kinds (using out-of-range enum values) without touching production kinds.

Kinds a player may set on a structure that is placed but not built yet, so it comes out of construction with them. Only whole-component writes to the target itself, which no system acts on while the ghost is OutOfPlay and which construction keeps (it completes the same entity, ConstructionBotTaskSystem.FinishConstruction).

Kinds that also reach a structure of a station in flight: every kind but the two of `IsLockedInFlight`. Lift-off takes every structure of a mobile station out of the grid map, so a plain tile key finds nothing there; these kinds use the flying key instead (`TileKeyedTargets.TryBakeTileIncludingFlying`).

The key a dispatch sends for `target`: the one `TryResolveTarget` resolves on the host's request leg. Its `CenterTile`, except an InserterRange target's origin tile and, for `AppliesToFlyingStructures` kinds, a flying structure's flying key.

Kinds a structure in flight does not take: aiming a mass driver or a power distributor. Their range check and the relative tile they store are measured from the source's grid tile, which in flight is the tile it took off from, and the targeting system drops the target of a flying source anyway.

A rename is valid when non-empty and it FITS the component: `NamedEntity.Value` is a FixedString32Bytes (29 UTF-8 bytes) and an oversized string would throw inside the heartbeat drain. Shared by the generic StructureName kind and the hauler-family SetHaulerName command.

The key `TryResolveTarget` gives `target` back for, baked by the host's request leg for the broadcast: the grid-resolvable tile (`TileKeyedTargets.TryBakeResolvableTile`), or for an `StructureSettingKind.InserterRange` target its origin tile, or for an `AppliesToFlyingStructures` kind in flight its flying key.

The target of a `kind` setting at `tile`, the same way on the host's request leg and on every peer's apply leg: a live structure, or for `AppliesToConstructionGhosts` kinds a confirmed construction site (`TileKeyedTargets.TryResolveConfirmedConstructionGhost`).

Identifies which structure setting a `StructureSettingPayload` carries and therefore which applier mutates the target (see `StructureSettingAppliers`). Values are explicit and WIRE-STABLE: they travel in serialized payloads between peers, so never renumber or reuse a value. Adding a setting = new member here + payload class + applier + EditMode test — never a new `NetworkGameOperationType` member.

The ONE entry point panels (and `ffauto:setting.*` automation commands) use to change a structure setting. Builds the `StructureSettingPayload` envelope and routes it through `CheatCommandDispatch` — the proven MP-vs-SP split (research D4): connected → host-validated client request; single-player → the apply op is enqueued directly and drained on the next heartbeat through the identical applier.
Dispatches the panel's spawn acknowledgement (Deployed → None) for the local player.

Dispatches "my player-crafter finished a ship — deploy it". The ship id is the crafting queue's completed item (client-local UI state the host cannot see; it is validated against the shared config host-side).
Dispatches a fleet-transfer deploy of the completed ship waiting in a STRUCTURE crafter; the host bakes the ship id from the crafter's authoritative recipe.
"Follow destination" for a mass driver or a power distributor: the Follow toggle of the target panel and the settings paste.

Dispatches a hauler-family command for a HAULER target: the peer-stable key is the hauler's `HaulerId` when it has one, else the reference structure's `Placeable.GridTile` (see `HaulerKey` and `HaulerCommandPayload`).
Dispatches a hauler-family command for a HAULER STATION (landing zone) target.
Dispatches a range limit for an inserter arm or cargo barge, in tiles from its origin centre (0 = no limit). The range panel and the settings paste both come through here.

The light panel edits its two fields from separate controls. Each op carries only the field its control edited and the applier leaves the other alone, so nothing is read here: a value read at the click would be stale while an earlier op of the same player is still in flight.
A mass driver's laser colour.

Dispatches an oracle buy/refund for the LOCAL player. The acting player rides the op envelope's client id (research D3); `shopLabel` identifies the item for Buy and is ignored for RefundAll. `oracle` is the Oracle the panel is open on; its tile rides the payload so the apply enforces that Oracle's level cap (Entity.Null: the full cap).

Dispatches the LOCAL player's fleet-config toggles. The panel edits the two fields from independent checkboxes, so the un-edited field is filled from the local player's current authoritative state (last-write-wins for concurrent edits of different fields — research D7, the RequesterConfig precedent).

Dispatches a change to ONE entry of the LOCAL player's fleet ship-request list. The player entity is client-id keyed, not tile keyed, so this must NOT go through `DispatchRequesterItems` — that overload derives its key from `Placeable.CenterTile` and the player has no Placeable, which is exactly how the PlayerFleetPanel's requested-amount field came to be silently dropped.
Dispatches the COMPLETE new ship-request list for the LOCAL player (contract C10). The acting player rides the op envelope's client id, so there is no target key here.

RequesterConfig is a whole-value payload but the panels edit its two fields from independent widgets, so this read-modify-write builder fills whichever field the caller is not changing from the target's current authoritative state (concurrent edits of different fields resolve last-write-wins, research D7 — accepted).
Dispatches the COMPLETE new request list (contract C10 — buffer settings are full-replace, never positional patches).

Dispatches a research-queue mutation. Research state is global factory state with no structure tile, so there is no target key (research D3). For Add, leave `targetLevel` at -1: the host bakes the level an infinite tech will research to (in single-player the applier computes it at apply time — see `ResearchQueuePayload`). For Remove, pass the exact level of the queue entry being removed.
Dispatches a research-queue reorder: the entry (`techName`, `targetLevel`) the sender sees at `fromIndex` should end at `toIndex`. The op is skipped on every peer if the queue changed under it.

Dispatches a setting change for a placeable target entity (the common panel case — the panel already holds the entity; its CenterTile becomes the peer-stable key, re-validated and re-baked host-side; `StructureSettingAppliers.DispatchKey` has the two kinds of exception).
